Tl;dr version: Your money or your life!
Note: The pros and cons are mainly based on the singleplayer. Some things about the multiplayer near the end.
Pros:
- Has a lot of depth to the game.
-Your decisions for the most part matter. One example is like choosing whenever or not to release a lord, or take him prisoner when you defeat him. This can lead him to like you more, or dislike, depending on your decisions. You can't always choose the simpliest option.
-You are right there in the thick of the battle or sitting in the back commanding your troops as they take to the field against the enemy (which can range from several guys to a full on army).
-The open world map is large, with multiple areas to fight in. On the open world map, everyone is either running around, sitting on their♥♥♥♥♥doing absolutely nothing, or constantly picking fights with each other. It's overall chaotic in the world of Calradia, but you just can't see it (unless you use cheats). Not the greatest looking overworld/map, but it's not that bad.
-The combat is quite fluid and satisfying. Using the mouse to swing and block in four directions is simple and fun. If you are going to play the singleplayer, then do it right. Go to your options, turn the damage of you and your allies to normal, turn off auto block, and experience Warband with all of it's ups and downs :)
-Become the king/queen of Calradia. Who wouldn't want to become one? Just make sure to keep in the realm in check or else you might have some problems on your hands.
-Tons of mods to choose from, although the Vanilla game can last you for a very long time.
and other such things
-Pretty good music. Fits the game.
Cons:
-Not the greatest looking game. If you are looking for graphics, then this isn't the game to look for.
-There isn't really a story. You basically create your own story/background and then thrown into the world of Calradia, where 6 different factions fight for control over the realm.
-Can get quite repetitive, since all you are doing for the most part when it comes to the gameplay, is running around on the overworld, and fighting other parties.
-Has no real tutorial, and does not tell you about what it has within the game. Basically you need to either look up a guide or explore the game in-depth, in order to figure out what the game has to offer. Don't be to suprised if you've missed something or experienced something new after hours of playing the game.
-Siege battles are not great. Definitely not the strongest part about the game.
-Getting knocked out isn't fun. Neither is being taken prisoner (since you cannot die). Try and not get screwed over, or you will be put in a rather bad position.
-You may get graphical issues with the game, like having part of the overworld turning into a blue sky.  It isn't game breaking, but can be kind of annoying.
All of that was, for the most part, the singleplayer part of Warband. The multiplayer:
-Involves the combat system like the singleplayer, but with other players (obviously). It can be a blast, and quite chaotic if you can get on the populated servers. Watching 30 players charge into another 30 is quite a beautiful sight to behold, wouldn't you agree?
-Having a few men and woman swinging away in their undergarments is entertaining to watch. Especially if those players are wrecking♥♥♥♥♥♥:)
What else is there to say about this wonderful game? The combat is smooth, the gameplay is fun, there is alot to do in it, the multiplayer is chaotic, and the only thing lacking is a basic tutorial and not so good graphics. The pros heavily outweigh the cons and the only reason why you shouldn't buy it is because it isn't your game. So yeah, it's pretty much a must buy.

Ace of Spades is a multiplayer combat game combining Minecraft style physics with Cod/TF2 gameplay. This leads to an interesting style of combat that rewards people for their skill and ingenuity in crafting the landscape and building structures to their tactical advantage.
I have spent nearly 300 hours playing this game and the main thing that keeps me playing is the fun factor.  There are always people online obviously not as many as with some fps games but you can always get a match by using the server browser. The gameplay itself is also a main factor in its durability. As the environment is buildable you can create buildings and mould the landscape into something that allows you to outwit your opponents.
With it being in the steam workshop you can download user –created maps for use which adds endless variety.
While the graphics may not be for everyone, people that have played games such as Minecraft or more indie style games probably won’t mind.  I guess a bonus of this is that it runs smoothly . I only experience the odd, very occasional bit of lag.
Pro’s:
-	Great for lovers of first person shooters.
-	 Multiple classes to use to your advantage.
-	Tactical gameplay.
-	Plenty of games available and a good range of maps that come as standard.
-	Custom Maps.
-	Range of game modes spanning from Team Deathmatch to Capture the Flag and ‘Zombie’.
Con’s:
-	Lots of trolls and people that try and kick you for hacking if you are much better than them.
-	Small infrequent DLC.
-	No skill tree/ weapon advancement.
-	A few bugs which aren’t too big a deal.
-	Not a large emphasis on teamwork.
I don’t usually put this many hours into a game so with that in mind (and its low price tag) I’d definitely recommend Ace of Spades!    8.5/10

So... I finished The Evil Within on survival difficulty, and what I have to say is somewhat different from most reviews on pc.
First of all, yes, it's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ port, it has ♥♥♥♥♥♥ performance, but it really never felt unplayable to me, just not optimal, it wasn't the framerate that annoyed me the most, it was the hideous field of view and the aspect ratio, but I got through those problems and decided to enjoy the game for what it was and not for the performance and graphics. I got lucky with the crashes, the game never crashed on me or anything like that, I have a r9 280x, 16gb of ram, and an i7 4770k in case that affects something in that matter.
Now for the game itself, I got introduced to survival horror with franchises like Resident Evil and Sillent Hill, like most survival horror fans, and what I have to say is that if you played Resident Evil 4 you're not going to find anything new or original about this game, but you will find a lot of noustalgia and feel from that particular game. The game offers a nice set of chapters which seem very different one from another, with new enemies and environments each chapter, I liked the design of the environmens, with a nice balance of open places and claustrophobic corridors, all filled with good old school pools of blood and deceased corpses.
In terms of story, it's not that great, but it's not bad either, the characters are for the most part forgettable, with some exceptions, and the fact that the main character is not the best doesn't help at all, but the story is interesting enough and doesn't go into fillers or some random unnecessary plot twists.
When it comes to gameplay and control, it's all old school survival horror, ammo is scarce, you have your typical RE4 types of weapons (pistol,shotgun,rifle), and a new weapon which is the agony crossbow, which has a number of craftable bolts with different qualities, such as explosive or shock bolts, you can get crafting materials by disabling traps or grabing toolboxes in the environments. The movement and aiming are sluggish, often making you fail and die when enemies get to close because when aiming the pistol the camera zooms in so much and the aiming is so damn terrible that it makes it hard to shoot anything, but when you land a shot on an enemy is very satisfying, enemies react realistically to where you shoot and damage from the shot affects the models, making for some half exploded heads. Boss fights aren't anything new, but they are very fun and challenging, making you run around and try to find a way to weaken the boss or to kill him, pretty much like a RE4 boss fight would be, there's really not much of a difference.
In the end, I recommend this game for what it is to me, it's an old school horror game with a lot of gore and grewsome boss fights, it's just a shame that the port and some design choices don't hold up to the rest of the game.

Well it's just like it sounds , A FPS Warhammer game that plays in the End Times where you slay tides of Vermin.
It is fun , it is incompilcated but yet Challenging on higher difficulties.
It found the right balance between RPG and FPS and combined them to be THE BEST CO-OP FPS i've ever Played.
You Start off In The Inn which is a VERY Detailed Medieval Planning Room with alot of features such as The MissionMap , an Forge , an Shrine and an Inventory stash.
It is also the place where you invite your Friends or other Players join you to play the Mission the Host selected ergo the Mission the group supposedly agreed upon.
After you ended your Mission you can go with your Party/Friends back into the Inn to change Gear Craft or Demolish your goods to create new ones.
It's a Useful feature and makes the Partyplay Simple and takes away the need to leave early.
The Difficulties are all together well made and balanced at this point , from personal Experience i can say that as a matter of fact you can Climb +1 Difficulty per day if you Learn ,  Adapt and Smack the Hell out of Vermin all day long.
The Settings Options on the other hand are Mediocre , you have Only a Limited Choice of Options you can Enable or Disable WITHOUT having access to the important Settings such as adjusting the VRAM Pool for the Texturestreaming , setting the correct Audio Channelsize , changing the Specular Map amount of Static decals etc. list goes on and on.
And therefore you cannot really Optimize the game for yourself , which leads to guaranteed FPS drops on most Systems.
And here we are ... at the Point where we talk a bit more about the Games overall Performance.
Now it is indeed stated that the game is processor Heavy , but what is sold as working game is a Butcher for your CPU it puts 100% Load with X Workers on X cores and still performs only meh , it is neither Optimized for AMD or Intel since both seem to have heavy fps dips with alot of Trash on the Map and yea ... you kinda need your FPS when you have to deal with 50 Vermin don't you? especially when your Hero's loadout requires a bit of aim to work.
It's not only the CPU performance going south ... The GPU performance is even worse , i'm running a r9 390x(not gonna buy an nvidia card so shht) and the Game is using .. uhh 1.5 of my 8GB VRAM .. ye Really. also the Useage of the GPU don't go up with lowering/cranking up the Settings it just stays the same for the Entirety of my Gaming Sessions so is my Temperature . for such an hardware heavy game i Honestly expected more than an Maximum of 53°C after 5 hours for example.
I'm the kind of guy that doesn't really care when it dips into 40 fps because it's still playable yes sure it's annoying but not gamebreaking.
People that don't see it that way might want to wait until the Game/Engine receive a proper overwork aka Patch.
Well ... All in All i got to say i'm having a blast playing this game with Friends and going for the Loot and climbing difficulties together.

I don't usually write negative reviews but I looked on the store page and I didn't see many others highlighting the issues I had with this game.
Let me start off by saying I think the first Hotline Miami is one of the best games I've played in the last few years. Its mixture of arcady fun, great replay value, and gameplay at a break-neck speed made for an almost perfect game experience. If you are interested in the series and haven't played it yet please purchase the first one.
The second game however is, quite simply, a mess. The smooth and fluid gameplay from the first game that rewarded twitch reflexes and skill is now replaced with gameplay focused on hiding behind a corner and hoping there isn't an enemy off screen who will one shot you. There is a mechanic in both games that allows the player to look a room's length ahead just to see what's coming and in the first game I barely had to use this feature. In this game I had to spend every waking second holding left-shift down because in most situations there were enemies on the other side of the level that wouldn't hesitate to one-shot me. This led to frustration as the game was punishing me unnecessarily.
This game also decided to have a whole new mask-system that is also flawed. The first game allowed the player to choose from dozens of masks that each had a special attribute linked to them (extra speed, more ammo, deadly fists, etc.) In this game each level is assigned a mask that limits the players gameplay decisions which severely cuts back on the replayability and fun of the game.
I was anxiously awaiting the sequel to one of my favorite games of the last decade and I was given an inferior product that seemed to forget what made its predecessor great. Some people who played the first game loved this one but I fail to find enjoyment from it. Again, if you haven't played any Hotline Miami's before just play the first one.

Hotline Miami 2 has put me in an odd predicament for a review.
If you played the original as a stealthy player--like me--then you'll find the game unforgivably broken due to the original's problems becoming worse. Also, if you liked the extremely vague plot with no purpose in the end, then you might find the "sequel's" context to get in the way.
On the other hand, I inevitably came to love the game when I gave up my old style. I found replaying old levels like Rambo (though cautious) more enjoyable, and it helped me finish the rest of the game. As for the story, I couldn't understand the first game's plot besides its nihilistic message about game narratives when it comes to the mechanics. So having more context and characters was a bonus.
I guess the easiest way to recommend this title is if you can appreciate the changes made from HLM1, then you'll love HLM2. If you prefer the classic's style of narrative and gameplay, then you probably should stay with the original.
The same problems with lacking options for visuals are apparent in the sequel.
So if bright lights, motion-swaying and changing colors in the background bother you, then I don't think this series is one you should play. And if you thought the camera-swaying was bad in the original, then you have not used a sniper-rifle in HLM2. It's vomit-inducing.
However, the developers did add rebindable keys for all characters' actions--except for the dodge-roll which is mapped to the execute button--so it's a step-up from the original. Though I'm surprised there aren't more PC pitchforks raised at this series.
(There's also a "graphic content" setting that disables a two-second forceful sex scene at the start. I don't care that the content is in the game nor the setting to turn it off. My question is what was the point of adding that to the game--or the character--because it doesn't feel relevant to the rest of the narrative. Nor is there any visual penetration to make it that graphic. In the end, it just comes across as needlessly edgy.)
The best change from its predecessor is that the whole game now plays like a top-down "tactical" murder-puzzle shooter. There are three basic enemy types--two from the first title and a new one that is immune to bullets--and there's a better focus on creating variety throughout the game with a smaller number of "masks"/playable characters.
Gone is the curve-balling car that spawns enemies, the unkillable police-forces ambushing you with sniper-rifles aimed at the windows, and the god-awful bosses that break the rules of the HLM1. (There is only one boss-level in HLM2 with several bosses, and they follow the same rules like other enemies.) Now we have a game that has consistent challenge.
Now we get 24/25  similar levels that can last anywhere from under a minute to 15+ minutes. For the average person, there is probably 7+ hours of content, minimum, which is more than replaying HLM1 three-times. This is excluding the "Hard" mode, which not only flips the levels upside down but adds more enemies and takes away the aim-lock button.
So if the game is more of HLM1, then why does it also feel like a step-back from the previous game?
The main source of complaint is how HLM2 has taken away your options for how you play. As previously mentioned, you cannot get through this game playing conservatively all the time.
This problem comes from several sources: Having to play 10 playable characters--but not all are always available-- having three distinct "styles" of play, the nurfing of melee weapons, and the rules for some characters being thrown like a book to your face.
The reason for having so many characters is because of how the narrative is told in HLM2. Because the first game wasn't confusing enough, the sequel is a side-story, a prequel and a conclusion all in one. Changing from from one scene to the next randomly also alters the way you can play.
Some characters you'll play have nothing special about them other than limitations. For example, the soldier character can only use one gun that he equips and he must find specific ammo boxes to get more. Or there's the news reporter who refuses to use guns unless you execute someone. These limitations are quite annoying when the game plays consistently throughout the whole game, forcing you to change your playstyle because the developers made it that way.
When you do have options, such as when you're playing as the Fans, Jake or the Son, they all boil down to No Weapons (Fists only), start off with guns (or a nailgun), or you get some quirk that works with only one character. For example, there are these twins James & Ash that can be played simaltaneously as a glass-cannon of destruction.
All together, these changes go against a lot of what was appealing of the original. Masks gave you small bonuses but didn't limit your playstyle. Some even offered a new challenge. Best of all, these masks were available from beginning to end, excluding the hospital scene. That was enough to offer replayability, and the point is none of it was forced on you.
Now whether these changes were made to make tighter levels and/or to tailor them for specific playstyles, the result is that the whole game can feel abrupt with its difficulty and give less of a reason to replay every level.
Perhaps the worst change is how the new level design has made the original's problems worse. AI behavior is finicky at best, unfair at worst; enemies will shoot you beyond your line of sight all the time; and choosing the right weapon in the middle of the moment can get you killed.
Unfortunately,like what you'd expect from sequels, HLM2 goes for the approach that bigger is always better. Instead of adding more floors/checkpionts in-between these each level, the game goes for making huge environments while using the same checkpoint system.
The larger environments simply do not work with the the enemy AI. This problem isn't sucking at the game or the trial-and-error gameplay of HLM1. Mooks can spot you a mile away from windows at an angle or two screens away, some of which will require a specific tactic to kill.
This problem will lead to needless deaths, which far outways the abuse if you could see enemies all the time. And because the AI can sometimes be unpredictable, your"solution" can sometimes feel unsatisfying or pure luck.
As for the story of HLM2... I like it, especially how it doesn't ruin the story for HLM1. The plot is ultimately the same result as the first game, a tale about nothing learned (in-game). However, now you have actual characters developed instead of characterizations being hinted at or unexplained.
The story will still make no sense your first playing--especially if you have not finished the first game or read the comic--because of how unorderly the narrative is told. It's a story that you'll piece together clues and dates either by noting them down yourself or by looking up videos on YouTube.  What I can say is that the narrative gives more substance to characters like Beard/Register-Man, Jacket (and Richard?) and the 50 Blessings.
The narrative could be clearer if there was a name listed to every face. You'll have to remember details like that, and note weird lines in relation to something maybe an hour later. And you'll probably still end up with more questions than answers--but the story is actually very interesting, and it could still be interpretted from various angles.
Although I am not a fan of the series, I'm glad I finished HLM2. It's the apex of what made the original so good yet also bad.

Possibly my favorite things about this game are the fact that the four nations of the game are
player-run. Economy, Ecology, etc. I play as a character that makes sure other players have enemies to fight and I try to keep a good ecological balance in the places I go. New players don't seem to realize that you
actually make an enemy type go extinct, so you have to be careful. This game gets an 8.5 or a 9 out of 10 from me. Anyways, that's it for my little introductory, brief review.
- Wakfu has an anime art style. This is because it's based around an anime of the same name, which is a french anime that, while I've personally never watched it, I do know plenty of the characters from it and I do know that it is a really rather nice anime, at least, from what I've heard from my friends. It has a great soundtrack also reminescent of the anime, and the humor is right around the same. The character designs for the game are all very solid, and even though it looks more reminescent of, say, a flashgame, where you can notice like, how the limbs move, maybe stretch, you'll notice that here, but it's in a cartoony sense so you won't pay it much mind, Id think.
- Wakfu has a very robust crafting and harvesting economy. All your resources, except for ores, are things you either have to hand-plant, or harvest from groves or gardens that are maintained by other players. Nations can impose limits to how many plants can be harvested or planted in a percentile range, and going over or below those percentiles will actually impose a penalty on you, being something as low as a 'citizen-level' penalty, to something as strict as a kill-on-sight bounty. The monster ecology for this game is exactly the same as the herb/tree/plant ecology, and everything is controlled by the players, even influencing the weather in the game for certain regions, making one region better for certain plants, and even time of years will influence the temperature!
- Wakfu's
is probably just as robust as it's ecological and economical parts, and I'll echo the sentiment that this game's combat system is similar to Final Fantasty: Tactic's. I can't really say too much about the current state of the combat system, as it's apparently undergone a good deal of revisions, according to my friends, and skills and passives no longer work like they used to, and work in different ways, but the combat system is still very in depth, and you can view all of it's workings, majorly, in your own character screen, so it may be intimidating at first, but the more you play around with it the more you get used to it. I'm not a very serious combative player so I can't fully explain how the combat system works, but there are a lot of classes for you to try out and tinker with, so there's probably at least one playstyle for you to like!
- On Wakfu's
.. I'm going to make one thing clear; Every game will have it's people who are there to ♥♥♥♥ with other players. This game is no different, and there's no exceptions. Players from hostile nations can invade your nation and try and instigate you to attack them, or deforest your region you're in. They can also try and bring your nation's enemy population down, but that's majorly it, people can be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s, but a major group of people are either rather kind and helpful or they keep to themselves, which is understandable. This game shines in my opinion for how it's all player run, and you, yes,
could be nominated for helping whichever country you join, or even ruling it, if you make enough friends and prove yourself to be worth of such a responsibility. It's daunting at first, but you'll meet plenty of people who've played as leaders or as parts of nations. It's like, a half-sort of roleplaying thing, half nation management for your role. Wakfu is...an experience. I am still going through my experience but from what I've played of it so far I can give a fair and detailed review of it. I will cover it in four sections; tutorial, gameplay, combat and community. I would also like to mention that I used to pay for and play this game when it was still in open beta about four to five years ago.
Tutorial:
The tutorial for Wakfu reminds me very much of the character actors at Didney Worl; they never break character. Your UI can give you all the information you need to break the fourth wall but when it comes time to learn from an NPC they will talk to you, the player, as if you are your character. The NPCs outside of the tutorial follow suit to this.
Ankama has made one class exclusively for the tutorial which, in my mind seems rather pointless. Back in beta the reason I bothered going through the tutorial areas was so I could get a proper feel for my actual class before I committed to playing it. That said, you can opt to skip the tutorial. I wouldn't advise that if you are a brand spanking new player.
Gameplay:
Wakfu is what most people call a grindfest, but there is reason behind it I like to think. Monsters will drop items that are guaranteed to end up being used for something, no matter the level. Gear can either be combined into sets to be sold, worn or even ground into powder which can be refined into runes to improve the gear you use.
Killing mobs and running quests aren't the only thing you can do in this game, you may also pick up professions. All of them in fact, conveniently located in the starter area known as Astrub. With this in mind a lot of players tend to lean towards one or the other based on their mood at the time. I personally rarely fight and would rather just go farm wheat fields.
Combat:
The combat in Wakfu is unique, something I've never seen in an MMORPG. Ever played Final Fantasy Tactics? This is it. You (and your teammates if you brought any) as well as monsters have a set initiative score, which is a stat you can increase. Those with higher initiative go first and you follow along a grid-based system to fight your enemies. Your character has access to a plethera of passive abilities (able to swap them out between battles on the fly as you unlock them), class-specific utility skills and three skill trees, each one has an element (meaning that you will have access to three of the four elements, I advise you to look through them when you make your character even if you haven't unlocked them).
The player versus player content this game provides comes in some different ways, but ultimately ends up the exact same. There are four nations that you may pick from to be your home upon reaching level 15, with the option to join an outlaw nation at level 30... I wouldn't recommend this though and some people get confused. Let me break this down real quick, if you play this game and hit level 30 you'll recieve a quest called "Riktus for a Day." Do not complete this quest, you will automatically join the outlaw nation that only has one outpost in the ocean and are free game for anyone wherever you go. Aside from this, at level 30 you can opt to become a guard of your nation, sworn to protect the land from Riktus, eco-terrorists (will cover this in another section) and PKers.
Another feature to note for combat are sidekicks. They are NPCs that can act as party members you control. They aren't as powerful or versatile as players but they get the job done when you need it. Part of the beginner quest is going through a dungeon, rewarding you at the end with an Astrub Knight. This is the only sidekick you get for free, with the addition of the free trial sidekick. Out of Ankama's list of sidekicks, one is chosen every so often as a free trial. Kind of a try before you buy sort of thing, this gives you the option of not only playing as yourself and the Astrub Knight, but a third teammate once every...I wanna say three weeks but I honestly never noticed. These guys don't offer what other players can provide and you can easily solo your way the entire game with a little patience, the sidekicks only offer you some help along the way.
Overall the PvP in this game is pretty fun so long as you don't get stacked against someone much higher level than you.
Community:
As far as I've seen, pretty dead. I wish I could say this, but in the town hubs (Astrub and nation outposts) there are people everywhere. The further out you go you see less players though, most of them are hidden in small haven bags (which act as a portable home and player shop) either afk selling their wares or just plain afk. That said, if you're looking at only the game's point of view then you are sadly missing out, the wiki for this game is regularly updated and the forums always has people poking their heads in to say hello. That said, if you plan to play this game for a while then get into a guild ASAP, I suggest you head over to the forums to find one to your liking.
Before I finish, I want to add that this game does have a cash shop. Is it pay to win? Not really, most of the things you can buy are either cosmetic or do really minor things. You can buy weapons but they don't compare to the gear you can find and make. You may also buy extra sidekicks which can help out, but aside from your Astrub Knight you have access to a different free trial sidekick every once in a while.
Overall:
Steam is asking me if I recommend this game and do I? I'm a little torn, but yes I do. This is a very fun game with combat mechanics that require you to actually think when things don't go as planned. The community is there and very friendly but only if you take the time to actually look for them. When you're feeling bored of grinding mobs, go grind resources! Its tedious but addicting after a while.
TL;DR
Game is fun, try it out. RTFR.

This is one of the most original MMORPG's I've played in my life, I started playing Dofus and checked Wakfu since the beta, and I loved it. I don't get how this F2P sequel hasn't get as much popularity as it's prequel, but it totally deserves it. I'm sure that Wakfu, after five years of development (on it's current state) is way better game than Dofus, but still we can't get sufficient people to play on the servers, we have a stable but very small community, while Dofus after 10 years keeps having hundreds of thousands even being mainly P2P... This game is far from dying and a very unique MMO experience by it's combat system (I haven't found any other like this), and I'm sure there's a lot of people out there that would like to play Wakfu with their friends (it's extremely better playing on groups), they just don't know this game exists, and that's really sad. The game left the beta last year and is still being updated regularly with new areas, characters, equipment... If you played games like Final Fantasy Tactics or Disgaea, you'll absolutely love this.
Pros:
-Unique combat system for an MMO.
-Beautiful and stilish graphics which don't require high-end computers.
-Twelve totally different classes to choose between (they've specialized even more since the Spell Deck update).
-Seventeen useful professions to level up if you get bored of doing quests, dungeons or whatever that will help you in your journey.
-Two thousands levels, imagine how many different mobs, dungeons and loot can you get while leveling up
-F2P, everything is free, you can absolutely get the same benefits than a Premium user just by playing, the in-game shop is purely cosmetic (and doesn't has the best items).
Cons:
-The combat system can get repetitive (this has been tweaked a bit since the Spell Deck update, what's more, since the release of the game, if you're Premium (which is roughly 6$ a month) you get +100% xp (cap at +300%) if you have a character of higher level than the one you're using, so you'll progress faster which means you won't be stuck at any specific zone).
-It's hard to team-up with Premium users if you're a low-leveled non-premium player, they'll get way more xp than you and soon, you'll have to leave them or get carried while doing nothing (but seriously, you can pay 20 cents a day and get a Booster, problem solved and you help the devs).
-Extremely low playerbase: you'll be assigned to a server near your location to avoid lag (or you can use Remingtong, which is international), but most of the servers have only around 1000 players, that's really sad, let's change this.
I really think you must give Wakfu an opportunity, it's a really good game and you can play it for free, with or without friends, and for only 6$ per month you can get some benefits to progress faster, I'm sure you've paid 60$ for worse games than this.

Sonic Adventure 2 is said to be the best 3D Sonic game, but people who say that look at this game with nostalgia. I know it's an old game, but it have so many issues with the camera, controls and audio among other things.
Pros
- The speed stages are enjoyable.
- The story is interesting.
- Chao garden can be fun, but gets boring fast.
- Awesome soundtrack.
Cons
- Speed gameplay is the only good gameplay style in this. The others feel tedious and boring. I play Sonic to go fast and platform not sit in a stupid mech and shoot stuff.
- Poor audio mixing. I don't even need to say anything more.
- This game have aged poorly overall.
- The final boss is pretty lame, however the music makes up for it... I guess?
- GLITCHES. I don't know how many times I died because Tails or Eggman clipped through the floor in their stupid mechs.
Summary.
If someone says Sonic Adventure 2 is the best 3D Sonic game ever, it's NOT. It may be your personal opinion and I respect that, but people saying it's the best one like it's fact seriously need to take off their nostalgia googles.
This game is fun, if you take out anything that's not Sonic and Shadow in terms of gameplay.
However, I'm going to be nice to this game and say the game is solid if you like platforming, a bit of speed, awesome music and a good story you'll probably enjoy Sonic Adventure 2.

On your initiative phase, you get 3 action points (max 5) to cast spells, use units and their abilities. Then turn passes over to your enemy and he does his♥♥♥♥♥♥ You keep on doing this back and forth until one player completes their objective.
Conclusion, it's just an experiment using chess rules and trying to get players who like the Warhammer 40K sauce to buy it. The game doesn't offer much in terms of story or gameplay.
1. WH40K Lore
That's basically the main draw of the game.

While other games like XCOM have tactical movement and upgrade tactical aspects, Regicide literally copies chess. You have pawns, knights, bishops, queens, rooks and kings. All the rules are the same.

Now, as a Wizard enthusiast, I cannot recommend this game highly enough. Not only does this game contain Wizards, it allows you to PLAY as one of those wizards.
In gameplay not unlike Demon Souls/Dark Souls/Dark souls II/Bloodborne/Dark Souls III, this game allows for online play, but not just friendly, Wizardly duels. These online matches are for posturing, flexing your might at your opponents and pushing them around when they try to posture back. It isn't the greatest mind, or the fastest hand that wins, it's the biggest jerk.
Tricky Towers has players stacking blocks of varying shapes to satisfy various outcomes:
- get to the top first
- don't fall over
- and a third one
Whilst you are trying to get ahead of your competitors, sometimes you can gain the ability to cast a spell, each time you have a choice of two. You can choose the spell that effects you, mostly in a positive way, or you can choose the spell taht effects your opponents, mostly in a negative way. The fact is that in four-player your negative spell effects three people, and that's just too good value for money to not do. Sure, you could cast yourself the vine spell and then you have yourself a nice solid base there sir, or you could cast the OBSCURING MIST on THREE IDIOTS. Now which of those sounds instantly more satisfying? Thats right, it doesn't involve solid bases. More like the opposite.
Tricky Towers is a very fun game which can be played online or couch co-op, which is fantastic. It can almost reach Mario Party levels of hate-fun when you have a few friends all together casting spells on each other constantly to mess everyone up.
The only better thing is actually being a Wizard.

I just finished the game (11 hrs, Survival, 38 deaths) and I'm here to tell my own honest opinion about The Evil Within.
PROS:
-Atmosphere is decent
-Scavenging (This is good since ammo and meds are scarce and there are A LOT of enemies through out the game, you have to save your ammo for tougher enemies/situation especially in the later chapters. And the upgrades as well, be sure to search the area thoroughly for green jars.)
-Upgrades (Use your green gel wisely.)
-Stealth (Use your surroundings to your advantage.)
-One-time events. (The statues.)
-Laura (Adrenaline will run through your whole body.)
-Ruvik (The mansion chase part. It really adds tension since he can kill you instantly and you NEED to escape him.)
CONS:
-Bugs (for example, you have to Examine something and it will take a minute or two for the camera to return to its original position. In Chapter 3, when you're inside the barn, you can trigger the Sadist boss fight even though you're at the second floor.)
-Graphics (Subpar.)
-Boss fights (You'll end up saying, "That's it? or What the hell just happened?!". Seriously, boss fights should be challenging.)
-Oversensitive traps.
-You can already tell what's gonna happen.
-Double barrel shotgun is useless.
-Game is too dark. (Crank up the brightness, the game loses its scare factor. Lower the brightness, just turn off your pc.)
-The crow carrying a statue. (It is designed to waste your bullets, if you can't aim properly.)
-There's a new definition for the term headshot.
-Checkpoints + Ridiculous deaths (I don't want to repeat what I just did a minute ago because of my unusual death.)
-Chapter 15 (Especially the last part. Are you serious?!)
-Detective Castellanos can't jump.
Overall, this game is okay. You can clearly tell that this is just a port because of the graphics, control, and the cut scenes. I'll give this game a 6/10 since it's a letdown because I'm expecting Evil Within to deliver a RE2/RE3 type of experience but, unfortunately, it didn't.

What is Boson X? It's an infinite runner.
In every level there are floating platforms thrown around everywhere and you have to keep pushing forward and do your best not to fall down cause if you do it's game over. Your goal in each level is to find short strips of ground covered in glowing color (pardon my lack of scientific language but it probably has something to do with particles or some other obscure science stuff my simple mind can't comprehend) and run through them. The longer you run through those glowing stripes the more percentage is added to your actual score.
In order to finish a level you have to reach the limit set by the developers. Once you do you can still keep going (a lot faster than before, mind you) but the level is complete and you get the achievement (there are 18 achievements, each for completing each level) and you unlock new levels.
That's it. You have to do that in each level in order to beat the game. There's no plot, graphics are not amazing (good for its purpose though) and the game is very simple in its premise. Don't be fooled though, it's without question one of the hardest games available on Steam. If you like runners and challenges make sure to play this one as it's addictive as hell plus very rewarding, satisfaction you get from completing each level can't be compared to anything else.
Pros:
+ Fast paced
+ Good music and nice visuals
+ Very challenging and rewarding
+ "One more time, I swear" type of addiction
Cons:
- After you're done you wish it had twice as many levels
- Not easy on the eyes if you play it for long (especially the last level)
Rating: 9/10

Boson X is a quick fast paced runner game where you have to dodge obstacles and step on blue colored platform to collect some sort of percentage. The game will finish after you earn 100%, although you can still continue after that to aim for high score in an altered colored mode. There is also a high score list which is sorted by the said percentage.
This game is using 2D models on 3D environment and the characters are soft colored. I really like the character design and animation when they are running through the stages. The UI is also simple and easy to understand.
There are roughly 6 bgms in total which is played in each area. Each bgm has their own different characteristic and I really like the music except for the Graviton and Dark X Boson stage. The first one sounds like you're in temple and the second one is way too quiet.
This game is easy to learn but hard to master. You just have to jump through obstacles and (or) move left and right to dodge them. At some point, there will be a blue platform which will help you obtain some percentage. You'll finish the stage after you obtain 100%, although you still can continue the game to aim for high score in an altered color afterwards which might hurt your eyes. The more percentage you have, the faster your character will run.
There are 3 different areas which consists of 6 stages. Each area has its own unique mechanics which is slightly different from each other. The first few stages will serve as a tutorial (yet still difficult for beginners) to introduce new general mechanics and some stages and area will be unlocked after you complete a particular stage.
There are also 3 different characters to use although i doubt that there will be any difference except for their sfx when they are running. I have gotten used to the first female character which makes me can't focus when i switch it to the robot character.
Each stage took less than 10 minutes to beat. However, you'll spend more time to beat it because you have to remember and practice for each patterns in every stage. In the last level of each area, the view will be slightly altered which can hurt your eyes (especially the last stage in the last area, Dark X Boson).
When you died (and fail to complete the stage), there will be a graph which shows your progress in the last few runs. I really like the design because i can see how far i'm improved.
I don't know the reason why, but you can't pause mid game. If you have to do an important stuff when you're aiming for high score, you're doomed. There is also no restart button in case you messed up. However, this won't really matter because you can kill yourself easily.
Pros:
- 18 stages
- 3 different characters
- Challenging stages
- High scores
Cons:
- Some level hurts your eyes
- Can't pause mid game
- No restart button

Everyone says this game is like Left 4 Dead, and it absolutely is... If Left 4 Dead was way more out to kill you and had loot and was in a medieval setting with violent rat people that want to eviscerate you. This game is absolutely rad and probably my favorite video game based on the classic Warhammer universe.
You can choose between a few different classes, each using a different style of ranged weapon and melee weapon, and each with different armors and trinkets. Then you get to try to survive in an objective and progressive map that will throw enemies at you to swarm you. It's absolutely a team game, if you do not co-operate, you will not survive. Co-operation is key; and therefore, so is communication.
From the very beginning I noticed this game was dark and gritty, as you would expect from Warhammer, but this is way more intense than most other stuff we've seen from Warhammer. Use a single handed blade weapon to chop off heads or limbs, but switch to two handed and you can chop off the torso from the legs, watching the legs wobble before eventually giving in to gravity. Blood is everywhere, and the intensity of every battle is evident by this. The wounds on giant rats and special enemies will have you swinging in a panic. But nothing is more satisfying than pinning an enemy to a wall with a headshot from your bow. The soundtrack really kicks tail and gets the blood pumping at all the right moments. Vermintide has way more replayability than L4D with its loot and progressive system. An all around enjoyable experience that I highly recommend.
+ Great graphics
+ Intense, violent, dark, and gritty
+ End Times setting is perfect for a Warhammer game like this
+ Melee feels fantastic
+ Ranged weapons feel impactful
+ Magic feels powerful but straining in the right ways
+ Characters communicate
+ Loot
+ Progressive system
+ Absolutely fun with friends
+ Great soundtrack
- Heavy reliance on communication
- Intensity has a tendency to fade
- Not so much fun alone

TLDR: a game featuring interesting water physics and mediocre everythingelse. Worth the usual asking price of 0.50€ during sales  (but what wouldn't worth for that money?) but I'm not sure if it's worth your time.
It may be interesting on a proper, strong computer if you want to check a tech-demo of water physics, but as a game it's horribly optimized - just as a reference as my laptop's specs wouldn't say much. I can play Arkham Asylum on 1366*768 without much changes I think medium-ish graphics with 30-60 fps. In Hydrophobia I got 19 fps in the credits. It's a scrolling white text before black background.
As I said, the game is more of a tech demo. Opening doors with water behind them makes the water pour out, changing the water level, pushing items and you backwards, explosions don't just slash but really make the water moving, which is nice. But this does not serve as an excuse to have messy keyboard controls, way too high mouse sensitivity with mandatory autoaim, using a controller is gimped because not having reversed Y, only X axis, and the enemies often just forget to shoot you. They just walk in front of you, not even noticing you, even during the bossfight.
Gameplay: Third person, consisting about shooting, running, ladder- and pipeclimbing, door-opening and repeating a hacking minigame. It's incredibly unoriginal.
The bossfight at the end is also a letdown. You get powers to control water during the story which is cool, but the previous reviews were right - you get the power about TWO rooms before the bossfight, so you throw a bench away, complete a simple but well-used puzzle with the powers, shoot a few soldiers and there you go, bossfight, use your power to defeat it, woohoo!

When I finally got a gun and started shooting bad guys, the dudes where just standing there, blood sprayed after getting hit, but it didn't seem to affect them physically, unlike WinBack, if you shoot a knee, the guy winces in pain grabbing his leg, and that was on N64.
Anyway, nice effort, but this game is just mediocre. A good game is worth playing 5, 10 or 30 years after its release. This one seems to have been badly received even on its year of release.

I chose to "recommend" this game, but I'm actually quite on the fence. It's definitely worth playing when it's on sale for a dollar or so, but I think it's more of a cool experience than an enjoyable game.
The game looks very good, even if you can tell it's a few years old now. The water system is definitely unique, and it looks the best when you're running through a wet hallway and a wave of water comes sloshing at you. The game basically feels like an interactive movie. You control the action but your objectives are quite linear, so it feels like you're trying to play along as smoothly and effectively as possible. Although the combat is clunky, I enjoy the cover system and sometimes you can look kind of badass. I definitely think of the game as a sort of interactive movie. On the "game" side of things, I think the type of gamers who enjoy "perfecting" their abilities might enjoy playing through this game a few times so that they get to the point where the can complete it flawlessly. I think it would be really satisfying if you could beat the whole thing without dying and with maximum badassery.
Okay, so I tried to put a positive spin on the game by calling it an "experience", an "interactive movie", and highlighting the potential to have a really satisfying perfect playthrough once you've gotten used to the game. But the fact is that it's a bit short, and not exactly a lot of fun. There are a lot of really cool environmental elements (shooting objects, using cover, fighting against and eventually controlling water, shooting electrical cords to remove hazards, etc.), but because these elements are all novel, you have your hand held the whole time. Ideally a game like this would be longer so that you could learn everything and then be left to your own devices, or maybe learn one element at a time and have a few chambers to solve on your own. Movement and combat are quite cumbersome, so it always feels like you're supposed to be accomplishing things faster and more elegantly than you do. And although the water is really cool when you're running through it, don't the developers know that underwater levels are the absolute worst part of platform games? It would be qutie an amazing feat to make those fun, and Hydrophobia sadly didn't. Eventually you get the power to control water, but honestly I used it as little as possible because it just wasn't enjoyable. The main "replay" value of the game, aside from the intrinsic value of having cooler run-throughs, is to get a higher score on each of the three acts and the challenge room. But having completed them all, I'm still not really sure how to significantly improve my score.
I do recommend trying this game out. It only takes about 4 hours to finish, so you may as well see it for yourself. But its definitely in a weird place... It sort of feels like a demo for a larger game, except it's way too intricate and polished to be just a demo. Maybe if it were longer and a bit more polished, then it would feel like a GOOD game. I can't put my finger on why it's not, but it isn't..

I absolutely love Sonic Adventure! The jenk of that game somehow combines with Sonic beautifully! Sonic controls buttery smooth and the absurd speed and air you can get from spindashing are just insanely fun. Sonic is of course the main attraction but that's not to say the other characters aren't entertaining. Tails is all about out jenking sonic by abusing flight for shortcuts. Knuckles has fairly entertaining treasure hunts. The other characters are also fun, yes even big the cat, probably the one I like the least is Amy but they don't matter for this review.
Now... having said that Sonic Adventure 2, which I do need to compare to the first one, somehow manages to make everything in the first game feel worse... Sonic is a lot more stiff, yes he is easier to control because he moves far slower but once you get used to the ludicrous physics of the first game there's no going back. Sonic's fast yet responsive, in the sequel he is far more sluggish in every sense. You can no longer do immediate spindashes and they aren't useful at all. Sonic has forgone its marvelous jenk for a more standard yet obtuse way of play. Even the levels are worse. For some reason there are bottomless pits everywhere and many a time you will fall off unexpectedly. Tails is stuck in a mech that's just... not fun. You lock on into enemies and then let go to shoot. It's slow, tedious and annoying. Knuckles might just have it the worse though. His levels are huge and the radar is completely screwed up. It no longer pings when next to treasure unless it's the first one on the list. You can't freely explore most of the time, sometimes shards only spawn when it's their turn. Meaning you'll have to go to a place again to look for a newly spawn shard. I've had levels last up to 40 minutes with Knuckles because of all the running around and back tracking that is needed. Now I focused on these 3 characters but their counterparts on the dark side suffer from the exact same problems. I feel like SA2 is the one everyone talks about but it is far inferior to its predecessor. I had more frustration than fun with this game, something that happen very rarely with the first. I just cannot recommend this game unless you are absolutely curious about it.

Silent Hunter V is the last game in the WWII submarine simulator series. It's buggy, unstable, with odd design choices that take away some of the freedom of the past games. While being able to walk around your sub is cool, was it worth it at the cost of everything else? In my opinion, no it wasn't. Especially since on top of that the game is riddled with bugs and is generally unstable.
But why then would I be conditionally recomending it?
Simply put, The Wolves of Steel Modpack. Wolves of Steel compiles many mods (and makes some changes of its own) to make the game much more like the previous games in the series in terms of simulation (no more tonnage bar for example). Since it is a "full realism" modpack, playing with it can be extremely difficult and you'll most likely spend many hours watching YouTube tutorials on things such as target recognition, RAOFB use, using the TDC for manual torpedo firing, and more. It's not for everyone. On top of that, you do need to use some elbow grease to allow it to work with the Steam version. I installed the mods ages ago, only really started playing it recently, so I don't have much memory of that work but it couldn't have been too bad if I could get it to work.
If hardcore sub-sims appeal to you, then SH5 with the Wolves of Steel pack is simply put the best out there. So if you're into that, I can cautiously recomend the game (due to the unstable nature, and work involved in getting WoS working with the Steam version its still "cautious" for that group). If you're not into that at all, stay away.
Silent Hunter 5 lacks both the familiarity of the older games in the series and the innovative aspects that might have made it stand well on it's own.

If you liked Left 4 Dead, then you will certainly adore this game, as many refer to it as a spiritual successor to L4D. It adopts almost the exact same formula, with special enemies and co-op play. However, it places enough of a twist to make it different. This game is focused heavily on its melee mechanics rather than the "shooter" nature of L4D. As such, the skill level may be higher as it is required for players to be proficient in dodging, blocking and parrying attacks to perform well, especially at higher difficulties.
Levels are varied enough that each one is interesting to play through over and over again. However, after completing the game, you will find yourself in the pursuit for loot. Thus, if replaying same levels or grinding for loot isn't your cup of tea, this game will probably not provide you the amount of enjoyment that many of its current playerbase is getting. Ultimately, this is a L4D spin-off with RPG elements that certainly proves worthwhile if you have a party to play with.
If you are already a fan of the rich Warhammer universe, then Vermintide is a must-buy as it does such a big service to followers of the lore. It is very faithful to its source material, and the designs do just that. The characters are so full of life and backstory that gets you invested in them. The witty banter provides for enriching dialogue. The equipment used by the heroes are so rich in detail that it even tells its own stories.
Graphics are superb, but the game may not be fully optimized so only high-end machines can run this game reliably at the highest settings with an acceptable framerate.
Personally, this was my best purchase of 2015.
Edit: After almost a year after release, this game is pretty much dead. I suggest buying this game only if you have a group of friends to play with. Still a great game nonetheless. Not worth if playing solo.

Quite possibly the most addicting game I have in my Library.
What makes Boson X so great? Its simple formula. You jump from one platform to the next, trying to land on the blue ones to fill up an energy bar. When the energy bar gets to 100%, you have completed the level. But you can keep playing to try and increase your score even further.
Sounds simple? It is! Only it gets harder as you go. Much harder. First, the levels keep speeding up as your score gets higher, which makes an already hectic game even more hectic. Levels also get harder, much harder. The difficulty jump between the first and the last level in the game is astronomically high. Soon you will deal with more hazards. Platforms that drop once you step on them, platforms that come at you with speed and lightning bolts of DEATH are just a few examples of what you will have to deal with.
Some levels are just pure evil! Platforms coming at different angles, entire levels spinning around and jumps that at first seem impossible to make. Boson X is a really fun ride from the very beginning to the very end. While we are on the subject, let's talk about replay value.
I have completed this game in about 7 hours. And as of writing this review, I have 71 hours on record and I expect that Boson X will soon join the "Over 100 hours" Club. Why? Two words. Steam Leaderboards. This is the prime reason why I bought Boson X. I'm not a very competitive person by nature and most of the games I play are single player. But Boson X is an exception. The fact that I have a leaderboard where I can check my scores against other players provides a constant challenge for me. And it fuels the addicting part of the game. I want to go as high as I can on leaderboards. Even thought I have replayed a level close to 1k times, I still want to improve myself.
That is incredibly fun. Having a lot of bad runs and then having one great run that pushes you up the leaderboard gives you a big a sense of accomplishment. And then you want more, more, more, MORE! :)
The graphics are very simple, but they just work. Some levels look amazing, almost like you are in a different world.
The sound design is just right. The sound when you run on the blue platform and your score increases is the best sound in the world.
The music is simple. Each level has two loops that last about 15 seconds each. But the music works so well and is so charming that I didn't even notice how short the loops are. They just fit the game and what's going on the screen.
I only have one minor complaint and that is that I sometimes get random FPS lag where my FPS drops from otherwise rock solid 60 FPS to around 40 FPS. The FPS lag usually clears up quickly if it starts in the middle of the run. And if the lag starts at the beginning of the run, I simply restart the level. I don't think that's the game, I think that's my machine and OpenGL being a bit funky. But It's nothing major. Otherwise, the game is polished and has no bugs.
Still not sure if you want this game or not? Try the free version then! Boson X started as a free game, which later released on Steam with more content and Steam Leaderboards. So if you like the free version, get this one to support the amazing devs and get 12 more levels and 2 more playable characters. The price is fair compared to how many potential hours of fun you can get out of the game.
PS: This game is hard by the way. Super hard. It's one of those games that you are going to pull out your hair while playing. If that sounds fun to you, get the game. You won't regret it.
Boson X is a great platformer that can be completed in short and enjoyable sessions.

This game is breaking my heart, and no I'm not talking about the sappy story. In fact, I'm going to leave the story out of this review entirely. I'm here to talk about what could have been possibly the most immersive game I've ever played, COULD have been. I've been experiencing some incredibly irritating and immersion breaking bugs that are drastically limiting my enjoyment. Namely the terrain bugs, everything that's over four inches high you get stuck on. This happens everywhere with everything and It's killing the game for me. Try to walk into the weapons shop, oh hey, there's a single tiny step, now it's time to stop and try to jump or crouch or even walk backwards through the door, and be painfully painfully aware that I'm playing a buggy glitchy incredibly unpolished video game. One that would probably be one of my favorite games of all time if it wasn't hell to travel through. Radio Tower? RADIO TOWER?!?!?!?!?!
There's also the not quite bug, but say, terribly implimented hill physics, where you're walking up a slightly steep, but absolutely IRL walk overable hill and you find yourself sliding backwards and gaining momentum, then just kind of "water-sliding" over bushes and Tigers and Dingo's and♥♥♥♥♥♥until you fall into a river and get eaten by a crocodile....... Yes that happened, like ten minutes ago, yes I laughed my♥♥♥♥♥off, no It's not always that amusing. Usually it's just irritating and again, immersion breaking as all hell. It's like someone pushed you backwards onto a slip and slide. This game has a special way of making you lose yourself into it that I love, it's just that for every amazing step forward, there's some sort of bug or bit of wonkyness that breaks the spell every time. It's frustrating enough for me to write this, though I'm still giving it a thumbs up I'd say a good two points get shaved off my rating. If this were ever fixed, like by Ubisoft, unofficial patches and mods that might help don't count in my eyes, I'd give this a 9/10. As it is, recieved through steam with nothing but in game options tweaked. It's a 7/10 for me. I'm tempted to lower that to a 6/10 for BREAKING MY HEART! But I'll try to leave at least some of my saltiness at the moment out of it. It's still recommended though, there's a reason this is the second time I've bought it and the third time I've played it. I would be interested to know if it's better on consoles. I've never played the console version, but I've had this terrain issue on two PC's.

A suprisingly entertaining game that deserves a try by anyone who enjoys turn based strategy games! Obviously similar at first glace to games like Final Fantasy Tactics and the Disgaea series, but with it's own twist and features for online multiplayer!
A few hours in and I still have quite a lot of learn about how to play Wakfu, but that's part of the fun! The medium strength learning curve means things may feel familiar to you from other games, but not entirely.
One of the best designs is the classes themselves. A large number to choose from and not the standard, boring names and designs like Warrior, Mage, and ...well actually there is a Rogue, but it's cool! The artistic design of this game is fantastic and also adds to the familiar, but fresh feeling that Wakfu brings!
Oh, and you get a crate for your bag....house...thing! :D

First impression review:
They are not kidding when saying this game have too much cutscene.
The game is good, the water physics is great even for 6 years old game, the combat style is interesting.
#################
Updated review:
Okay, review updated after finishing main game. So my updated impression is:
✔ The concept is great, and interesting,
❌ but the story is not, I think they made it carelessly, look like this is a demo game for their engine.
❌ It's short, but not too short, just 3 hours of gameplay. Again, think it's just their demo,
✔ The water physics is so great, I am impressed.
❌ Cutscene: I think they can't mix main key element stories in your gameplay, so they decide to just make a lot of it.
✔ It has puzzles
❌ Too much gunfight, at first it look like an adventure & puzzle game, then it change to "just like another FPS game", a single heroine shoot as many bad guy as she can, and then
✔ in last minute (maybe 30 mins) of gameplay she got a super power that I think it is not so magic-ish, but a sci-fi-ish (a plus for me)
❌ but I can't play with her super power for a long time, again it's short. And too bad the developers/studio is closed, so the sequel is unlikely.
6/10 - I like it, but the series is dead, and I hate it. But still like it.
5.5/10 - If you are into fps with beautiful water physics, give it a try. If story matters to you, skip this.

I don't write many game reviews, but I felt it was necessary to write one for Scrap Mechanic. So here's the basic rundown of the game in my mind and in this review I will be listing items that I think should be addressed.
So far on this game at the time of writing this review I have almost 16.5 hours played. As far as Early Access games go, this one is by far the most advanced from Launch Date that i've ever
seen on Steam, from Launch it had more than enough to keep you busy for hours on end right out of the gates, not very many games can say that. I started off watching the Videos on the game's
page like the Introducing ones that showcased the Controller, Thruster etc etc, then as I experimented and numerous trial and error situations, I started getting better and better at knowing
what was going on and how things click. I started with a little piddly concrete car with a horendous design, but then I started to get more intricate with my designs, using pipes and I-Beams
to make an overall badass design, then I found out the steering mechanics and how to work the controller with ease, once all this clicked I made some of my best creations.
As fun as this game is when you're alone, I thought to myself, "Wow, this would be so fun if I had some buds to play this game with." Sure enough this game was already equipped with a
Multiplayer from Launch! At first that seems amazing, but then once you start getting a total of 4 players and even sometimes 2 players, the servers lag tremendously, my friends and I
both checked and we came to the conclusion that it was in fact server side lag, now I know the game came out almost a week ago, but I think that Dedicated Servers should be a rather large
priority for a game of this proportion. Overall, the Multiplayer in this game is rather flawless when I doesn't lag, it makes for an amazing experience with friends and it has so much potential
like the rest of this game. My rating for the Multiplayer alone is a solid:
8/10- This rating due to the Server Side Lag, which can be fixed in the future, otherwise, its spotless.

Right kiddie bops, get ready for the only review you will need for this game. Period...
I bought this tasty game about a year ago and I am well and truly hooked even now.
Its game play is smooth and seemless, perfectly crafted mechanics make for an enjoyable and attractive experiance.
It has several game types (with more coming) the best of them, which i would recomend buying the game for alone it "Hunted".
Hunted pits player against player in action packed, thrilling and challenging game play on maps built to test the players skill and ability to not only survive the Zombie Horde but to loot and salvage what weapons they can to fight off fellow players. You can sneak through the streets, baracade houses or try your luck and be ballsy. The goal is to out live the other players .
The game has themes similar to that of Left For Dead but in my personal opinion and in the opinion of many in the Contagion comunity is that Contagion is far the superior game despite being a small budget Indi Game.
This game is not expensive and is often on sale but no price can really be put to the mass amounts of fun i have recived from this endearing and exciting game. Playing on this game with a friend or on your own i can garentee you a good time.
AND HEY, if you dont like it (which you will) there is a Steam Refund System so try this game and trust me you wont need to use it but if you somehow dont like it, trying the game wont hurt you or your wallet.

I have been an Adventure Quest fan since 2008 and I have been waiting for this game to release for quite some time now. Most of the people who play it love it and praise it because they know the company and games so dearly. I can say that I am one of those people, however, I am not going to review this game like one.
First off, don't expect any next-gen groundbreaking graphics from this game. I feel that people are giving this game so much crap for what it really is : A game based off cartoonish and silly animation.
This game is at the bare bones of its early stages as well. The game has just been developed in to working beta stage and people are treating like its verion 600.
The game is just being bult so don't expect much from it in that extent.
Needless to say, the game features a loads of monsters, quests, items, and lets you fully customize your character with stat based items. You can spend hours after hours on this game with your friends just doing quests and farming for rare items. Overall, the gameplay is relatively fun.
What makes this game amazing is the atmostphere and community. You will have so much fun meeting and teaming up with fellow players to go and defeat dungeons and quests. With the new release of The Ashfall Saga, you and your friends can embark on a very witty and challenging adventure.
So if you don't want to read all of the above review, here is a short pro and con list.
Pros:
Fun
Witty and funny dialogue
Great Community
Vast customization of character
Fun for farming
Great time spender
Can play on truly ANY device
Cons:
Extremely challenging
Cannot solo your way through the game
Requires much training in one area before you can proceed
Graphics may be a turn off
All items have stats so you can only wear the items with highest stats rather than wearing whatever you want
Not too much of a storyline yet
Buggy at times
Requires much time to be put in to the game

The toughest gripe about this video game is purely knowing and literally seeing the potential spread between the mess that's the length and shortcomings within the story. It's either presenting itself as a disjointed short cinematic film purposely filled with unanswered questions or what would become a bloated adventurous game had it been thoroughly developed with care. Various things were heavily underutilized to an extent and would've given it a broader identity had there been various adjustments. There's particular creative sequences that surprisingly twists expectations but are merged between some tedious ideas that could either downgrade the enjoyment or levitate the replay value.

A tale of two games, Hydrophobia prophecy starts wonderfully. Trapped aboard a city-sized ship as it is attacked by terrorists, you must survive and hide with your heroine's athletic climbing abilities. You'll be climbing and swinging on pipes and scaffolding to make your way around. Swimming is a large aspect as water fills hallways and elevator shafts. The effects are beautiful and the water will knock around objects. Eventually you get a gun but combat starts minimal. The story seems interesting and there are cool notes scattered around. You can hack cameras and use them to open doors. There are even a few water puzzles.
Then everything takes a turn for the worse in the 3rd act. There is way too much combat and not enough of the platforming or climbing. You get the ability to control water somehow, but only get 1 power and it's a bit hard to control. More importantly, it's a "weapon" so you have either that or your pistol. The problem is that it doesn't switch well and it's difficult to attack using the water, which is what a player obviously wants to do. The game ends with a terrible boss fight that emphasizes the combat, which is the worst part of this game. The story just ends with no follow up on the other people you came into contact with.
I really enjoyed the first two thirds, but the final act was a horrible, frustrating, chore.

This is an interesting one.
There is definitely a lot of potential here- the game is great showcase for impressive water physics which brings the game alive and I don't think it has been bettered in a 3D action game since. Unforunately there is not a very good game around the water physics.
It's a action adventure / puzzle game.
This is the big feature of the game- realistic water that I don't think I have seen bettered in any newer game. The water is the main gimmick of the game (the premise of the game being you're on a sinking ship). Water realistically sloshes about, bounces off walls, creates waves, and if you open a door water will realistically pour out of / into the next room. The really nice bit is that the water level will eventually settle down- if one room is full of water and the next empty, open the door and both rooms will end up half full. Actually, it is more than a gimmick.
In the last 10 minutes of the game you unlock a weird water movement super power that doesn't really add anything and is a pain to use (you use it only a couple of times).
The puzzles are standard water-game puzzles: raise and lower the water level (by shooting leaky vents etc), put floating stuff under crates / containers (like the boat level in HL2). However the water physics distracted me just enough to not find them tedious. I would have liked to see "better" (I know that isn't very informative!) puzzles (maybe with the ship listing to one side) as the water physics, in my opinion, can hold the game up on its own if utilised well.
The combat is adequate and not really necessary; if the water puzzle aspect was built upon I think it could hold up the game by itself (after all it is the interesting game mechanic we're here to see!). You have a couple of different types of ammo for your one gun but it doesn't really add much- just shoot the bad guys and they die in slightly different ways. The game has a nasty habit of spawning dudes whenever and wherever it likes- you'll clear out a room, flick the switch to unlock a door and dudes will spawn back in the room you cleared (not even come storming through doors)
What I did like was the underwater gun battles- I can shoot dudes on land in thousands of games, but shooting dudes underwater is a lot rarer! Coupled with the water physics these were pretty good.
There are also uncharted-y climbing sections. These fit in a bit better with the watery game play and are again adequate but this time could definitely be improved and support the "watery adventure" gameplay without the gunplay if it was integrated like it is in uncharted.
(The graphics, the sound, the story, the voice acting...)
This is big let down for the game. The story is terrible, with the intro cutscene setting up some backstory of the player character having, you know,  a phobia of water but it is not mentioned once in the game (nor is a prophecy). There is no backstory as to if the world is a mess due to overpopulation, and how it got like that. No inforamtion as to why the tech company is respectable (after all, they're usually the bad guys!), or why we should trust Scoot the voice over the radio (co-incedentally he disappears without trace 2/3 of the way in and we never hear back from him at all! Is he dead?). No information on the ship we're on and you wouldn't know it was a ship if you missed the few lines of dialogue saying it is a ship- it could be any old industrial unit / bad guy base really.
There are no cutscenes within the game (other than the odd pan around an environment to show you a door you need to get to), or even at the end! This is not necessarily a bad thing; all the story is presented through the dialogue between ***** (can't even remember the main character's name!) and Scoot. This worked for games like Firewatch, but I did not feel as if the events in H:P affected the relationship between the two characters at all. They'll shout "OMG are you ok!?" over the radio but that's about it!
The voice acting is actually alright, especially when you consider it is an independent game from 2011. I've definitely heard a lot worse in the world of AAA games.
I would also like to add that the developers added a feedback menu within the game- choose the 'topic' you would liek to give feedback on (graphics, story, controls, water...) choose positive or negative, and why (boring, exciting, realistic, vague...). I think this is a really good idea and should be implemented as much as possible!
The developer has shut down their studio due to the low sales of H:P (their only game). This is a shame as the game (and water physics) had potential, and I hope they went on to do great things at other game development studios.

In my few hours playing Tricky Towers I have mostly played the 'endless puzzle' mode as it is the most similar to Tetris, which is why the game appealled to me. Here are the pros and cons:
Pros
- I really like the concept of Tetris with physics. Having to balance the blocks so that they don't fall is the most fun element of this game.
- The game looks great and has a nice style.
Cons
- If you make a mistake, it is very difficult to come back from it as the presence of gravity means that all your future blocks will just slide off the misplaced block, unless you manage to create a wall and roof around the misplaced block.
- The game creates floating blocks as the puzzle progresses, but these often spawn very close to the laser (which you fail if you surpass). This means that as your tetris blocks start moving faster as the puzzle progresses, sometimes they will hit the floating blocks and instantly fail the game for you. Maybe this is a feature but it seems like more of an annoying fault.
- When you rotate a tetris block, it swings around instead of instantly rotating. If you do this anywhere near placed blocks, the block you are holding will instantly drop and will tend to result in a misplace.
- The controls aren't amazing. Moving a block downwards, it seems to keep it's momentum after you stop and will usually crash into your tower. I figure they did this for stylistic effect but it ends up just being annoying. Also, trying to nudge a block into sideface crevice, sometimes you will time it right and sometimes you won't, it would be better if it was a little more forgiving on that front.
- I'm not really into the spells and random huge blocks of the other game modes.
These cons together mean that you can't make any clever manouvers, and if you make a mistake you will often have to restart. To me this is unlike how a Tetris based game should be, as the clever manouvers and coming back from mistakes are what make the game fun. Otherwise it is just mindless stacking blocks like this game seems to be. It's fun for a while but I find myself just wanting to play normal Tetris.
Suggestions
- It would be great if they could fix some of the cons I listed.
- Also, having customisable game modes (the player can change options such as removing the floating blocks from puzzle mode etc.)

While I do not recommend this game, I will address all aspects: the good, the bad and the ugly. Also, please note that this was just
(Also, not sure why it's showing 65 hours of gameplay. Definately lost my patience sooner than that.)
Good: Decent graphics, well done voice overs, realistic and immersive gameplay; You really feel like you in the cockpit sometimes.
