This game is pure genius.  The battle style is similar to Fire Emblem, but you can actually play with other people in real time.  Only annoyance might be waiting for them to complete their turn.  The game is colorful, bright, and welcoming.  Plenty of "classes" to choose, all which have a male/female version of them (even Robots).  Level up and do dungeons with your friends to gain equipment, stats, skills, items, and keys to more dungeons.
The game even features some other skills such as mining, farming, and crafting.  There seems to be always something to do.  The game even has competing nations, PVP, and guilds.
The only gripe I have with the game is that it's primarily sandboxed; in the beginning you'll have plenty of quests to get you going, but at some point the quests do stop, which leaves it up to you how you want to play the game.  Do you want to grind to the highest level?  Do you want to help newer people grind to the highest level?  Do you want to take it easy and become a farmer for the rest of your life? The choice is yours.  However, when I got boosted to a higher level, I had no idea what to do because of the limited amount of quests.

I really want to like this game.  I mean I REALLY want to like it.  There are a few things preventing me from giving my full life to this game.
-Pros-
-Great design and look
-Unique classes
-Interesting skills (more on this later)
-If you like tactical RPGs and MMOs then this is probably for you.
-Cons-
-VERY complicated for a beginner to get into. (this seems to be a theme)
-Not very beginner friendly, most things have to be explained by long-time players within the game.
-Skills are horribly explained, skill buffs/beduffs are explained in pop-ups within pop-ups within pop-ups at times.
-Very convoluted texts and quests.
-Some things such as haven bags, setting a location, and professions aren't explained very well at all.
-Unexplained reasoning for actions having to be taken by the player, such as HAVING to have a respec at lvl 10 or you cannot fight anything in the game, ever.  If this is a bug of some kind, it should be stated as such by the developer.  Otherwise, it's quite jarring to suddenly realize you can no longer battle anything in the game.
Again, this game is great and has wonderful depth to the classes and skill sets, but the convoluted execution of it all does not create a well-thoughtout package for beginners.  The tutorial in the beginning leaves much to be desired and only prepares the player for the battles.  Everything else in the game has to be found out, missed, or learned through other longtime players in the game.
I still recommend trying this game out and see if you are willing to spend the time necessary to learn all of what it has to offer.  I'm still learning as I go, gaining a little bit more knowledge as time goes on through other players.  It's a slow going process but it might pay off in the depth and fun to be had.

I do agree that the game has its shortcomings, e.g. physics being a mixed bag in that it isn't as refined as Dirt Rally, but it does have its share of strengths like more events and Your Stage, even if the latter tends to churn out repetitive or recycled corners. It would perhaps be better if we are given an option to make a handmade stage Far Cry-style, shaping terrain, adding roadways and scenery in however way you choose. Series veteran Nicky Grist returns to the co-driver's seat alongside Jen Horsey, and they did their parts well for the most part, even if it had a couple or so flaws as far as I have noticed. Overall I don't think the game is as bad as some make it out to be. DiRT 4 aims to provide more variety, but seasoned rally fans may want to go for either DiRT Rally or Richard Burns if buying a used copy or downloading it off the interwebs is your thing. To each their own I guess.
PROS:
* More events and disciplines
* Multiplayer sessions
* Pace notes from veteran co-drivers
* Your Stage
CONS:
* Stage generator is too basic and full of repetitive scenery
* Handling needs refinement for sim fans
* Graphics are a mixed bag
* Inconsistent AI
I'd give it a "thumbs sideways" if I wanted to, but I felt that would be too harsh for a game like this. Looking forward to what the Codies has in store for racing fans. :)

Coming into this game from Hotline Miami is quite the suprise. While both game are superficially similar, it feels like they were built on completely different priorities; hotline miami 2 trades some of the first game's amazingly well designed gameplay for story depth and level variety.
+The soundtrack manages to outdo the first game. A wide variety of tracks and artists complement every level.
At times the game feels more like a rythm music game than a gritty, ultraviolent action game.
+The game tells an interesting narrative: the levels bounce between different characters, settings and time periods to expand on the first game's story.
+There are many different levels; where the first game saw the player clear dozens of mobster infected apartments, wrong number sees you fighting in jungles, boats, hotels, warehouses and banks, all drawn in wonderful pixel art.
~ There is a massive difficulty increase, compared to the first game. Beating wrong number one provides a hard mode that somehow pushes the challenge even further. By itself, it would not be a problem if not for...
-Weaker level design. While the levels themselves look georgous, they are often very frustating to play. Wide spaces filled with gun using ennemies that see you before you see them. Unlike the first game, there are quite a few levels that
feel cheap, or railroad you into using a particular strategy.
-Removal of the mask system: Wrong number lets you choose from 0 to 5 variation on your character for each level. It's no longer possible to choose your playstyle from level to level, or to retry a level with a different strategy.
For whatever its flaws might be, Wrong Number did not fall in the trap of being a mission pack sequel. It feels like a worthy addition to the first game's story, and provides more of its hectic gameplay and excellent music. It's a must play for any fan of the first game.

I picked up Mount & Blade: Warband on sale during the 2014 Hoiday Sale on Steam. I had recently gotten the original Mount & Blade for free during the
Winter Sale and had been playing it. The original leaves a lot to desire and Warband actually does a pretty decent job of adding more content.
The premise of Mount and Blade is simple; You play a charcter who has traveled to the medival realm of Calradia which consists of multiple constantly warring kindoms. You can mind your own business and simply kill bandits, be a bandit, help villagers, or even start your own trading operation. Or if you want, you can ally (or just start and uprising) with one of the kingdoms and TAKE OVER THE WORLD!! (Well, not quite the world, the GAME world.)
The graphical differences between the two games are minimal. TaleWorlds has changed some armor and weapons and has added a bigger map with a new faction which is meant to resemble Arab cultures. If you've played the original, you'll also note some differences in how weapons are swung, while they are definitely more realistc, if you are used to the original then it takes some getting used to know when to release the mouse button to swing the weapon.
In War Band, TaleWorlds has added more quests and other things to do. Bandit quests are more present, you can get married, the role playing aspect of the game has been improved overall. And the premise of the original game has been preserved as well.
Overall, even if you own the first M&B, Warvand is well worth the buy for the added features and I absolutely reccommend it.

1 – GENERAL
Far Cry 3 is an open world FPS created by Ubisoft. It shares lots of the traditional Ubisoft game mechanics like climbing a tower to reveal part of the map, or having the chance to explore to know more about the story of the Island.
Speaking about story, the plot of the game is not the best I've seen, at best is solid, but we forgive all its faults when we see that characters are well built and one of the villains is probably one of the all time greatest in videogames. Resumed, you are on vacations on an Island with your friends and you are caught by pirates. If you want to know more, just play the game.
Graphics still old even from today's standards, but I've experienced a lot of framedrops after a nVidia update, later partially solved, but I still suffer from unexpected framedrops when driving vehicles. The world is not as beautiful as in Ghost Recon Wildlands, but is still very enjoyable to watch.
Sound effects are well set together, but the NPCs have just a little amount of voicelines, so we spend most game listening to the same ones. The music is atmospheric, and it always sets a good mood for gunfights, despite that it changes when every NPC is dead, so we know when we can stop paying attention.
2 – GAMEPLAY
Most of the game fights are satisfying, guns are properly balanced and they all feel different and fun to play. We have to loot corpses and boxes to gather money to buy and upgrade weapons, but after a while they all become free at shops, so all money is only important until a certain part of the game, after that it just become useless.
Most times you can approach a mission from more than one angle, and that's rewarding. Sometimes a mission has a small difficulty spike, nothing to worry about, but you end up going by trial and error, and eventually you end up doing the mission with just brute force.
There's tons to explore in the islands, and also a lot to search and find. Interestingly enough the map is not packed full of repetitive missions that we have to do in order to develop our skills. I've mostly just done the main story and some sidequests, and I still progressed at a good pace. It took me about 20h to finish the story, I think that a completionist can take another 30h from the game, or even more, so the balance between story and repetitive sidequests seems to me spot on. Way better than actual games. Now is not common to say this, but thumbs up Ubisoft!
3 – CONCLUSION
I have three major problems with this game:
· Its peak is not the ending, but the killing of the firs villain;
· The best moments of the game are QTE, and that ruins the fun;
· Both endings are not very inspired.
There's still some funny bugs, but none of those ruins the experience, they are just fun.
Multiplayer is still active, even more than lawbreakers, but is not very interesting.
So, do I recommend the game? OFC, it's a great game, that worth's the current full price, but is so easy to find it in a sale, that I recommend you to wait a bit of one of those.

I went back and forth a lot on this game. When it runs well it's a pretty fun 3PS, but there's weird bugs all the time, and you can just randomly die with very little warning (because of a fire thats under the water you can't see).
I like the storyline, not to give away spoilers but it's kind of bioshockish, but I can't be bothered to read 400 journal entries, so I can't say for sure. What I get from cutscenes and character conversations is pretty interesting.
The controls are pretty terrible though (at least the underwater ones) when you're swimming and you press spacebar the camera will freak out like a cat in a tumble drier and spin uncontrollably while you push your head against whatevers above you. If there isn't anything above you, then you'll IMMEDIATELY surface. Press C to go down, which immediately pins you to the floor. Swimming is pretty rough, and this is compounded by the fact that the game celebrates its water physics. The cover based shooting isn't bad, cover to cover works, I don't get what sprint does, except that she leaps forward about 5 feet then resumes regular walking speed. Also the majority of my deaths were from her not quite making a jump correctly, or invisible fireballs in the water (or from trying to get a stupid diary near fire that pretty much insta kills you). Rarely did the AI have a hand in any of my injuries.
The enemy AI is dumb as a box of rocks, and will scan every square inch of where you aren't. They'll miss constantly, which isn't always a good thing as there always seems to be 400 exploding barrels and electrical boxes nearby. In more open firefights its useful, but the thing is supposed to be stealthy.
I like this game, I do, but the bugs kind of kill it, and honestly if this was from a bigger developer, or not under 50 cents I don't think I'd reccomend it. I might pay a few bucks for it, because it is pretty good, but its just kind of a let down for much more.

Hydrophobia is an enjoyable little game that can easily be finished in two to three hours. It's a platformer with mild shooting elements set on a floating city beseiged by Malthusian-inspired terrorists.
The game is surprisingly feature rich for a small title like this, and the water effects are particularly impressive. You can open doors to flood rooms or drain them, you can use water to knock down and stun enemies, and you can also use water to overcome environmental hazards like fires or stray electrical wires. There's also a novel hacking minigame.
Considering the length, I'd appraise the game at $5.00 to $7.50 at most, and anything equal to or beneath that price point is a steal.
There's a plot, but it's told mainly through picked up documents. There's also a few fun little easter eggs for gamers.
If you like aquatic games, platforming, and blowing people away with a sonic pistol, then I recommend you check this one out.

I've only played this game as Germany so I guess this review will be more or less a little biased. I am not saying yes to recommend but I don't have any options. But anyways I' ll get started:
Germany is extremely outclassed, at least by 5 years, when compared to US and the Soviets. You start of with a Gehwer which really isn't a match against M1 Garand. The M1 should be able to kill a man with 2 shots at medium range, but on the other hand, the Gehwer is a 3 shot kill in most cases and paired with ridicilous recoil (they both use the same ammo). You still can fight with it of course, just takes some more work. And MP 34 was made in 1934, which is your first submachine gun. While the Soviets start with their huge mag PPsh and US their grease guns, both I picked up if I ever saw one. List goes on...
Tanks. Lots of people rant about tanks. And I don't reject. When you level up high enough, you will jump into much bigger maps with light tanks, medium tanks, etc. There is often too many tanks vs infantry, which doesn't really make sense unless every battle was the Battle of Kursk. I often encounter maps where American M1 Stuarts and Chaffee dominate the tank battles and snipe infantry from afar. Additionally, the Americans got their M1s and Chaffees, and Germans got their Panzer 1s and 2s and 38(t). They are no match for the Americans, but I guess you probably guessed that. American medium tanks are great as well, with their 75 and 76 Shermans vs Panzer III and IVs. Most of the time when I drove my Pz IV, I have to flank the Shermans from the side or back in order to penetrate, while they can 2 shot me easily.
That brings me to repair and the grind of the game. Lots of people rant about this, and I agree with them 100%. Weapon usage and mods take a lot of ingame money to repair and unless you are always top 5, you won't be making much money. I guess this is the same for all the nations. When you put that into consideration, getting your next weapon seems further than it seems which makes the game more grinding and forces you to use gold.
I like WWII warfare and I continue to play the game, despite its shortcomings. I would not recommend this game to anyone unless they like that kind of warfare. To people who like WWII, give it a try at least, since it's free, see if you can handle that grind and if you pick Germany, prepare to work harder than everyone else.

text:
Sonic Adventure 2 is truly a fantastic game. The Sonic/Shadow stages are some of the best stages I've ever played in a 3D platformer, with near-perfect control and fantastic level design that flows beautifully. The movement is easy to learn but hard to master with many subtle complexities, and the variety of moves Sonic has, such as rail-grinding and light speed dashes, only enhance the enjoyable movement. There isn't a single one of these stages that I don't like. The Tails/Robotnik stages and the Knuckles/Rouge stages may not be as good as the speed stages, and have a few duds, but they're still a lot of fun and add variety to the game while still remaining a fast-paced platformer at its core. The fact that playstyles alternate during both stories helps eliminate fatigue of playing one playstyle for too long, and the fact that each character gets their own stages for a total of 31 unique levels makes the game's story mode sufficiently long without being padded or suffering from repetition.
The story itself is a lot of fun, with good pacing, memorable set pieces, fantastic characterization and solid animation for the time. Some aspects of the presentation are dated, but the game's story is still a ton of fun with many memorable moments of both cheesy hilarity, such as the infamous "faker" cutscene, and genuinely great storytelling, such as Shadow's backstory and character development.
On top of the already sufficiently lengthy story mode, Sonic Adventure 2 contains an absurd amount of replay value for a platformer, with 5 optional missions, a ranking system, and stages that are inherently designed around repeat playthroughs in exceedingly clever ways. The existence of the Chao Garden, a game-within-a-game that provides a slower-paced alternative to the fast-paced main game, while managing to be just as deep and enjoyable as said main game, is icing on the cake.
In addition to the excellent gameplay, Sonic Adventure 2 sports an excellent presentation. The game's graphics are excellent for a Dreamcast title and still look good today, and the art design is solid, if a little lacking in color variety. Additionally, the music is beyond stellar, offering different musical styles for each character that give the soundtrack great variety while also adding to the already great characterization of the story. The compositions are high-energy and memorable, perfectly fitting the levels while also making for great listening outside of the game itself. The instrumentation combines good variety with downright ♥♥♥♥♥♥ic use of the electric guitar, especially in the titular theme of the game, Live and Learn. Music is naturally a subjective medium, but you'd be hard-pressed to find a person who can't jam out to at least one track from this title, and if you're anything like me, you can jam out to nearly all of them. Technical polish is admittedly one of the weaker aspects of the game, with a few glitches being present and a handful of wonky moments that can disrupt the play experience, but when everything else is as good as it is, it’s easy to forgive the few technical hiccups that exist.
Overall, Sonic Adventure 2 is a downright phenomenal 3D platformer that I find to be just as fun now, if not more fun, then when I first played it as a kid in the early 2000s. It’s a game that I can pick up and play no matter what mood I’m in, and it almost never fails to leave me with an ear-to-ear grin. It’s a game that fills me with the kind of childlike wonder and joy that I haven’t felt since I got Super Mario Galaxy in Christmas 2007, and those kinds of games are very hard to come by. Sonic Adventure 2 comes highly recommended for any fan of Sonic the Hedgehog or 3D platformers in general.

Sonic Adventure 2 was my absolute favorite game as a kid. This was the game that made me beg my parents for a GameCube as a Christmas gift. I had hundreds of rounds played in the multiplayer (since the game kept track) and definitely put in a lot of hours. I thought this game was absolutely amazing and while I had liked Sonic prior, it was from here that I became as big a Sonic fan as I am today.
With that said, I can't recommend. It actually hurts a little to give this game a negative rating because I loved it so much a decade+ ago. Unfortunately, Sonic Adventure 2 has aged extremely poorly.
Sonic Adventure 2 follows a similar format to Sonic Adventure. You're not just racing through fast stages - you'll be playing a few other game modes.. I'll cover my thoughts on all of them.
Sonic and Shadow share the speed stages. These are what Sonic is known for. Fast platforming. Simple as that. It can be fun at times and I loved these stages as a kid. These were the ones I was constantly replaying. Playing them again.. its just not the same. The control is very slippery, the camera is awful, and the level design is horribly linear. There's not much more to say. I just don't think the stages are designed well and its not anywhere near as fun as some of the other 3d Sonic speed stages.
Knuckles and Rouge share the treasure hunting stages. These are the same as the ones from Sonic Adventure, except you have to find the emeralds in order (unless you're lucky and spot one). They're not very enjoyable. The characters control well and its fun to maneuver through the stages, but looking around for gems isn't fun. It just isn't.
Tails and Eggman share mech shooting stages. These are similar to Gamma's stages from Sonic Adventure, except you're in a much more bulky mech. You pretty much go forward and spam shots. Its really tedious actually. There's one or two levels that's a little fun, but the controls are sluggish and these stages are honestly a chore to play through.
Apart from that, there's some terrible driving stages. If you really want to compare to Sonic Adventure, think of the Twinkle Park course. The difference is the cars controlled much better in that game and it wasn't mandatory (other than about a minute or so in Sonic's stage and even that was fun as hell.)
The last thing to mention is the chao garden. There's actually a lot of depth in it. I really enjoyed it when I was younger. Its still good, but not it doesn't pull me in much anymore. Its created very well, but I don't feel like talking much about it.
All in all, the gameplay is only about 1/3rd traditional Sonic. The rest is extremely mediocre and even the speed stages aren't designed well. I really think it just comes down to quality over the years. This game has aged poorly, mostly due to the character control.
Fortunately, the music is still absolutely amazing. I can't get enough of Jun's guitar work. The instrumental tracks he creates are as "Sonic" as it gets and the songs with vocals are extremely memorable and fun to listen to. As soon as you get to the main menu, you're greeted by pure awesome.
The visuals are pretty bad. Yeah, its an older game. They could be worse, but I feel like there are some older games that look much better years later. All in all, I can't blame it because of how old the game is. Most games from this time period weren't gorgeous and it looked fine for its time.
The story is pretty decent. Actually, the story is better than a lot of the later Sonic games. I'm not saying its something wonderful, but it does a decent job at keeping interest. I also have always liked the ending quite a lot, but I won't spoil anything.
This port is okay. For the most part, everything runs fine. One minor issue though - some of the cutscenes have black bars on the side. I'm not talking about pre-rendered cutscenes. I'm talking about standard ones using the in-game graphics. The weird part is if you look at the black bars, there's a top line of pixels that show the game is still rendering behind them. Its like the bars are actually covering part of the screen. Very strange.
Some of the audio mixing wasn't perfect, but it didn't ever bother me.
I did find the game really buggy though. I don't know if this is because of the port or the game itself, but it was really frustrating at times. Also, I don't have the DLC that upgrades this to the Gamecube version.
Maybe if I had that, I would have liked the game much more but considering the multiplayer is only local, I had no real interest in buying it.
Also, there's a lot of mods. As a kid, I remember using an Action Replay to get characters into different levels but its now possible with some great PC mods. If you disagree with me and still really enjoy this game, definitely check that out.
As said before, I really loved this game when I was young. It just hasn't aged well. Playing through it was a chore to me and as soon as I finished the story, I uninstalled it with no desire to ever play it again.
If you want to play an early 3d Sonic Game, I recommend Sonic Adventure (that game is still awesome) or Sonic Heroes. Adventure is similar to this game, but I feel its aged way better. I actually enjoyed replaying it, unlike this one. And Heroes may have gotten a somewhat bad rep, but holy♥♥♥♥♥♥that game is SO much better than SA2. Traditional Sonic style and stages, good camera, non-linear branching paths, and only fast-paced gameplay. Unfortunately Heroes isn't on Steam, but its pretty good.
Sadly, I just can't recommend SA2. I love Sonic, but I can't be blinded by nostalgia. Its just aged too poorly.

TL:DR: If you're debating buying this, just buy it. Most of the cons I put are not even problems with the game, just personal opinions. It is a very smooth Early Access Game.
Usually I'm not too serious with reviews, but man...this game. Let's start out with the Pros:
PROS
-Creativity. If you can think it, you can get it to work.
-Incredibly easy to get ahold of. Vehicle building might take awhile to master, but it's a really cool concept.
-Great multiplayer. The best part is if your friend is riding a vehicle, you click on them while holding the Lift item and put the Lift down. Have fun ;)
-Lots of content, especially for an Early Access Game.
-Multiple Block Placement: Remember playing Minecraft and you had to build a huge wall? Placing each individual block was a pain. But now you can place several blocks at a time. There is a limit, but it is much nicer.
CONS
-A little glitchy in Multiplayer. Now I was playing with my buddy and he was hosting a server while in a hotel room, so that might be why.
- You can only connect one switch to one bearing at a time. If you were making a door, it really can only be one way. This is a little bit annoying as you'd have to make multiple entrances, so hopefully it will be fixed. But maybe that's just part of the game, I don't know.
- This is just a personal annoyance: you can't fly in creative mode. Sure, you can make something that flies, but it would sure help with building if your character could fly. I was trying to make a monorail system and I just gave up because I had to go on the rail and build backwards. But if this isn't something they want to add, I understand completely.
- No modes other than creative as of right now. However, it was comfirmed that they are going to add a Survival aspect so I look forward to that.
These cons aren't all that bad though. Seriously, if you're debating to buy Scrap Mechanic or not, just buy it. It is such a fun game and even though it might take a little time to master, it'll be worth it.

Hotline Miami 2 is probably one of my favourite games on Steam. If you're thinking about picking it up, I'd recommend playing the first game before this.
The game plays the same as the first one, however to me has a slower pace which can make it easier. The story is told in a confusing manner by fastforwarding and rewinding throughout the game, looking at events prior and after the events of the first game. The story itself does not focus on Jacket himself, focusing on other characters such as the Russian mob boss, and the 'Fans' that idolise Jackets murder sprees. While the story may struggle to make sense at first, it makes sense when viewed chronologically and helps the player understand the story of the first game.
'Hard Mode' can also provide a good challenge once the game has been completed, with features such as a reversed map, less ammo in weapons, less damage resistance, extra windows and extra enemies.
The long-awaited level editor has recently been added, finally entering beta mode. This means crashes and bugs can occur, but this can be expected. Viewing user created levels is currently a little tricky as workshop has still not been implemented.
Overall the game is good, there isn't much to complain about apart from the slower paced, larger maps which can prove frustrating when dying deep into the level, however this can be expected from the Hotline Miami franchises gameplay. Would recommend both games.

text:
Wrong Number has a lot to talk about:
+I remember playing HM1 and thinking nothing can top its tunes. But holy crap Wrong Number’s collection is way better.
some of these tracks were SO good I ended up following a lot of artists that were featured. Not a single track I hated, it's magical. while I'm at it, Bloodline by Scattle is fantastic, probably my favorite. I'm going to stop now before I start praising every song individually.
+sick new characters to discover. I really love the fans. ALEX AND ASH. they're so. much. fun. slash slash pew pew pew
+ Interesting story. if the story was a strong point for you in HM1 then you're gonna want Wrong Number regardless (like me). It's pretty neat, like you get to see some dear jacket and biker again if that sweetens the pot for anybody. Storytelling matured and was more elaborate, imo. The VHS aesthetic of the whole game was great.
+I mean, this COULD be a negative point as well, but I appreciated the increased player detection sensitivity in the enemy AI. It makes luring enemies around corners and walls a lot faster.
-lame ending (ending spoilers) I think this is justified... It really sucks seeing your faves die, right? At least it fits with the title screen theme?
-no masks! UGHHHH!!!! I absolutely loved the mask system in the first game! It let you work out your favorite play style for the best expereince or variety. Instead in HM2, other than like, 3 or 4 skill variations (that need to be unlocked...) for the few characters that have them is all you get! (♥♥♥♥ you, dodge/roll). You just have to suck it up when you're playing as skill-less characters.
-Dogs/psychos freak tf out near open doors. it becomes really frustrating to kill them because their leaps are so broken you can barely hit them sometimes. As if it skips animation frames or something so you can't predict the attack. Also I've had dogs leap through walls to kill me?
-rooms are far too open and large, level design isn’t what it used to be. This becomes a nightmare on hard mode in my next point. There are too many offscreen kills, watched a lot of playthroughs just to figure out where they're coming from. It becomes sooo annoying and average players like myself will just end up luring by corners which is a really slow and tedious play style.
-obviously favors ranged weapons and nerfed melee playing styles ... that’s a big deal for me since I’m not good with guns. See: Melee weapon swings have weird timing now. It feels so off compared to the first game. A lot of times it's plain luck that you hit an enemy. Sometimes they charge at you and you die 'cause your swing just??? Misses???? Doesn't feel smooth and swift like in HM1. Another kick in the nuts for melee lovers: your weapon throws will be awful because they don’t go far and you can’t retrieve it since it just barely hit your target.
-oh my gooood hard mode, what the hell. idk if I should complain about this since it's optional, but as a completionist I need to get it done. Hard mode has me clawing my eyes out. Gun Hell. All these windows make slower strategies impossible. Sometimes I wonder if the Dennaton duo can even play these levels in less than an hour
I still had tons of fun playing this, it's just that I became frustrated much more easily because there is a huge difficulty jump compared to the first game. Levels can’t be handled quickly anymore.I talked about how I'd be willing to pay more in my HM review but I dunno about this one. Obviously if you loooooooved the first game like I did in all aspects then you don't want to miss out on this one! Just go buy it. It has a lot to offer, just differently. If you weren't enamored with HM1's gameplay style and don't really care the characters or story, then yeah, give it some thought because I can't say Wrong Number is an improvement in those ways. It’s hard for me to recommend to just anybody. It terms of gameplay and time spent having fun vs. time spent playing angrily, it unfortunately feels like a clunky downgrade from the original.
Still recommending it though because it's fast bloody fun no matter how you look at it.
everybody should totally give the soundtrack a listen regardless tho. At least that's something good we can all agree on.

Quite a long time ago (like in the Commodore age) my parents gave me this book with rather difficult chess puzzles and tutorials – so I wouldn’t waste my life away on them silly video games. Well, it finally paid off!
Warhammer 40K: Regicide is heavily based on chess but offers a variety of chance based skills and attack options after every regular move. And this extension works very well. The single-player campaigns alone make it worth your while, since they offer hours and hours of different chess problems (with the extended rules set).
The competitive multiplayer is fine too, but it does require more patience than regular online chess. Matches in Regicide tend to take even longer, partly because of the fancy move and kill animations. Also expect the ultra violence and over the top tone of any other WH40K video game, which is a good thing. Just by looks and style this game fits right into some niche between Dawn of War and Space Marine. So, yeah, it’s awesome too!

Overall its a decent game, and as much as i like it, i'm not going to recommend it.
Game looks nice, plays smoothly, with a couple of "glitches" here and there, wich i think is just somewhat sloppy for a game that essentially is quite appealing. I like the idea of chess+warhammer, and you get this blend that works really well, with one aspect that pretty much ruins the whole game for me.
Every action you perform is subject to chance, so in short you can take your strategy, and flush it down the box, because nothing is certain to the point of becoming entirely unpredictable. Its not uncommon to play two rounds, perform 6 actions, fail at performing every single one, while building up some real world aggravation everytime it happens.
I'm not this incompetent in real life, so why does this game let me play like a blubbering idiot? Can you imagine failing at least 1/3 of everything you do in life? Go ahead, grab a glass of milk, i dare you, go see what happens.
Psychologically, it just doesn't work. Winning is a relief, and losing is a pity, neither are satisfying because its not really in your hands. Its just this one little element from the tabletop i think that should have been left out, or within (severe) limitation.
They should take this game, fix it, expand it, and re-publish it, because there is something really cool there, but for now its only provoking potential homocidal tendencies wich i think are never good and should be avoided at all times unless you have low selfesteem issues because then it simply wouldn't matter and its all the same to you.
But really, this could have been so much more and better, and i dont think i will be spending a whole lot time on a game that's quite discouraging.

Not really much to say here that I haven't already said in my

).
That said, I'll summarise the problems I had (as of release day).
The controls are incredibly unresponsive (on keyboard, didn't test a controller). Several tutorial levels are near impossible to start, and the end screen upon completion of a tutorial level does not close upon pressing space like the game says, forcing you to ALT+F4 out of it.
The loadout screen is fairly unintuitive in terms of how to close it, you need to close any active menus before you can back out which isn't obvious at first. Also, the game doesn't tell you that right click closes any active menus.
As a minor complaint, the mouse sensitivity settings don't seem to change much (if anything) and the rotation feels way too sensitive to me as I usually play games with a fairly low sensitivity, leading to a lot of over rotates.
With all of these control issues, I can't recommend the game in its current state. It has an interesting premise, and the match I played was fun, but the inability to close menus hits even after playing a match; you have to ALT+F4 and relaunch the game after every match you play.
It's entirely possible I'm part of a minority with these issues, and it's entirely possible these issues don't exist on a controller, but reading the other reviews for this game only emphasises the point that something is currently broken control wise, for both keyboards AND controllers alike.
When these problems get fixed, I'll come back to the game and give it another look. If they have been fixed then this review will be positive (unless a new major issue rears it's head, but that's unlikely).
If the premise of the game interests you and you don't mind buying into a product that has a chance of barely functioning, then pick this game up. Otherwise, wait a few weeks for some patches to roll out and for the game breaking issues mentioned here to be fixed (which the dev's have informed me they are looking into).

Updating my review because it's been a long time since the issues have been fixed and wanted my review to reflect the experience I've had with the changes.
Performance: Constant 60fps during gameplay with everything on high and no black bars. I have a GTX 970 and a Xeon E3 1230 V2.
Gameplay: 8/10
- Very satisfying and rewarding gameplay.
- If you like resident evil 4, you will love this game. It almost feels like a sequel to RE4, which isn't a bad thing.
- Some refinements have been made to the gameplay and mechanics over 4 and overall I find it much better. I like the new weapons, upgrade system, sneaking and cover mechanics, knifing, matches, etc. Feels like a mix of RE4 and RE 1 Remaster.
Graphics: 7/10
- Not as great as it could be, looks like a previous gen PS3 game. I guess they were limited by the last gen engine they used.
- That said the environments are varied and interesting, dark and grimey, just what you would expect in a survival horror game.
- The bosses are really cool too. Some people don't find them scary, but there were a few that creeped me out.
Story: 5/10
- Very confusing and hard to follow. I don't like how it's fragmented and all over the place. I've played the game a few times and there is still things I don't understand.
- The game got its inspiration from Inception, Matrix, and Shutter Island, so you can imagine what they were going for.
- I would have liked for the world to feel more connected, but you just go from one seemingly unconnected area to the next, there's no flow from one area to another. It broke the game up too much for me with each level not feeling connected to the last, but that's probably a personal preference.
Overall: 8/10
- Very good game overall, especially if you are a Resident Evil/Silent Hill/Survival horror game fan, it blends a lot of elements from these games together.
- The gameplay is very fun and rewarding, especially sneaking up on enemies and killing them silently to conserve ammo. There are many ways to play and strategies you can take.
- The story is a mess so what really motivated me to continue was the gameplay, The game was just very fun, story was really just an afterthought for me. If they can develop a better story for a sequel and iron out some of the issues with this game, they will have something great.
- The game is also very replayable, just like RE4. There's tons of challenges you can do once you complete the game, with other modes unlocking.

I'm having a little trouble with this game really...
The more I play it, I find the less I am enjoying it.
Don't get me wrong it's a good game and I am really trying to enjoy it but there are things that have been going on since before it was released that are still going on now, graphical glitches, movement glitches etc.
I like how the "Special Infected" ; ) cause you to change tactics and work together and I like how it is melee focused and quite violent, it's cathartic to literally smash an enemies head in sometimes but the game is horribly imbalanced and sometimes your whole group can unload all they have on an enemy for two minutes and that enemy will simply activate id softwares old god mode cheat and eventually wear you all down and kill you...
The graphics are also quite intensive and considering they aren't really that pretty it makes me wonder what the game is doing to my system.
It tries to paint a picture of a world ending and a gloomy end-time image painted with greens, browns and greys given a horrible - literally - lighting system just makes the game ugly, and whilst we're on the subject of light, this game has the worst fire effects in the history of video games.
Sound wise it is quite unique but it loses Left 4 Deads urgency in the sound effects and musical area and quite often the warning effects and music can be drowned out by your players yapping on or fighting.
Overall the game is trying to open up a new genre that has been enjoying quite a boom of late, the first person co-op chaos shooter, L4D, Alone in the Dark, this, Orion Prelude... The only problem is this game just misses the mark a little bit, there is no sprint function and your character moves quite slowly and the maps are sprawling and open-ended, which would normally be a good thing but it just means it takes ages to get anywhere...
I have to still give this game a recommendation however because when it really bears down to it it is still a lot of fun, it could just be a lot better.
But the developers seem to be working with what the community are saying so here hoping that in the future a lot of the issues I have been experiencing will be fixed... For now however I will continue on with Left 4 Dead 2 and pay occaisonal visits to grimtown to see how it is getting on...

Warhammer: End Times – Vermintide is a first person action game developed and published by Fatshark who have brought us a few notable titles to Steam over the years such as Bloodsports.TV and War of the Roses. The game was released on PC in October 2015 but is due to be released on PS4 and Xbox One in early 2016.
The game play is very similar to that of Left 4 Dead. You team up with three other players to battle through stages taking on rodent like creatures, the Skaven. There is also an element of character progression in the terms of equipment. At the end of each stage you get a reward of dice to roll, the better you roll, the higher quality item you get.  Each character has its designated role within the group of playable characters. There is a good mix of range damage dealers, melee and tank characters.  The combat melee system is really well put together, the blocking system in this game is very key to playing a melee character correctly as you will just take too much damage to be beneficial to your party. The mage class does a ton of damage, but also runs the risk of dealing damage to herself through overpowering her magic. I particularly liked the mage class as there is a pretty high skill ceiling between playing the character OK and playing it really really well.  You can play the game single player with bots, but you are going to get the most enjoyment out of playing it in a group of four.
The visuals in Vermintide are really good. They capture the Warhammer feel and atmosphere perfectly. The animations of all the characters are nicely put together with no weird movement cycles or attack animations. The lighting is extremely well done too as you delve deep into dark parts of the city. There is a loosely connected narrator to the game as well; the narration is done in real time as you reach certain locations on the stage, and this also provokes a reaction out of the party members, each character will react differently to what is happening. I thought this was a nice little addition that breaks up the repetitiveness nature of the game.
Each stage has a variety of different difficulties to play on, the higher the difficulty you play, the better chance you have to get improved loot at the end of a successful run. You can jump straight into doing “Normal” runs, but you will find yourself being severely overwhelmed due to your equipment not being up to par, once you get yourself a decent set of gear you can start jumping into the normal runs and then work your way up from there into the harder difficulties.
The stages are all nicely designed. It reminds me so much of Left 4 Dead with the layouts and how there is different styles of Skaven enemies to take on. Throughout the stages you will also have the chance to find treasure chests which also can reward you with additional dice for the end of the level, as well as health potions or stat potions.
At the moment I have been playing Vermintide for just over five hours; I can see myself dipping in and out of the game for a few reasons which I will go on next, but there is a good level of replay ability here. The loot factor being the main element that will keep people coming back; everyone loves getting loot and you will get plenty in this game. The other key factor is the multiplayer/team based, if you can find yourself a group of friends to run stages with, you will find yourself being sucked into this game for hours at a time.
Now, onto the technical issues. First of all, the performance on Vermintide is pretty poor, even when playing on SLI 970s I wasn’t able to push out 4k graphics without sacrificing frame drops. I was happy to drop my resolution down to 1440 whilst also keeping settings on max. The major technical issue I ran into would be random crashes.  Every two runs I did, I would get at least 1 crash throughout, and sadly if you crash, you can’t reload your game and jump straight into the last party. This became very annoying and to the point where I don’t see myself playing this game too much in long stints, I’ll jump in for a run or two here and there, but nothing more than that.
To sum up, Vermintide is a very good game in thought, and when it works it is absolutely awesome. I really hope they manage to fix the random crashes because this game would be right up my ally. The fact the game has such stellar gameplay which reminds people of an even better game, Left 4 Dead, will do this game huge favours. The game is retailing for £22, 99 on Steam and that is almost as low as it’s been since it was released. I will recommend this game with the premise you get it when on sale, purely because of the technical problems.  If you are lucky enough to get by without having crashes, Vermintide is an awesome game that will give you hours and hours of content.

Recommended, it's a quick, well-executed, arcade-like experience that is quite difficult, but not impossible. It's not cheap difficulty, when you lose, you know you made a mistake, not that you were cheated out by RNG or something. This is a very lighthearted free-running type of game very similar to something like Subway Surfers. There are 18 levels here of varying difficulty; from Normal Geon to Anti-Boson X. I have spent 4 hours collecting achievements (beating the game) and the rest of my time shooting for top 1000 (then 500) scores on each level.
I played the free version before this, but the Dark and Anti versions of each particle were a pleasant new feature. They are NOT retools or reskins of one another.  Each stage usually retains the same core structure (gravitron likes moving/falling platforms, Y boson is a big fan of electric beams, etc.) but otherwise each level is fresh and unique.
Players with slow reaction times WILL have trouble with the later levels. This game gets pretty darn rediculous, especially once you take on the Anti particles. Anti Gravitron had me stuck for a good 30 minutes (1/8 of the time I was playing).
This is a very good game in my opinion. While it may not be a genre-definer like Super Meat Boy or a masterfully crafted experience like Limbo, it's nice for good quick fun, a coffee break or a reflex test.

Well it's like Battle Chess from years ago except 40k and it is not like it :D. It can be played campaign or skirmish (AI or human player).
The campaign which can be tricky depending on difficulty, uses pre-arranged boards (some pieces missing and placed in strange starting positions) with obstacles and a generic space marine vs orc storyline.
In skirmish you can play classic mode which is chess or you can play regicide mode which adds some special abilities to your pieces that can be frustrating if you're expecting a clean chess game. Took me around 2 hours to utilize these abilities more wisely and stop getting stomped so hard. Important lesson: If you are playing marines, be aware that orks have a nasty assault ability that allows them to dish out heafty damage if adjecent to your piece. In many cases I found it wiser to hang back and just pepper them with bolters (snap shot) unless they opened themselves up to stupidity and checkmate. More replayability if you are really into chess and see yourself playing more games against randoms and skirmish AI.
If you dislike such games and are just looking for a 40k title, I'd ignore this game or wait till a sale. I consider myself not that grand a chess player but I love 40k and I do enjoy chess so I give it a 7/10. Would give it higher if it had different factions other than just orcs and space marines but it does the trick when the craving hits.
(Edit: It is worth noting that the different chapters/orc clans have different stats in regicide mode.)
It's awesome!

For the sale price on steam of $4.99, this game is fantastic.

Antispehere is a skill-based competitive twin-stick shooter in which you go against 1 opponent with an addictive ranked system very similar to Hearthstone. My only issue is that the tutorials don't really give you an idea of the game and the best way to learn is to play casual mode. The playerbase is currently very small, although to be fair the game came out not even 24 hours ago from when this review is posted.
If you've ever played Lethal League then this game is quite similar in that you interact with the ball to eliminate the other player. The only difference is that instead of picking a character with set qualities, your "sphere" is customisable in appearance and in abilities. You can use these abilities to manipulate the ball and the opponent to eliminate them.
The game is very pleasing to look at and has a good enough soundtrack to not annoy you but won't stand out particularly either.
This game could absolutely shine with a larger playerbase. This would motivate the devs to put a lot more into this game and make it stand out as a very unique competitive experience. At it's current price it is absolutely worth it. I recommend using a controller!

I'm going to write a first impression for the moment, likely to update once I have beaten the game.
Now, to start with, my machine can only really run this game on lower settings. 720p, low shadows, AA off. I cannot attest for the look of the game, I do not care about the look, so long as it is competent and I feel it is. I really wish I could play with shadows on high, because the lighting in this game is phenominal. The only thing I feel is off is the aspect ratio, which is a forced 21:9 and apparently on some resolution settings you get an odd full black box around the screen. I don't get this playing on 720p, but I have seen some experience it. But so far the atmosphere has been enough to keep the odd aspect ratio from really bothering me.
And yes, the game runs at a locked 30 FPS (I'm just barely achieving that consistently, so no complaints there). Apparently you can unlock it to 60, where they promise to fix any issue with that. But any issues involving a fully-unlocked FPS specifically will not be tended to, unfortunately.
In terms of gameplay, it works rather well. I mostly played with a controller, but I tried out the keyboard and it works just fine as far as I can tell. You can rebind keys and even assign an action to multiple keys. The controller has a few predetermined settings, you can't totally change which button does what, but the setup works just fine.
Enemies seem somewhat intelligent, I had one get caught on a fence for some-odd reason, but that was the only instance where the AI seemed poor. There's some stealth elements, because getting overwhelmed or running into traps is the easiest way to get killed. It works for what it is, hide under a bed, in a closet, or just crouch-walk to your next destination, hoping not to get seen. Stealth kills are also a thing, which is great because that saves you on a lot of ammo. There are some parts in the game, however, that force you into combat. So far those sections tend to partner you up with someone, but only if the enemies are coming in large waves.
The weapons in this game seem really damn satisfying though. You can blow off chunks of the zombie-enemy-things, even with the starting pistol. There's a crossbow in the game, and, without giving too much away, it's good. Very good.
As for the story, well, it's pretty nuts. I can't say if it's really good or bad because I'm not at a point where any real explanation has popped up. But it's engaging and interesting to say the least. I can't say it's terribly frightening, though I've played enough survival horror games to build up an immunity to most scares. I am looking forward to playing more, even if it's due to my own morbid curiosity.
Overall, it's a competent title. I'm enjoying it for what it is. It's clear that Shinji Mikami hasn't given up his idea for survival horror, as you can see hints of some of the Resident Evil games in there. Specifically, RE1 and 4. I'm sorry to hear that others have had issues, but I, personally, have not. If you are intruiged by a horror atmosphere and don't mind a couple of oddball, but mostly harmless game design decisions, I'd say this is a good one. If you're hesitant, I wouldn't blame you for waiting for a sale or a patch of some description. I plan on updating this when I get around to actually beating the title, so my opinion may change. We'll see!

Ignore the negative reviews, a lot complain about grinding and saying about the little content in terms of raiding etc, but it is early access and the grinding is the same as any other MMORPG, World of Warcraft is a game of grinding, but the difference with this game and any other MMORPG I have played is that you finish most quests and you can click the finished quest in your quest log and turn it in and accept the new one, you do not have to run from A to B to A to B, you just move on with the quests, not only that, most grinding in MMORPG requires you to get the same mobs as others and you only have a few to hunt, mean while you struggle to get the kill in before anyone else or you waste time just standing around waiting for respawns, in this game the respawns are almost instant with nearly all mobs, as well as this game promotes team work by letting everyone who attacks the mob get the kill, no waiting around, no griefing, just fun team work with strangers or friends.
Ignoring the fact that most people complain about a grind and I have just explained why that is a stupid reason to give this a negative review(as in may as well just say all MMORPGs are bad if grinding is an issue, which again, it is less of an issue in this game) you also have the beautiful sights on this game, it is so easy on the eyes, the animations are great, the emotions in the faces of the characters are great(something I have never seen in any other MMORPG)
Will add, this game lets you buy stuff, you can buy the guardian gear but it is terrible in stats up to level 4 or so, so it isn't pay to win, the mounts are hardly amazing, the most you get from using money in this game is just stuff like getting potions are easier or not waiting on crafting(which isn't a big deal as you craft items, wait for it to be crafted while you quest).
I have 20 hours in this game so far, I put money into the game about 5 hours in and haven't put anymore in since, I can't recommend this game enough, free to play, great game, no monthly subs, no massive load screens or downloads, instant jump in and play, if you do buy a pack then great, support the game, it is a great game and it costs so little(mostly vanity stuff if you are paying)
The updates to come in the game look amazing and will get rid of all the "no content" rubbish, again it is early access, it is expected to lack stuff, but they are adding plenty and have set their long term goals and they are amazing, once just a few of these goals are in the game, it will have features that no other MMORPG I have played has ever had.
Lastly, you can go from your PC to your phone instantly, the phone version is easy to play, great controls and literally the exact same game as this one on steam.

I mean, the comments that the questgivers can make, and often the other players, cracks me up almost the entire time I'm playing. It has a bit of Allen Wake-ish feel to it, rather than Outcast or whatever like that. Meaning more mysticism than pure "horror". This is a good thing, for me. It is very good in terms of graphics, including the gory stuff.  It has style. The style, I actually could use, if my idea of a game takes a hold somewhere. Maybe I will send the idea to Bethsoft...
The bad thing is... It's trying to bee too cinematic. For that purpose there are black lines at the bottom and at the top of the screen (supposedly 'cause of that) and camera is very close (gonzo style). Both of that limit the FOV, which makes gameplay... Uncomfortable. It could also use a "quest guiding system", like to show you general destination for your current objective, but that's optional. I also noticed that AI is not that smart, in 1st chapter there were no keys for the door on 1st try (saw them after I died and checkpoint got reloaded) and some minor game-design "issues", which do not make the game worse by themselves, but do spoil the picture further.
Either way, I am dropping it for now. I hope, that there will be some kind of a patch or a mode to zoom out the camera (and better yet - remove the black lines) in near future. Preferably an official patch. And now, console options are not ok for this, because they make it worse.
I am not recommending it, but if a patch is released - I'll play it further and update the review. Otherwise, I guess I'll stick with some videos of the walkthrough or something.

While the story may struggle to make sense at first, it makes sense when viewed chronologically and helps the player understand the story of the first game.
'Hard Mode' can also provide a good challenge once the game has been completed, with features such as a reversed map, less ammo in weapons, less damage resistance, extra windows and extra enemies.
The long-awaited level editor has recently been added, finally entering beta mode. This means crashes and bugs can occur, but this can be expected. Viewing user created levels is currently a little tricky as workshop has still not been implemented.
Overall the game is good, there isn't much to complain about apart from the slower paced, larger maps which can prove frustrating when dying deep into the level, however this can be expected from the Hotline Miami franchises gameplay. Would recommend both games.

Dofus was the brainchild of Ankama, a unique and very imaginative strategy based MMO, y'know with the final fantasy tactics kind of gameplay. It featured a pretty huge world with unique enemies on nearly every zone and map, with many freaking dungeons to enter as a team of unique races, each with their own set of abilities that all contribute to your chances of clearing these dungeons.
Wakfu is supposed to be the sequel MMO to the world of Dofus, the world is flooded because of Ogrest, an ogre who swallowed a dofus, which in dofus, was the most rare and expensive thing in the world of twelve.
You can play 14 classes, same as in Dofus, each race has been graphically updated or changed a little.
What wakfu did right is that it tried to create a world that was entirely run by its players, environments and even the 4 divided nations are still entirely run by players, with its own governors, vice governors, treasurer, eco protector, guards, soldiers, activity chiefs you name it. From the tree's to the monsters its all provided by the player themselves.
which is also exactly why its greatest and most unique feature is also its worst.
Imagine the average lazy♥♥♥♥♥MMO player destroying an entire ecosystem you as a player worked really hard to preserve within an hour? it actually costs money from the treasury (who you pay your taxes to) to patch up, annoying right?
imagine an item on the market you want with incredibly high taxes to go with it.
better vote for a different governor next time, what's that? You didn't know you could? Well you can!
Every week or month (can't remember) there's elections for a new governor, even you can become one. With enough votes you'll win and you can put your own friends in charge of handling various government jobs in your nation.
you can even declare WAR on the other nations and allow your nation's people to attack visitors from the other nations on sight.
with this system though it's easily abused by guilds and stuff funneling their votes into a guild master or whatever, which is too bad. Combat is a little more fast paced which I find sad really. Bosses can be very fun to fight in a grup though.
The classes themselves feel a little like dumbed down versions of their Dofus ancestors, you'll only be using maybe 6 or so abilities through your entire playthrough.
It's still worth checking out as its free to play, and I still do recommend you play it. It's artstyle is incredibly nice.

A cautionary tale in allowing business decisions dictate what is "fun". This is not a recommendation, this is a warning to stay away from this atrocious butchered dross at all costs. A pitiful attempt at trying to appeal to a number of core FPS demographis its style, tone and gameplay, simply can't hope to overlap. While at the same time both looking and running terribly on the very low-end PCs of the original userbase it appealed to, (how you can make blocky voxel graphics look even *worse* than the beta is a remarkable feat in itself)
This is of course not the Ace of Spades people heard of and discussed wildly in indie-circles, no sir, this is a man's Ace of Spades, made by Jaqex, (your friendly neighborhood developer/publicher of RuneScape Browser MMO fame) and it shows! By which I mean it's so utterly bland and generic, desperately hacking together pieces of other and better games and popcultural references in order to appeal to as many demographics at once. While failing to satisfy anyone (besides maybe falling-sand game enthusiasts) A game designed by committee... Of marketers and executives.
The potential for fun is in there somewhere, but it's hampered by its schizophrenic tone and often completely contradictionary game mechanics. Compounded by a uncaring to downright malicious development team, (Though I say that loosely, more likely that the developers hands are thouroughly tied in the matter and whatever the bossman says goes.)
This isn't saying much of course, - I've always held that Ace of Spades was to modern FPSs what a cardboard cigar is to a terminal nicotine addict, but it was accessible, simple and would run on my intermittedly spotty connection without a care in the world and if you got nothing else, it was worth wasting a few hours on. - This "fast paced reimagining" at least lives up to its new ideals, after 17 minutes I was so thouroughly sick of it I think I'll never boot it up again.
Thankfully the community picked up the pieces... Not that Jaqex would ever admit it. Cowards.
2 out of 10,  "Please keep your executives out of the development and community management processes next time."

After 100 hours in Dirt Rally and another 40 in Dirt 4 I feel like I am finally able to give a good comparison of both games while also reviewing Dirt 4. This review will be comprised of 5 categories of which "Handling and Realism" is the most important for me at least.
It is immediately clear that Dirt 4 is less focused than Dirt Rallye being a sequel to Dirt 3 rather than Dirt Rally but this does not mean Dirt 4 is less realistic than Dirt Rally.
On the contrary cars have more weight and are not as floaty as in Dirt Rally. There is no more pogo jumping over bumps and driving techniques like lifting/breaking before jumps are actually useful. In general weight transfer is much better in Dirt 4 than in Dirt Rally lockups are more present than in Dirt Rally encouraging good driving and on-throttle braking.
Grip levels are quite high in places probably because of the added car weight at least on gravel stages. On tarmac Dirt 4 is way better than Dirt Rally still not very good since there is no tire flex but cars do not seem to drive on rails grip is significantly lowered compared to Dirt Rally and cars are more lively.
The real issue Dirt 4 seems to have is on-throttle traction. In general cars have to much traction especially when driving RWD cars on-throttle oversteer is not as progressive as you would expect on a gravel road and traction breaks very sudden thus playing with the gas is not as effective in creating oversteer as it should be making RWD cars quite boring and stale compared to AWD and FWD cars. Weather does not affect handling too much on gravel and tarmac which is a bit of a shame since it seems like there are tools in place for simulating aquaplaning. On snow weather has no affect on handling whatsoever. While both games have deforming snow banks in Sweden leaning still does not really work since the snow banks in both games just feel like guard rails with some padding attached to them more deformation would be better. Damage models are great and internal damage seems to occur more often than in Dirt Rally but the damage model is far from realistic and just not punishing enough a hardcore mode would be very much appriciated since all the necessary tools seem to be in place.
FFB hasn't much changed since Dirt Rally it still requres a lot of tweaking and is missing many effects and settings other sims like iRacing, Assetto Corsa and RaceRoom have.
Nonetheless Dirt 4 has a more realistic driving experience than Dirt Rallye.
Codemasters has put a lot of effort into highlighting the procedural track generation tool of Dirt 4. While it is an intriguing idea to have countless tracks and endless content the execution lacks variety. It seems as if the tool is combining certain premade sections procedually. The issue could be fixed if codemasters creates
more sections the algorithm can choose from. Also a track editor where users could make their own track sections and tracks would help mitigate repetition and prolong the games lifecycle. Also rally stages are quite short compared to their real life counterparts which can exceed 40km more than twice the length of Dirt 4's longest stages. Codemasters is keen to make Rally stages longer but claims that the Ego engine cant handle stages longer than ~18km. Still repetition is way smaller than in Dirt Rally which has maybe 20 hours worth of original content. The selection of locations is limited due to licensing but diverse enough. Rallycross has more tracks and is more fleshed out than in Dirt Rally while retaining the official FIA branding and Landrush is a nice addition to the game while not necessarily needed.
The car selection lacks a bit. While most of the really important rallye cars are in the game some classes like WRC are missing completely due to licensing issues making R5 the fastest available class in the game for rallying. Rallyecross on the other hand has all cars you can really wish for since Codemasters hold the license for the FIA World Rallycross Championship.
Overall the graphics haven't improved much since Dirt Rally. While lighting and effects have improved the overall looks of the game are hindered by the quite repetitive stages. Also variation is very big while sometimes really beautiful e.g. a stage after some rain Dirt 4 can come across really stale looking. Still the game does not look bad the engine just needs a  refresh.
Like the graphics Dirt 4's sound didn't really improve since Dirt Rally. Sounds are generally informative but not much more also Dirt 4 has some layering issues and you probably need some adjusting to get a good mix. The co-driver is really good considering the tracks are procedually generated but bad camber call-outs would be appreciated. Really nothing bad but nothing special either.
While Dirt 4 may not be a perfect game in any sense, it improves upon Dirt Rally and still delivers a good challange. Many of the general directions are IMHO correct. Going to procedually generated stages is the way to go in the future but still needs a lot improvement and polish to really become what it is intended to be. Also a better damage system and further evolution of the handling would be much appreciated but still the basics are done right so if you were on the fence buying this game give it a try.

I really don't know how to rate this game. I really love it for so many things, but at the same time it does so many things wrong that you just want to throw it in the bin.
Negative:
- Enemy AI on rally stages is so badly written, it hurts. The enemies aren't even a challenge until you crank the difficulty up to at least "tough" and even then the AI does differently well at different locations and in different classes. In NR4 I gained 1 minute and 20 seconds in ONE 4 mile stage in Michigan without the enemies really posing a thread to me. Meanwhile in spain I can't win a single stage. It always feels like the game cheeses you.
- The enemy AI does amazing on straights and light corners, as soon as the stages become difficult and tight you will take time out of them like they are amateur drivers.
- As soon as you get up to speed in fast parts of the stages, your co driver will become utterly confused and tell you about the upcoming "right 2 crest" while you are already off the track avoiding trees. This is especially bad in Australia.
- Everything looks the same. The same corners over and over again. After a while you don't even need your co driver anymore, because you know what's gonna come up anyway. On one stage in Australia, I counted the same left 3 corner with the big tree inside 5 times....
I'd rather drive on quality stages multiple times (like in Dirt 2), then on these half♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ generic ones.
- Your car becomes a tank as soon as you upgrade all the parts to A.
- Stadium trucks feel totally out of place. It's so little content opposed to all the rallying you do and it's only 3 tracks iirc. Why does it get a whole entire championship if it only takes you like an hour to complete. You can feel that it's unfinished.
- "Clean stages" are counted unconsistently. I can cut through grass and literally ignore the corner and still be "clean" as long as I don't damage my car. Meanwhile hitting a bit of snow with your rear bumper in sweden won't be counted as clean.
- Overall satisfying sponsors is never really a challenge.
Positive:
- Rallycross is a lot of fun and probably the most well made part of the game. Enemy AI is still pretty beatable even on brutal, but a good challenge. Tracks have the most variety. Sadly you only spend like 2 races in the super 1600 and then you already get into faster cars.
- Game looks ok. Nothing ground breaking, but it's ok.
- There is a good variety of cars in most classes. Some are lacking like the WRC class, with only 3 available cars, but overall I can't complain
- Sound design is great. The Subaru boxer engines rumble, the Audi 5 cylinder screams, the turbo's flutter like they should and the anti lag sings the song of his people. Well done!
Overall I just can't give this game a good rating. I would probably give it a 5/10. It saddens me to see such great potential wasted. It feels like the Dirt series takes 2 steps forward but 4 back each time they release a new game. Playing against the AI in rally stages is frustrating, because it either can't keep up or it will deminish you where it shouldn't be possible. The game feels repetetive already after a short while. There isn't enough content to keep you invested. Even rallycross which is the least repetetive makes you lust for more variety.

I bought this game a long time ago when I saw it on sale for next-to-nothing.  I was really shocked at the quality in this super-budget title!
In the game you play a female protagonist in her linear adventure in a floating city. She is led through the bowels of the city's utility systems by a male co-worker who speaks in her earpiece.  He is watching most everything you do via the many security cameras in the city.  The exchanges are quite humorous now and then (and one time VERY humorous!).  The city is under attack from a villianess-of-the-week and her many rent-a-thugs.
The game has controls similar to the Tomb Raider reboot although not quite as polished.  It also has Batman Arkham Assylum Detective vision for solving some simple puzzles.  The game also throws in some Half-Life 2 styled electricity and water puzzles.
The thing that impressed me the most in this game are the water physics.  If the developer is reading this, my hat is off to you my friend.  The water physics are -=AMAZING=-!  The best I have seen in ANY videogame!
Gun combat is not great but passable.  Fortunately this little missy is very tough and can take quite a few hits.  Combat in flooded rooms adds a new dimension as enemies are difficult to see on the other side of the water's surface.  I was frequently diving and surfacing to keep up with the enemies as they appeared above and below the water-line.
I have not finished the game but I believe I am very close.  It is a short game, maybe 8 hours.  I read in the forums the final boss fight is a pain.
PROS:
+ -=Excellent=- value for your money.
+ Novel gunplay situations in flooded areas.
+ Varied gameplay from platforming to combat to environmental puzzles.
+ THE FREAKING WATER PHYSICS!  Holy crap it is amazing!!
+ Occasionally amusing banter between the main characters
+ Documents and objects to collect along the way if you are into that.
+ Graphics are quite good for a budget title.
CONS:
- Platforming is a little rough around the edges.  Character animations are a little stiff at times.
- Environments can get a little samey as you make your way through the maintinence chambers under the city (where most of the game takes place).
- While the main character looks nice, some of the other character models do not look so good.
- Some of the environmental (Half Life 2 style) puzzles will test your patience.  These just aren't as fun as they were in the mid-2000's.
The game is not perfect, but the value you get for the price is outstanding.  It would be worth a go at twice the asking price.  If you enjoyed the Tomb Raider reboot, this game is a no-brainer!

Too many people are judging this game on its optimization... Or lack there of in this case. Is the game perfect? Absolutely not! But, does that make it a bad game? Far from it! One thing this game nails is its atmosphere. The Evil Within has a very dark and gloomy tone to its environment and it really gives off the sensation that each room you walk into holds something very sinister within it. The art style of the game is also rather impressive and adds greatly to the overall tone of the game... The character models however do not share the same style. While the creatures of The Evil Within look particularly twisted and gruesome, the character models of the human characters are unfortunately rather bland. The voice acting is serviceable but not impressive. I cannot make a full opinion of the story because at the time of this review, I am 7 hours into the game but from what I have played so far, the story plays heavily on the psychological horror aspect of the game, causing players to question what's real and what isn't.
My feelings about the gameplay of The Evil Within are mostly positive but there is certainly room for improvement. The gunplay feels good and the lack of ammunition and resources is a very welcome return from what players have had to endure with other recent so called "Survival Horror" games. The Evil Within is unforgiving with the amount of items that you can find in this world of nightmares and you will find yourself having to count your ammo, sneak past enemies and use quick thinking along with using the environment itself in order to survive. The user interface and character movements however are rather clunky and can land you into some serious trouble at times... One thing inparticular I found to be odd is the weapons menu is opened by clicking the right analog stick on an Xbox 360 controller. There have been many occasions where I have shot at an enemy and accidently opened the weapons menu because I clenched the controller when I fired.
Overall, The Evil Within has its share of problems that need ironing out and the lack of optimization for the PC version is inexcusable. But, The Evil Within is definitely a game that needs to be experienced by Survival Horror fans and can help bring the genre back to being something to be feared instead of staying the laughing stock it is now for big budget Horror games.
