Wrong Number has a lot to talk about:
+I remember playing HM1 and thinking nothing can top its tunes. But holy crap Wrong Number’s collection is way better.
some of these tracks were SO good I ended up following a lot of artists that were featured. Not a single track I hated, it's magical. while I'm at it, Bloodline by Scattle is fantastic, probably my favorite. I'm going to stop now before I start praising every song individually.
+sick new characters to discover. I really love the fans. ALEX AND ASH. they're so. much. fun. slash slash pew pew pew
+ Interesting story. if the story was a strong point for you in HM1 then you're gonna want Wrong Number regardless (like me). It's pretty neat, like you get to see some dear jacket and biker again if that sweetens the pot for anybody. Storytelling matured and was more elaborate, imo. The VHS aesthetic of the whole game was great.
+I mean, this COULD be a negative point as well, but I appreciated the increased player detection sensitivity in the enemy AI. It makes luring enemies around corners and walls a lot faster.
-lame ending (ending spoilers) I think this is justified... It really sucks seeing your faves die, right? At least it fits with the title screen theme?
-no masks! UGHHHH!!!! I absolutely loved the mask system in the first game! It let you work out your favorite play style for the best expereince or variety. Instead in HM2, other than like, 3 or 4 skill variations (that need to be unlocked...) for the few characters that have them is all you get! (♥♥♥♥ you, dodge/roll). You just have to suck it up when you're playing as skill-less characters.
-Dogs/psychos freak tf out near open doors. it becomes really frustrating to kill them because their leaps are so broken you can barely hit them sometimes. As if it skips animation frames or something so you can't predict the attack. Also I've had dogs leap through walls to kill me?
-rooms are far too open and large, level design isn’t what it used to be. This becomes a nightmare on hard mode in my next point. There are too many offscreen kills, watched a lot of playthroughs just to figure out where they're coming from. It becomes sooo annoying and average players like myself will just end up luring by corners which is a really slow and tedious play style.
-obviously favors ranged weapons and nerfed melee playing styles ... that’s a big deal for me since I’m not good with guns. See: Melee weapon swings have weird timing now. It feels so off compared to the first game. A lot of times it's plain luck that you hit an enemy. Sometimes they charge at you and you die 'cause your swing just??? Misses???? Doesn't feel smooth and swift like in HM1. Another kick in the nuts for melee lovers: your weapon throws will be awful because they don’t go far and you can’t retrieve it since it just barely hit your target.
-oh my gooood hard mode, what the hell. idk if I should complain about this since it's optional, but as a completionist I need to get it done. Hard mode has me clawing my eyes out. Gun Hell. All these windows make slower strategies impossible. Sometimes I wonder if the Dennaton duo can even play these levels in less than an hour
I still had tons of fun playing this, it's just that I became frustrated much more easily because there is a huge difficulty jump compared to the first game. Levels can’t be handled quickly anymore.I talked about how I'd be willing to pay more in my HM review but I dunno about this one. Obviously if you loooooooved the first game like I did in all aspects then you don't want to miss out on this one! Just go buy it. It has a lot to offer, just differently. If you weren't enamored with HM1's gameplay style and don't really care the characters or story, then yeah, give it some thought because I can't say Wrong Number is an improvement in those ways. It’s hard for me to recommend to just anybody. It terms of gameplay and time spent having fun vs. time spent playing angrily, it unfortunately feels like a clunky downgrade from the original.
Still recommending it though because it's fast bloody fun no matter how you look at it.
everybody should totally give the soundtrack a listen regardless tho. At least that's something good we can all agree on.

Regicide is a game made half chess and half WH40K with lot of potencial, which is indeed a dream come true. And I even like both the idea and the game. It's very fun and I will keep playing it.
However, after playing for some days I can not recommend this game at least at full price. If they make some changes I will edit my review, but for now it is what it is. And it's a pity, because I love the idea, and somehow I even like the game, and many of its features.
So, why am I giving a negative review even when I like the game —and a lot—  you may ask? Continue reading the long review.
Short review:
+Very good strategic game overall. Some deep tactics involved
+Campaign is fun and even some missions are hard
+Nice graphics
+Game is really cool
+Developers are really friendly, nice community also
+DLC chapters can be obtained playing the game
+Cross platform multiplayer
-AI is sometimes a bit silly
-Enemy AI cheats you with RNG hehe
-Lack of information, ingame Librarium (help info) bugged, skills not well explained
-Hard to find a match online because few people; sometimes more than 40' and no player found...
-Multiplayer does NOT work, it's currently a crash fest, unplayable (bad servers).
-They introduced an async mode, but you can't watch enemy turn in any way, so pointless
-Cutscenes and intro don't have subtitles
-No borderless windowed mode
Long review:
Game was released months ago, but is still lacking some features. Let me explain a bit. There are two modes, CLASSIC and REGICIDE. Let's talk about Regicide:
Gameplay consists in two phases. First is similar to chess: you make one move and capture an enemy piece, and that is. Pieces are WH40K based, so you will see a marine killing an orc, or the opposite. Some movements doesn't have animations, and some are repetitive, but anyway it is a lot of fun. If you played Battlechess you know what I am talking about.
Second phase is what makes Regicide unique: consists in a very interesting tactical turn with shoots that involve armour and chance to hit, toughness, weapon strength, each unit also have a different health, etc. So it's very fun and well designed, I must say even brilliant. Also, each piece have different skills and the faction you are using also have some. You can use them depending on your total available points to use each turn, the cost of the skills, its cooldowns, range, etc. Also, some of them affect other units, some give buffs, debuffs, area damage, shields, etc.
So the system looks awesome, and indeed it is. You move one piece, and after that, use some points to use skills with some of your pieces (even the one that have just moved), shooting at enemies, etc.
However, UI is a bit clunky, and the game presents an alarming lack of information. For example, you are not able to look ingame at the skills if you have used them this turn or if they are at cooldown, or if you can't use them this turn, or if you don't have line of sight, or in the main menu, etc. Example: it is your turn and you have to move. However, being a deeply tactical game you would like to know which skills you can use after the move and plan accordingly. Well, you can't do it, because some skills will not show up until you move. And even then, not every skill is shown, only the ones available. So you can't plan like 2 or 3 turns before.
Of course, you can ALT+TAB and check all the information in the internet. Because the ingame Librarium (help menu) is also bugged and doesn't show almost anything properly. So be prepared to alt+tab a lot in middle of the game, each time you want to know a skill or that. And enemies doesnt show ANY skill. So when an enemy uses a skill, it says what it is, but you won't know exactly what happened. So you must alt+tab, look and search in the Librarium in official site. Same at the start of the game for EACH enemy unit, because if not, you don't know how to protect against each enemy piece.
Bad part is not that. Bad part is that the forum Librarium (aka manual) is also a bit crap, because most of the information is missing: some skills say "heal a bit amount", but don't say HOW MUCH. Same with plenty of skills, cooldowns, damages, buffs, etc. So you will play the game mostly blind skill-wise.
Each unit has also 5 attributes. And game gives no proper explanation about what are they for. Good luck trying to learn combat mechanics and discover things like "armour is reduced each time weapon strength of the attacker is higher than armour of the defense unit", "each 2 armour points reduced 1 damage", "toughness reduce damage" and some things like that. Because neither the game nor the manual talk about that. You just know each piece got 5 attributes, but not how they work.
Also good luck searching information about line of sight and skill related ones.
More things... Well, game provides experience points, skill points, pieces have some tiers... and if you check forum and that you will discover soon how they function, but game doesn't show the minimal explanation about them, so be lost for some time.
You can buy DLC with money or playing time for more factions (well, mostly variations of the 2 main factions, marines and orcs), so chapters. And they are fun because some of them got different attributes and skills too (which are NOT explained unless you check the bugged librarium). However you can't buy it through steam, only ingame.
Other than that, the game got some bugs, more of them minor. And not fine UI, for example when you want to learn the units, there is a hotkey that lets you use an overlay for chess pieces over them. Well, it disappears each time your turn ends AND each time a death animation happens. So you must click 3 times that hotkey at the end of each turn, and after each death animation. Ugly.
CLASSIC mode is Chess with warhammer pieces.
Conslusion:
This is why I can't recommend this game —at full price—, for now. Game got potencial, is really fun, but the lack of information and some silly decisions added later, make this maybe doesn't worth your buy until they change some things and improve other ones. And multiplayer server looks bad, too many crashes at the start or at the middle of the game that make this game doesn't worth your money even in a big discount until its fixed (if someday it's fixed, which I start to doubt).
However it is somehow fun, and chess+WH makes it a must for some guys like me. So read some information about it and maybe you can enjoy it just for the campaign even with their problems if you are a fanboy like me. But be warned if not because multiplayer does NOT work.

I hope i wouldnt get any hate for this, a lot of folks really enjoy this game... I tried too. I'm a sucker for all 40k related, so that was an automatic buy for me. I'm not particular fond of chess, but i know the rules. I hoped maybe Regicide will help me get into chess more. That was a mistake, because this game is a weird combination of ideas.. and i can't really say i enjoy this mixture.
Main mode, so called "Regicide" consists of two phases. In one, you move your pieces, like in a standard chess game. Moving, capturing - the same. Next is the Intiative Phase. Now things get messy. You can use initiation points to ... shoot enemy pieces or use skills. Every piece has its HP and Armor, so if you can't capture it by standard means, you can just kill it from a distance. To add insult to injury, every action in the Initiative Phase has percentage of success. So... you can for example - miss every shot. Not mentioning that two pieces on both sides can be diffrent in stats. Assault Space Marine (Knight) will have other stats than Ork Rockteer (Knight). Which is obvious within the lore, but ... it's CHESS.
Why that bothers me? You have a SYNCHRONIC game like chess, in which luck is not a factor... and you add to it - ASYNCHRONIC elements and luck-based mechanics. I does not work for me. For some people, it's a new level, a new challenge. For me it's just ridicilous.... and i really tried to like it. I forced myself to play it, but every time results are the same. Above that game feels very sluggish, probably due to two phases which every player must go through.
What else? Graphics are fine, music is ok, but it feels like one track repeats all the time (maybe it's just my ears decieving me). Voice-over work is pretty decent, props for that. Overall, it's hard for me to recommend Regicide... Is it for chess players? Not really. Maybe for 40k fans? Maybe, but if you're not familiar with chess, you will feel completly lost.
So, its for Wh40k fans who enjoy chess? Such a weird focus group.  I'm a 40k fanboy, i do enjoy a bit of chess... and i don't like Regicide. So we're in a pickle here.

I'm absolutely TORN on how I feel about this game. Combat feels workable, the core gameplay loop is great and there's actually a degree of depth in this game. At a glance it appears as a completely blatent knock-off of Left 4 Dead's model, and while it is very much *inspired* by the model to the point of replication the developers added in some new features that make it stand out and seem unique. Despite this there are quite a few issues with how the developers intended to make gameplay "last longer" utilizing a leveling/EXP system, a loot drop system at the end of each level based on rolling digital dice, and an infuriatingly poorly implimented 'crafting' system that was recently added (just before I began playing).
The good bits: I love the Skaven as an enemy type. They've got visual designs that appear interesting and are just so fun to tangle in a melee with. From the heavily armored Storm Vermin (who can come in patrols that can easily wipe underprepared teams), to the Bombadier Rat who lobs gas bombs at you, to the very sleek design of the Assassin Rat, every rat save for the notible exception of the Rat Ogre (literally a rat version of the Tank from left 4 dead in literally every way) looks absolutely fantastic. Combat feels visceral yet rewarding, with weapons acting somewhat well and a clear tradeoff between vicious attack speed and much-needed armor penetration for dealing with all of the scarier threats in the game. This game has a solid gameplay loop fixed firmly in the model that Left 4 Dead began with, and if you've got a few friends to play this with, it can be absolutely fun.
The not-so good bits: Many problems with this game stem from the absolute lack of innovation on an established, but tired model built in the Left 4 Dead franchise. In addition to that, the gameplay feels a slight degree of unrefinement- especially in the Melee combat (the whole reason you play this over Left 4 Dead, unless you have a thing for molesting rats with various fantasy weapons). Generally speaking I've seen three types of successful Melee Combat- Condemned: Criminal Origins has a standard center-screen attack, a charged swipe attack, and a block. Half Life 2 and most old-style shooters use a standard 'reticle' melee attack which hits exactly where you point the mouse, with laser precision. Dead Island had a location-specific aim and swing mechanic that allowed you to make tricky headshots or hit specific limbs. To Vermintide's discredit, neither of these approaches are used. You've got a 'close enough' center screen attack, a 'probably' charged swing attack, and a block that sort of works sometimes (depending on variables that I've yet to work out the meta on besides Shields being useful and everything else sucking). The melee combat feels like it's inching close to workability but sometimes trying to get headshots on the armored foes that you absolutely need to get headshots on can feel like playing a D20 system.
The UGLY truth: This game is a time-sink which has a reward system built entirely around one simple principle - Loot Grinding. You get EXP to unlock loot, the loot is randomly generated. You complete missions to get loot, the loot is randomly rolled for and generated. You can technically play the very-hard version of the game where you pick up hidden books that take up healing and utility slots of your inventory, just to modify how screwed you are in the RNG loot system. At its very core, Vermintide is a game that has solid gameplay built entirely around this loot system. Loot is tiered, there's even 'tokens' you get from losing missions or breaking down weapons using the in-lobby forge and it's just a mess. It's a game that wants you to play it for hours, but won't let you have the power-creep that any non-grinding person will want to play. I can't tell you readily how many runs of the first mission, The Horn of Magnus, I've played loot-grinds on. I can tell you that mission is hilariously burned into my brain- when more exciting missions should be instead.
Lastly, souring my experience is that the missions are kind of slotted together without any real narrative beyond some breifings and the premise of the game. Additionally, I've yet to find a way to disable the introduction cinematic and have to wait for it to load, skip it, and then load the in game lobby. Oh yes, the lobby loads every time- simultaneously a cool menu and a poor starting room for most players (you explore the menu in first person, essentially). If it had a better narrative, a more rewarding loot system (seriously, of the 14 hours i've played thus far, probably 10 of it has been spent loot grinding for a single decent Mace and Shield combo), and a bit more consistent melee system, I'd recommend it at the full listed MSRP. However, I can only suggest to purchase it on sale for now, until the game gets more fixes and/or some content added. Oh and lets not forget that loot system SERIOUSLY needs refinement.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

Review Update - Having played Dirt Rally and Dirt 4 back to back, I can see more clearly why people were disappointed with Dirt 4.  Dirt Rally's handling has far more weight to it and you get a greater sense of feedback from the tyres. Also, after playing for a few more hours, I notice that certain elements of the stages, especially the Spanish ones, get very repetitive in some places, repeating a similar if not identical stretch of road every now and then. Due to these factors, I have decided to reduce my rating of this game to an 8/10 from 9. HOWEVER, this does not mean I think the game is bad. Far from it actually. Below is the review that I originally posted. End of review update.
I don't really understand why people dislike this game. This was not intended to be a sequel to Dirt Rally, even if it borrows a lot of elements from it. I'm not sure why people are making that connection. This is a sequel to Dirt 3, so its arcade style elements should come as no surprise.
That being said, there's no reason not to have both Dirt Rally and Dirt 4. Because, truth be told, they are quite different games. Whereas Dirt Rally focuses on real life rally stages and realistic handling, Dirt 4 focuses on innovation and fun. I play both Dirt Rally and Dirt 4 and they are both fantastic games.
It's pretty obvious that randomly generated stages are not as realistic as replicas of real life ones, but the point of the 'Your Stage' feature is not to be realistic. It's designed to enhance the sense of unknown with rally driving, and make every stage totally unique. Yes, the stages can get repetitive from time to time, but Dirt 4 offers the best randomly generated tracks I've ever seen in a racing game. Way better than Gran Turismo 5's rally mode that's for damn sure.
And the random events that occur on the rally stages adds a whole new layer of immersion. Seriously, I haven't had this level of excitement with going into a stage since WRC Rally Evolved back on the PS2! That game also had random events such as broken down cars, rocks falling on the stage or animals darting out in front of you. I feel like Dirt 4 has bought this element back and I now believe it should be an essential part of all rally games to come.
The car selection is very good. Although, a few cars were dropped from Dirt Rally, most notably the 1.6 litre WRC cars including the Ford Fiesta, VW Polo and Mini JCW (probably due to licencing issues), but as a substitute, we get three R5 class cars, which are among the funnest cars to drive in the game. Light and agile with excellent power delivery.
I've played the Rally Cross and Land Rush modes, both of which are very good, but the main reason I bought this game was for its rally experience, so that's where I have spent most of my time. There's also a freeroam area, 'DirtFish', where the rally school takes place, as well as a variety of activities from smash attack to time attack events, all of which are fun in one way or another.
In terms of accessibility, the game offers two handling modes. Simulation and Gamer. I've gone for the former, but the Gamer handling mode is pretty fun as well. It really depends on your driving style. There are the usual assortment of options to allow you to change the difficulty of the AI, driving assists and so on, so the game is flexible for newcomers and pros alike. It's worth noting that the leaderboards for simulation and gamer handling modes are separate from each other.
Graphics and sounds are, hands down, the best Codemasters has ever done. This is arguably the best looking and sounding rally game to date. I'm personally over the moon at the fact they finally added supercharger sounds to the Lancia 037 and Delta S4! The game overall has an incredible attention to detail. My favourite detail is that car engines move when you rev them!
In terms of handling, it's largely unchanged from Dirt Rally, at least from my experience. I never really considered Dirt Rally to be a true simulation, not to the same level as Richard Burns Rally. With this being said, if you played Dirt Rally, you should feel right at home with Dirt 4 if you choose the simulation handling mode.
The online daily, weekly and monthly events have carried over from Dirt Rally, as well as a few multiplayer modes. The usual stuff. I just recently did my first Rally Cross online race (against one other person). Unfortunately, there doesn't seem to be a lot of people playing Jam Sessions. Most people do the competitive rally stages and that's about it. However, these are super fun, so no surprise that hundreds of people participate in those.
To conclusion, I love this game. Compared to its true predecessor, Dirt 3, this is a huge improvement in pretty much every area (aside from the fact there's no Gymkhana, but that personally doesn't bother me).
I play Dirt 4 with a PS4 controller, but I've also played it with my Logitech Driving Force GT wheel. An oldie, but a goodie! Are you an Open World RPG lover?
Do you like to use bows, spears, Shields and Swords?
Then this game is the perfect game for you.
I have spent 42 hours the past week in this game and i am going to spend another 42 hours the next week. And do you know what? After those 84 hours there will still be more to do.
The game is basic. You start off by yourself, a noob in the land of the Kings. Here you get to decide your fate. You can be a vassal, a bandit, a king, a queen, you can probably even be an outpost (Would be quite boring though). Due to the games awesome character development you also have to chose what kind of person you will be in this game.
Will you use Swords? One hand or two hand?
Will you use throwing weapons? Bow and arrow? Polearms? Crossbow?
Will you travel fast and light or perhaps slow but immense inventory space?
There are numerous skills you can chose between, but limited skill points to use.
You then run around in the world, gathering forces and developing your character until you have conqured the world. This, as mentioned before can be done in different ways.
It is the opportunity to do as you please that gives me the goose bumps when playins this game, it is as I want to play, how I want to form my fate that matters. And for these quite simple features the game becomes immensley fun.
I recommend this game to you whom is looking to spend some time in a game and already is or wants to test the sandbox RPG genre that M&B Warband so succesfully has placed itself in.
If you are going to play the game, i also recommend you to first play it a while in the "Native" setting then if you like it serach out mods that are out there.
The mod that i am currently using is called "Floris" which is just an expansion on the native, giving a better game experience.
This is the game for all RPG lovers, if you skip this for any reason you have missed the a truly awesome game.

I really loved the first installment of Hotline Miami & wanted to love this game.
Unfortunately, I became bored with it halfway through:
- My main irritation is that progress is saved per chapter, a chapter consists of too many levels which are rather large and difficult in the second half of the game... which means that you'll have to replay large chunks of difficult levels when you have to log off.  When you get a bit stuck in a level, you'll have to replay the previous ones multiple times... gets very frustrating.
- The AI is still as stupid as in the first one, but the larger levels & distances make this more painfully obvious.
- The story is much less engaging than in the first one, I just wanted to skip these story scenes completely.  It broke the flow & didn't add anything for me.  There were way too many of these.
- There's different characters with very different strong points and weaknesses this time around.  This sounds good on paper, but it is determined who you play with in which level most of the time.  This got me forced into mechanics and playstyles I didn't like at all, giving me ridiculous constrictions that broke the flow/emersion completely... and made some levels a chore instead of fun.
If you haven't played it yet, buy the first one.

So most of the people reading this review are going to be people who've played this game in the past and wish to play it again. If you're not one of these people, I probably wouldn't pick up this game. It's not a traditional Sonic game. There's 6 different playable characters and two of them do Sonic based levels (Sonic/Shadow). This turns most people off who've never played the game (based off of what I've seen in the reviews anyway). Go look up some gameplay of Tails/Eggman/Rouge/Knuckles in this game if you're still interested though.
That being said, let me just clarify some things for those old players.
- The port is a piece of♥♥♥♥♥♥ I actually bought this game quite a while ago and wasn't able to play it at all, regardless of what I did. I later built a new computer (not just for this game of course) along with a new monitor. That monitor actually ended up causing me some issues. If you have a 144hz monitor the game is going to run at double speed. It took me a while to figure out why the game was doing this and I couldn't find any solutions online. Turns out all you have to do is change your monitor to 60hz. The game flat out just won't play on fullscreen, and I wouldn't stand for windowed. So I got Borderless Gaming (Steam application) which basically allows you to play games on borderless window regardleses of their settings. There are free versions of this program, but anyways that's what I had to put up with just to get the game to play. I also get a 1 second stutter roughly every 5 minutes. I've got no idea why this is, but it doesn't really matter anymore since I almost have all the achievements anyway.
Despite my (and many others) experience with the horrible port this shouldn't discourage you. There's a refund feature on Steam that not everyone knows about. Here's some information about it:
If the game doesn't run well for you (which believe me there's a good chance it won't) then simply refund.
- The game seems to be ported from the Dreamcast version, meaning the easter eggs that were (previously) only on Dreamcast can be found on here too.
- If you want to get all of the achievements you >must< get the DLC.

Since Ankama Games is a French game company, creating a connection with the United States and other countries really helped the game with one of the problems it had, population of the English servers.
I believe Wakfu is a great game and it should be looked at for players who want something different in their MMO. However, Wakfu lacks the ability to keep the players they recieve and although I greatly enjoy the game, and everything it provides, I can't help hoping for more of the game.

Again and again I find myself returning to this game, only to encounter a diffirent disbalance and same broken AI. One would think that since the game came out, developers could adress these issues. Instead, we get alternative questlines and new cash shop items.
The gameplay is enjoyable. The artstyle is good. But the world feels very, very empty.
The game was originally intended to have a community. Players run faction politics, entire economy and even location ecosystems. It has now gotten to a point where people jump to another server, just because it has a spike in population. Many people who return to the game after a long time seem to be bewildered by the state of affairs.
There is variety of classes, each with their own, unique abilities that grow stronger as you use them. This is great, except because of the aforementioned imbalance, which in turn leads to a class getting nerfed or revamped. Remember that character that you played a while ago that you really liked? Here, have a totally diffirent one.
Crafting is a grindfest. If there was an active economy going, this would have been easier. But if you want to create a good item, you have to personally collect all the components required for a specific item and craft it. Both of these require a good amount of time to get the skills for. And the list of required components can often be quite extensive. This repeated process is the only way to advance in a crafting profession.
There's an extensive list of unique enemies, who often come in matched groups, so as long as you advance in level or just travel a lot, you get to face various new challanges. This only lasts until later levels, when the grind sets in, or when you just need to acquire specific components or a piece of armor. This uniqueness also causes AI to frequently do random things. And woe upon you if you picked a summoner class - healers who prefer full health targets over dying allies, melee summons who decide to just step back a bit and skip turn...
I wish the game would do better, I really do. But so far I've come to be repeatedly dissapointed.

TL;DR:  Very well-executed game, packs a bunch of lore into a 4-person co-op game in the veins of Payday 2 & Left 4 Dead 2.  Recommended for those fans of first-person-co-op games that enjoy playing with others, but less so for those people who aren't prone to play online.
Pros:
* Controls are smooth and (mostly) intuitive
* Graphics are very good-looking and a wide variety of settings are available
* Audio is excellent -- when you hit a rat, it sounds exceedingly satisfying
* Gameplay is good, but the RNG really hits hard when you start getting to the highest difficulty (cataclysm) if you're not prepared
* Story is well fleshed-out, brief enough to keep your attention and brush the top of the End Times lore
* Developers are very invested in their job, and frequently listen to players' input and comments
Cons:
* Still a little buggy in places, but much better than release
* AI improvements to rats make the game harder, but the AI for the bots still needs some tweaking
* Client-side hosting (P2P)!  Rat damage is calculated on the host's end, but the damage you do to rats is calculated on your end, working well for right now but making for awkward situations when one person (the host) has sub-optimal internet
I would heartily recommend this game to any of my friends, and I applaud Fat Shark (the Devs) for making such an awesome game.  Can't wait for any DLC or sequels!

Silverfall is what you call a Diablo clone. There are some great examples of such games, like Torchlight, Titan Quest, Grim Dawn, etc., but for some reason for me Silverfall is the best, i'd say this game is really underrated and is even hidden gem of genre.
Well, this review won't be very long, i will just point out what i really liked about this game. It's combination of little good things, which make this game really fun to play.
For pros I'll start with... graphics. This game actually looks amazing, it uses cell shading technology (yeah, before our favourite The Walking Dead game and Borderlands), and because of that all scenery and character models look really unique and cool. Sound effects and OST are amazing too, they add great deal to the atmosphere of the game.
Gameplay... can't say much about that, it's your typical "kill monsters, earn XP and weapons, equip better gear, repeat". The only non-typical thing about gameplay is variability - you can combine several classes as you like, like you can be warrior-mage or tank-healer with familiars no problem. I'd say it's a great trait for a game of that genre, because it adds replayability value (I myself completed the game more than 10 times and wasn't bored of it, so yeah).
Plot is kinda simple, but it's okay. I liked voice acting and liked characters, so nothing much else to say.
So the only real issue with this game is that it's really hard to run. For some reason this game doesn't go well on new computers (on every computer, to be exact) because of a really old weird DirectX plugin, so you must do a litte work and download proper patch to run this game. This sucks, yeah, but this stupid technichal issue is really the one thing that I (and many other reviewers) dislike so much about this game.
So yeah, if you want to spend few evenings with a good old RPG action game - Silverfall may be the game that you are looking for. It's really cheap too, especially on sales, so i really recomend you to try it out.

I own the hard copy of this game, and played the hell out of it, when I was young with my friend Christopher. the times we had with this game was awesome.
The game can be tricky for new comers and experienced gamers alike as the interface and controls are a bit clunky. like most top down dungeon crawler lootfests you move your character by clicking the mouse where you want them to move, Or you can hold the mouse button down and drag it to move automatically. The graphics in the game are nice, although I'd recommend playing on lower end graphics, if you want the best performance as framerates can take a dive if there are too many enemies on screen.
After the tutorial level, the game throws you into the real world, and says "Go for it" one of the things you will notice is in this game you have to pick a side between either Nature or Technology. You can try to stay neutral, though if you do, not much will get done, and you won't be able to use the best possible items that each tree has to offer. Like most lootfests, you have a large amount of weapons to use, so you will generally find something to your liking. whether its swords, axes, maces, hand weapons, or halberds, you will find something you like.
As I said this game is can be VERY HARD, and I mean it, essentially this game can make you rip your hair out more, than dark souls, hard.
basically, combat isn't that hard, but the enemies level with the player, so if you want to do some grinding, you can go pretty much anywhere and kill some mobs to level up.
BUT, one thing to note, if you die, you loose all the equipment on you, and its up to you to go track it down, thankfully the game gives you a marker on where your stuff is. Although, when you die before reaching your equipment, the marker will change to that grave stone, so you have to track down your original grave based on your knowledge. Although this can be avoided if you pay for life insurance in the game. basically there is this guy who says "Pay some gold to keep your sh*t" which comes in handy if you feel your underleveled, or not confident. however life insurance only applies for that life, so if you forget to purchase it again once you respawn, than you better not die.
This game is worth every cent if you want a good hack and slash lootfest.

I'm playing racing games since my early childhood.
Dirt 2, Dirt 3 (completed several times) and Forza are my favorites.
Dirt 2 and 3 were awesome games. Dirt 2 had an incredible setting with a challenging career. Dirt 3 offered so many different locations, great cars, cool setting.
That's what I also excpected  from Dirt 4. But I was let down massively.
Cars:
Theres a broad variety of cars from different eras. Rally, Rallycross, Landrush and some Classics are nicely modelled. But that's it. Nothing special, and some are lacking from the game, such as the Trailblazer Cars.
Disciplines:
Theres a sufficient variety of disciplines. I miss Gymkhana and Trailblazer, those were great fun, even though Gymkhana could have been excluded from the career.
Locations:
That's the biggest issue: In Dirt 3 you had so many different locations, you could do Rallycross on Snow, on Asphalt, on Gravel, everywhere. Same with Rally, Landrush etc. But in Dirt 4 you have only one snowy Location (Sweden) which is only available for Rally. It's really sad that they didn't include Aspen, that was my favorite. The locations in Dirt4 become extremely boring, extremely fast.
Everyone whished for narrower Rally Stages. But flipping the car in Sweden as soon as you touch the snowy edge of the road (which btw isn't soft) is not fun. The missing rewind option (at least I couldn't find it) makes it even worse.
Conclusion:
If you're looking for one of the best Racing Games ever, get Dirt 3. If you're looking for great Rallying, get Dirt Rally. Do not get this game.

I bought this game hoping it would be like Battlechess for the 401st century.  It's an interesting concept, but it has many flaws.
1. The AI is laughably bad, often throwing away units by moving to undefended positition where they can be captured without any threat of recapture.
2. The combat animations are repetitive.  There is only one animation for each possible capture, and only one animation for each attack.  Some skills don't even have animations.
3. The tooltips for the skills and stats have very little information.  They don't say what the duration, cooldown, or damage done by each skill is.  Damage and hit chance are somehow based on unit strength, toughness, weapon skill, and armor, but there is no explanation of how these work.
Fun warhammer themed chess easily worth the sale price.

Enjoyable and unique twist on classic chess, mixing in a tactics game with the Regicide mode and the campaign.
For all the talk about the microtransactions: I've played games that have the EXACT same unlock mechanic, but without the option of forking over some money to get it early. There are no complaints this kind of system.
Regicide, on the other hand, allows you to bypass maybe an hour or two of game time to unlock a cosmetic by spending 99 cents. Whooboy, that's crazy talk. Actually it isn't. This is what people are talking about when they want microtransations done properly. So no, you can't play as the Space Wolves immediately, but that is simple progression. You can either play the game, which is great, or pay some money.

Regicide is a great game, as long as you read the descriptions and know what you're getting. If you're a fan of 40K and you quite like chess, you can't go wrong. This can be played as classic "battle" chess, simply playing using the usual rules, but using the animated pieces. Honestly, your opponent's piece is so much more satisfying when your units fight to the death, claiming a square on top of their disembowelled enemy!
On the other hand, you can play with the actual Regicide mode. This is broken down into the "movement" phase, during which you play a move much like standard chess, followed by the "initiative" phase, where you will follow up your move by spending initiative points to perform actions such as shooting another piece at range. This adds a whole new layer to standard chess, and any usual chess strategies quickly get blown out of the window when your pawn (marine) gets annihilated by a group of orcs!
In addition, a storyline has been added, with the board set up in various ways in keeping with the scene. This is enough to keep the games interesting and varied, and I like the addition.
While Regicide may not be for everyone, I personally love it. It's one of those combinations that sounds like it should be terrible, but turns out to be a real gem. I paid the sale price, (which is actually why I took the risk and gave this a go) so it's safe to say I'm more than happy with the value. That said, having now played and had great fun, I think I'd also have been happy if I'd taken  the original £15 price tag. Well worth a look.
The only reason you wouldn't like this game is if you HATED chess, because this is chess ON STEROIDS.

I see a lot of people whining about aspect ratio and FPS, which is silly, the creator intended for it to be experienced that way, and if you don't like it, it's a VERY simple console command.
As for the actual game, it's very compelling. I have zero issues with lag or controls, but then again, I am running a high end rig, so I imagine most peoples complaints are because their machines aren't as powerful as they expect, and haters gonna hate.
The story has been very intriguing, and keeps me looking forward to the next reveal. The game looks great, though the cut scenes do seem to lack a little, in game the atmosphere and enviroment really shine. The monsters look great, and the quick decision to either run, or fight your way through at a high risk of wasting ammo, makes a fun and exciting game system. So far though, it hasn't been "scary", have not had a single jump, nor have I felt exceptionally "on edge". It is more of a psychological and grusome horror.
This isn't a blast your way through everything game, sometimes it's best to just SURVIVE.
I am really enjoying this game, and think most of the negative reviews are from people that expected something different out of it, or, as I said, have underpowered hardware.
Haven't finished the game yet, but definately going to play it through, and already am glad I bought the season pass.

Hello all! Finny posting here, some of you who are reading this might want a brief review, some of you might just be looking at another Hardcore Wakfu players opinion so I'll give both. Played hours here 600 odd actual? 3.3k (no life)
1st things 1st, this game is extremely unique i've never played a game like this, a game like this is truly amazing and so is the fact that the game is available on the Mac platform (what i'm using).
TLDR: Game is amazing but VERY VERY grind-y, lonely and un-sociable (Read bottom paragraph). Would recommend :]
Story: This is extremely limited, this is newbie friendly but is very short and only links to Ogrest which is still yet to be incorporated into the game (I think this was going to be level 200 content) once you progress to mid 100 content (level 50) the newely revamped islands (currently 2 out of 5-6+) you then get new quest-lines which feature ways to get Kamas (In game money) quicker through even more exploration of the game, this is tedious but can be fun for people who are casual and don't mind spending 20 hours+ running around the game. The story then jutters and jumps to mid game content (level 100, 118, 120 and 125) these questlines again feature kama making methods and are EXTREMELY fun and give an insight into the story of the game and the Ultimate Bosses (weekly bosses, sadly no challenge what-so-ever) you then have the section of the game which is the most grindy, intensive, game quit feeling inducing moment ever, this is the jump from 120 to the next 140 quest, this is the most boring and lonely grind experience ever, this puts most people off the game. From here you have more quests more frequently and you would have probably found a guild and start to have some online Wakfu friends, you then lead into the high level content, I won't speak about this since you'll probably have a basic understanding of the game and some good friends etc.
Guilds: This is all down to preference but the size of the guilds aren't huge and you are basically forced into high level guilds just to see anyone online, there are a few English guilds which are really nice and newbie friendly (notice how I said few, it really is hardly any guilds that are newbie friendly) when entering this game it's not advised to ask high levels for leeching I will give you a quick run down of why:
XP is grindy as HECK
You'll be on 0.5-0.75x XP meaning that someone grinding you a few levels will feel like a life time, period.
Fun factor
Is it fun for high levels? Yes and No, depends on their mood and what you're like as a player etc.
Language Barrier
Hit and miss remember this game is multi-cultural so be wary of whom you ask for help due to language barriers!
In game revenue / money method
This is called 'Kamas' you gain some each fight and with chests that you open from completing a respective Questline, this is tedious but you get quite a lot of money, awesome!
On Remington you have quite a nice economy meaning that while some items are crazy high they are endgame and so you'll only aim for these once you have complete knowledge of the game and dungeons etc. Majority of other high level stuff is dirt cheap so that's cool!
Dungeons:
Fun and grindy you don't have to run it 1,000 time for an item to have 1 chance of dropping it but instead....! You can run it 1,000 times to get enough tokens to buy it huzzzah! So it's all down to your opinion, there's also major awesome guides online showing you how to complete these dungeons as-well as other players that you'll be running with experience!
PvP:
Completely broken due to only a select amount of classes being revamped and overly powerful, unless you follow the crowd with new classes i'd advise against it.
Classes:
Old ones are much weaker and often not taken/ accepted as much in dungeons compared to newer classes, same with other games but sad really R.I.P Sadida ;w;
Bugs:
This game has a fair amount of bugs in it but these seem to be ironed out fairly quickly, until recently where dupers have been duping end game items and selling them for very low prices, this has in turn kinda ruined the economy and the player base due to not trusting the market and other players, a lot of people such as my self feel slightly cheated that new people pick it 1-4 of these duped 20million each relics and I spent months farming 1 worth 4 million... This is a major problem as of May 26th 2015 so if you're reading the review take this into account!

Vermintide is an excellent co-op shooter. Mechanically, the game is very similar to Left 4 Dead, but with a stronger emphasis on melee combat. There are a limited number of levels, but they are all extremely detailed and as fun to play for a tenth or twentieth time as for a second or third. The loot system also adds to replayability, not because you ever have to grind for loot in order to progress, but because it provides customization and a fun reward for completing harder missions. The difficulty is also well balanced, with the book pick-ups enabling players to make things harder for themselves during a mission in order to get better rewards. Also, while set in the Warhammer universe, this is certainly not just for fans of the franchise. The rats are an appealing enemy for just about anyone, with approachably flavorful animation and voice lines. The player characters are a lot of fun as well. Definitely recommend for anyone looking for a game to play with friends.

1. Increase your mouse sensitivity

3. Watch your back and everyone else's.
4. Stay with the group or die.
5. Books are good for once, dont drop them.
6. Heal your allies (especially the ones who picked the grims up), dont be selfish....unless they are really really bad.
7. Get rid of poison globadiers ASAP.
8. Get a weapon with bloodlust/regrowth.
9. Get a blue weapon before trying hard, unless you got a good group. Its not so much as skill as it is your gear. A higher tier weapon can mean the difference between 2 hits to kill and 3, and when your killing 250+ rats, those can add up.
10. BLOCK AND DODGE!! you can also block and revive someone at the same time.

Artix Entertainment are passionate gamers first before developers. I've played their games for over 7 years with their consistent weekly releases, their communication with the community is top notch and I supported the kickstarter but I'm not going to sugarcoat my words. Unless you like playing unfinished games, or just like testing things out and helping the developers grow the foundation of the community from early access, I'd not recommend it as it is in very, very early stages of development. Beta will last for a long period of time (I'd say 4-6 years if they even want to compete with other games in the market and with their limited resources) from what's here and needed to be worked on. As the game adds content to convey what to expect from the full release the review will change dramatically as the game itself.
There's a lot of work to be done. In the state the game is in it's really, really boring and sucks quite frankly. I don't even want to play it. But I have if you look at my hours. Probably even more if you count pre-beta and unaccounted time on mobile. I'll say one thing quests are like this:
Artix: "I need bone dusts"
"Need more"
"I'll never be satisfied no matter how many skeletons you kill"
"Lol, you're still going at it?!?!"
"Keep killing skeletons"
"Here...kill some shadow wolves"
"BACK TO SKELETONS!!!!"
"Great work keep it up, now more"
Also getting a group for dungeons is horrible. There's no queue and you literally will be joining dungeons that are halfway or more done already. Therefore wasting keys. And progress in the dungeons don't affect everyone so if one of your teammates goes around killing everything without you you will have to use another key everytime for a new run to make sure you attack the monsters. You can only invite people if they are your friend which is dumb. And even with that said, the party system doesn't even work like an actual party system. Monsters feel way too powerful and makes the grind and questing even worse. Additionally, your player character feels absolutely underpowered during the grind to 15.  After every battle, resting and potions would be required as if you're fighting a mini boss. And that's literally just one field monster. You'd need a group of players to make it feel less of a chore.
One major issue though though AE, AQ3D is not AQWorlds. Do not bother to push out any further crazy cash grabs business models like in AQWorlds. Hell, I'll admit I've spent too much money for me to quit in AQWorlds but it ain't no pay to win MMO. Everything is for fashion only. HOWEVER, remove the Pay2Win microtransactions to skip farming materials to obtain the gears right away from this game. REMOVE IT. Focus on the MMORPG aspects of its 3D counterpart. Make it an MMORPG. There's no need to follow a similar guideline as its 2D counterpart. AQW is more of a fashion MMO game with RPG elements. We need an RPG like those are your single player browser games but evolved and something people would expect in the years to come. And please just because the game is also on mobile as well...don't think you cannot do as good as other MMOs in the market. Though, it's the mobile part that worries me if it affects development for this game making it a crappy mobile mmorpg on PC. Even if it's a good port. I know you guys want to make this game a multiplatform friendly game that anyone can play and enjoy but from what's here it ain't gonna cut it. It's time to get serious and make a game that can pull in serious competition.

I. Introduction and Background
I have started playing Artix's games since Adventure quest in 2002, since then I have only played DragonFable and AQ3D. What I loved about adventure quest was the actual strategy required for end game gameplay. And how indepth the story was. I put about 1000 hours into it and about 800 into dragonfable. So far with AQ3d I find that the feeling is different than the original AQ, obviously because it is in open beta and is 3d and has a sliver of the content AQ has but still.
II. The Gameplay
The gameplay of AQ3D needs a little bit of work with controlling your character but after a little bit of playing; the average player will get used to the "snap" feel of moving the character and the camera. This does not hinder your performance as a gamer or hinder the fun either so it isnt really a big con. One thing I do like aboout the gameplay is it just feels right.. Not too much, not too little. Which is what makes a beta memorable.
III. The Graphics
Here is where most people with a $1000 pc and up may disagree with the game. I personally have a modest $500 build that I built myself. But most may not be appealed to the graphics that the game has to offer. But they must realize where this company came from. A strictly 2d only game making company has made a 3D game that consistently runs 60 fps, on almost all systems, and mobile devices! whilst mobile devices and PC's can play with eachother! This is a huge and incredible step. Not only does this keep the community of the game together and not split. it keeps their credibility as a good company high as well. It is not easy to do what they are doing. But overall the graphics represent there style as it should be. Imagine minecraft not being pixelated and "blocky" (pun intended you trolls). Minecraft would lose that special feel to the design, and I feel that is what they are doing here. They are using their special cartoon-like style to keep theiur franchise going and guess what.. it is still working.
IV. Early, Middle, and End Game
Due to this game currently being in Open beta, this section of the review will be harsh and nice. For starters, I Love the early and mid game sections. if you dont do the stupid bridge strat at level 1, you can really get some good gameplay out of the first 11 levels. The feeling of running that dungeon just one more time to get that badass sword or armor piece is a great feeling and is actually the core of many huge MMORPG games today. Like running a raid on WoW. Early and Mid games really shine from this. Then we get to End game.. End game right now is Frankly boring. Which is understandable! Open Beta is a term that will be used often in this review. But rightnow, end game is just the shadow Skull bridge and the shadow skull tower and/or angered acevorah if you are going for the dagger. That is about it. The grinding isnt necessarily hard because You can go through the dungeon at the shadowskull tower at level 13 pretty easily. So the second you hit level 15 after being on the bridge for a couple of hours, you can craft all of your wanted sweet loot and gear! but what then? you technically have the best gear available.. Exceptions like necrohen hat put aside.
V. Potential Awareness
This is the most important part of the review in my eyes. Whether or not I see potential in this game. I see a buttload of potential. Every game that Artix and his crew have started, they have finished. Heck, Dragonfable is about to get a new class and armor! They still support most of their games, they have always treated their fans to a good time. They listen to their fans too. So I believe that this game does have a high potential to become a hit.
VI. Overall grade
I give Adventure Quest3D a 4/5. Simply put, it is a great game. It is simple now, but in a year... This game will be the bees knees! so go on and collect rares now so that in a years worth of time you can look back and remember grinding 8 hours to hit level 15 from 14 ;P

Adventure Quest 3D is the third Adventure Quest game so far. From what started as a simple but fleshed out in-browser web game has gone to a side-scrolling MMO and now a fully 3D RPGMMO. Honestly one the most underrated game series of all time Adventure Quest 3D only builds upon the already in depth lore. Not only did they recreate the original town of Battleon in 3D but they also expanded upon the simplistic combat style of the original game but added a more engaging feel to fighting overall. However I am a bit disappointed that they didn't include the Healer class from AQW. And the game has a wonderful sense of humor, rather than do the run-of-the-mill tutorial it thrusts you right in on the action while also adding in a sarcastic comment about it. AQ3D is simply not afraid to go against what has already been established in common RPGMMO games and going for a Morrowind type of questing, giving you a quest and a location and then having you go out and find the quest location. And you simply cannot ignore the fact of the seamless intergration of cross-platform play between PC, Apple and Android products. I would have to give this game an 8/10 and I can only imagine it will get better as time goes as Artix Entertainment updates their games frequently.

I don´t know why, but I need to write kind of a full review on this even if nowhere near professional. I´ll try to keep spoilers out as much as possible for anyone that could care about the story.
This game is super short, myself I beat it around 4 hours.
Story: Some terrorists invade your home/ship/whatever (???), you try to escape and get powers because reasons. The game didn´t tell much that I understood, there´s 0 connection to the characters and why they are doing what they are doing. For example: why in the world would the main characters friend stay to risk his own life just to make really dumb jokes and being almost useless? Said friend is just gone later in the game and is never heard from ever again.
Final boss is not explained why it´s there, the ending is just dumb and everything is just horribly cheesy.
Gameplay: It´s a third person shooter with climbing. swimming and platforming. Sounds great, right? It´s not. The shooting is alright at best, but the platforming... oh god the platforming is bad. I found myself going climbing down instead of up, and sometimes just falling to my death because why not. The best part is the swimming. If there's anything good in this game, it´s the water. It would be the perfect swimming simulator if there wasn´t this little girls voice constantly giggling and screaming inaudible stuff. I get what it´s trying to do with the whole fear of drowning thing, but a little girls giggling only makes it annoying.
Now the shooting. The shooting is pretty good, only one big flaw: the ai. The ai really loves to walk into you and shoot you until you are dead, but at least you get to kill stuff... in water.
Graphics: The graphics look really nice even on lowest settings. Most people would tear their eyes out because they want super realistic graphics, but I say the graphics is alright in my book.
The water isn´t ultra realistic, but it looks good enough. Probably don´t belong here, but I really liked that the water kept slowly rising instead of just stopping at a certain point... mmm, water.
Audio: Wow. The voice acting is actually better than a certain bad game about motorcycles and revenge... at least they attempt to bring life to the voices instead of simply reading off a script... mostly. Water sounds? Sounds realistic enough. And that´s all that matters in this game. Water.
Summary: If you enjoy swimming, drowning and shooting in third person then this is for you. I actually would recommend this game, despite the flaws I had some fun out of it and the cringy dialogue made me keep going to hear more bad lines. Worth the full price? Hell no. Wait for a price drop or a sale, then buy it.

This game is right on the edge of what I can recommend. It is a Diablo-Siege clone, albeit less polished. Like its predecessors, it does offer a wealth of character upgrade options, and different looking weapons and armor. Combat is more or less typical of the genre, so if these are qualities you enjoy in a game, I would recommend it. I certainly enjoyed playing it for quite a few hours.
However, there is definitely plenty wrong with the game. My personal caveats:
1. The UI is very clunky. Menus don't scroll all the way to the bottom, quest logs don't automatically take you to your active quest, and the font can make numbers difficult to make out (can't count how many times I wasn't sure if I was looking at a lvl 23 vs a lvl 28 item).
2. Gameplay is not very smooth. Movement is erratic, especially if you are holding LMB to move. Sometimes a piece of scenery way above the ground level will get under your mouse, and your character will move very unpredictably (often straight into monsters I was trying to avoid). And the view panning never felt elegant. I always felt like I was lugging around this terrible camera man, and waiting for him to get into position so I could see where I was going.
3. RP opportunities are few and not great. There are some decent companion interactions that were well scripted, but they don't seem to have any purpose other than flavor. The only mechanical RP elements I could find were "science vs nature" themed, which were just awful. The choices were always so absurdly binary ("do you want to destroy entire eco-systems or completely trash all technological conveniences?"), it was hard to take them seriously, and I just picked whichever had the talent choies I wanted.

The game itself is fantastic. The world is well crafted, the voice acting is sweet, and the graphics and animation don't feel outdated at all.
However this pc port is borderline unplayable due to the constant stutters, especially when player is in a vehicle (which gave me motion sickness). I have researched a little and it seems that the pc port may have optimization issue.
For reference, my system has r5 1600 cpu and gtx 1060 with standard 16g ram. The game is installed on a standard 1t WD blue hard drive. I don't think the hardwares are at fault since more hardware intense titles can run significantly more stable compared to this.
Again, the game itself is great fun, but I recommand you to immediately test its performance on your pc and refund it if you experience any stuttering issues, since it seems to run fine for most people here judging by the comments.
Also it requires Uplay. If there ever was an excuse for pirating games (not saying there is), it would be Uplay.
Do yourself a favor; get a gamecube ROM version of this game and play it on dolphin.

This game has some incredible visuals, the open world is beautiful to just wander around and immerse yourself in. I'm loving this game!
First let me do some comparison.  If you read the reviews you'll see alot of comparisons to L4D.  And with good reason.  4 player squad fighting your way through hordes of enemies to go from A-B.  Pretty simple.  And like L4D there are hordes of standard, easily dispatched, mobs.  With special enemies that closely resemble the specials from L4D.  There are "events" that occur much like in L4D.  In general the pace and flow of the game are the same.
The differences are in the nature of the RPG aspect of Vermintide.  Instead of all the weapons being dispersed throughout the level Vermintide has permanent gear.  So as you complete missions you have the oppurtunity to roll for new weapons and trinkets.  And there is an added "Forge" where you can upgrade the gear to get even better stuff.  However getting really good gear takes time and much grinding.  There are 5 characters to choose from, each with their own sets of weapon types.  And while each charater could be a general fighting class, the gear allows you to change up fighting styles so you can find a more comfortable niche to play through.  I prefer the Witch Hunter with a Rapier, and Crossbow.  But I could use a two-handed sword and dual pistols.  You get the idea.  So very much UNlike L4D, there is a sense of progessing your characters.  If you are willing to put in the time for grinding at the "Normal" setting and moving up to "Hard" eventually, and more difficulty settings, then you will have something to show for it.
The level development is a delight for me.  Straightforward enough so you don't get lost tryng to learn the levels, but with plenty of hidden closets, and alleyways containing the possiblity of support, or healing items.  And the atmosphere for each level is dark and forboding.  Perfect for the story setting.  I also want to mention there are more levels than L4D.  So even though you will be running the same levels eventually to grind for gear, there are enough levels so that they don't too old, too fast.
I've owned this game for less than a week, and I'm 20+ hours into it.  I definitely see myself adding several hundred more.

Reviewing Boson X

This really is an overlooked simple but well made little game. I noticed and picked up Boson X when it appeared in the weekly offers at -90% on the Steam store, less than a year after release and that was clearly a steal. It's a small rotational platform runner title that clearly went unnoticed and despite being fairly short and lacking much content, it's definitely worth picking up when on sale, if not at full price.
Most of the low priced little indie titles on Steam aren't well realized, or come with too many problems to be worth the hassle, but Boson X is short and comes together really nicely. It's polished more than you'd expect and the sound and especially the music in particular is worth noting for being fast paced, at times thumping, and fun, while also tying into the levels really well.
The entire game is packaged under a scientific theme of physics, and from the chemistry lab looking title screen which reminded me of Half-Life 2 and Portal, to the physicist and particle references, it's themed subtly but well and compliments the gameplay.
The random placement of the platforming elements falling into place along with the randomized directions, speeds and distances of certain things all make for a changing difficulty and unpredictable level. Some of the earlier and later levels in particular can be both easy and very challenging in the same playthrough, and it added a small level of that "want to play again" and "just one more try" feeling.
There are some annoyances with this title, but at the price and length they're mostly forgiveable, but more so they don't actively break the game and don't take away very much overall.
As mentioned, there's a nice level of unpredictability built in by the random selection of speeds, times and platform locations which probably adds more than it takes away, but at times it's definitely more annoying than if the section had been given fixed timings. Dying at the same sections because there's no way to predict the placement of a block up ahead, or crossing lightning paths which may make it impossible to chose a safe direction are frustrating more than they need to be and should have had more attention spent on at least making them more fluid. In short, the game is often unfair, and that's the last thing you want in a game involving precision, timing and player planning.
The other complaint is the lack of content or length of gameplay which clocks in at an average of around 5-6 hours, which is great value for money, but because the mechanics are fairly flat, even unexciting at a push, it means there isn't anything to make you go wow or keep you engaged for very long. The developer has mentioned all the open license libraries and given links to the engine and more in the file directory, presumably to encourage modding/development, but Steam Workshop is a common request and honestly would've added a lot to this title, it's a shame it hasn't been added.
Fully priced, Boson X is available on Steam at just £1.99/2.99€/$2.99 and with an average gameplay length of 5-6 hours, it's great value for money. It's also regularly on sale for as much as 90% off, which makes it nearly free. It's probably not going to rock your socks off and keep you playing, and if you have a long backlog it might be worth missing out on, but at the price it's a fine pick up for anyone taking an interest from the store page.

It's not DiRT Rally 2, it's not meant to be DiRT Rally 2 and it doesnt feel like DiRT Rally 2.
This is a continuation of DiRT 3 and is more arcade-y and has more varied racing disciplines than DiRT Rally. DiRT 4 is a more fun racing game which is also very capable of being a simulator. The multiplayer has been improved on (thank goodness for push to talk, no more always-on microphone in multiplayer. ) and the addition of being able to create your own team is great.
One thing though, there's now more Outbreak! There is no more Hoonigan/Gymkhana stuff in DiRT 4 and therefore no more Outbreak, which is a real shame. This was in my opinion the most enjoyable multiplayer gamemode and i wish Codemasters would add it back in. They have the map for it, the DirtFish area, which is plenty large and has some obstacle to hide behind.
If you're looking for a racing game that's perhaps not as serious as DiRT Rally but also not as arcade-y as Need for Speed, this game is for you. You can make DiRT 4 as difficult or as easy to control as you want and will provide fun for the casual and the hardcore player alike.

I enjoyed the first Hotline Miami. It was difficult, but for the most part it was fun; and the story, while fairly barebones, was interesting. It's not my favorite game in the world, but I liked it enough to replay it, and to go back and replay levels to get higher scores, achievements, etc. I have absolutely no interest in ever replaying Hotline Miami 2.
Story-wise, the game is a confused and confusing mess. It kind of seems like the developers wanted to tell a story about the consequences of your rampage in the first game, but not everything connects to that, and it's hard to follow what's going on when you're playing about ten different characters at different points in the game.
That being said, story isn't the main focus of these games; the action is. But that's problematic as well. First of all, each of the characters you play as throughout the game have their own special mechanic. Some of these are cool, some of them suck, but the real problem is that (1) you're never given any indication what that mechanic is and (2) you don't get enough time with any one character to really get used to it. One character will not use guns, and disassembles any you pick up. Another has a dodge-roll. Others will only use the weapons they start with.
The levels in this game are also far longer than in the original, which can be infuriating in a game where you die in one hit. I never felt like the first game was really unfair (except maybe during the boss fights), but the second one constantly seems like you're getting screwed. Also, the most annoying thing from the first game (those big enemies that can only be killed with guns) are back, but now there's also another enemy type that can only be killed with a melee weapon, and a third enemy type that can only be killed by throwing a weapon at them and then beating them while they're on the floor. Again, there is nothing in the game to prepare you for this, and you WILL die the first time you encounter them.
Even the music is not as good as in the original. Overall, it's just a disappointing sequel.

A lot better and not nearly as disappointing as some claim to be. The mechanics, story and even music are much better than the first game, the only thing I can think of that doesn't live up to the already great original is the level design. It's good, but not as well crafted as Hotline 1. That being said, it's still a phenomenal game and the soundtrack is unparalleled.

Played this game for the first time since its release...still disappointed
TL;DR check the bottom.
Details why not to buy, please read.
When I first got it, the game crashed on startup, it had permanent letterbox settings, and a set framerate of 30. The only way one could fix the latter two was to enable console and rewrite portions of it. Luckily I bought this at a local store and they gave me a refund because so many others had been bringing back copies.
Today I figured these things had been fixed and I'd give it a whirl while collecting its cards, and not much has changed. Now that I can have fullscreen and 60 FPS set as options (Seriously, why give these as options and not default? You're not Ubisoft, Bethesda, just getting close) I can play without crashing. That doesn't mean the following problems still exist:
1. The controls still are terrible like it was before. Pretty sure this was originally designed for console/controller and just cheaply redone for PC. Best buy a controller for this game unless you want to feel like you're in a g-force simulator or like watching the world spin.
2. Story. Bad. People who write negative reviews and get crap because of little play time surprisingly aren't wrong. Watched a lot of walkthrough vids on this and was let down. Nothing new at all in the horror genre.
3. Voice acting. Remember the funny videos poking fun at the voice acting in the Final Fantasy series? Yup. Same thing here.
4. Sneaking. You can't shoot while sneaking. You may think that's whatever but if you have the patience to read this far, I'll explain. "Why sneak when firing a gun?" Good question. Firing a pistol at one guy surprisingly doesn't draw much attention from others sound-wise. If you stand up, however, you're screwed. You can throw a bottle while crouching, though I wouldn't recommend it because...
5. Sneaking is horrible. Here is why. So remember in Oblivion, Skyrim, Fallout, and other games that sneaking was a big deal in and had the cool eye icon? This has that, but instead of the half-eye indicating you're being hunted and the full-eye meaning you're found, half- eye now means "Hey, there's an enemy nearby" which WOULD be helpful if you were deaf and couldn't hear them growling constantly. So you're going to be sneaking and suddenly that eye's going to pop wide and you're screwed without warning. You could throw a bottle AT them, though they often sidestep it and it won't allow you to lock on like with pistols for some reason, so good luck with that. You could distract them with it and sneak kill, which sometimes but rarely works because...
6. Overall combat is horrible. Traps, bullets, sneaking, and all the cool things listed in the trailer are utter crap when trying. You have a gun, yet limited ammo, and no melee except spamming the "f" key which will end up getting you more damaged than the monster you're fighting. You're going to be doing more sneaking than fighting because the defense setup is basically "Hey, we're going to give you things to make you feel safe, but actually it just draws attention and leaves half-headed creatures still rushing you to pistol-whip for the next 2 minutes". Pray to God you don't get caught without a weapon or ammo because...
7. Escaping is a joke. You're a top notch cop with tons of experience, right? But in the second chapter, you're going to be briefly chased by a horde to which you must run from...except your sprint lasts maybe 2-3 seconds, which has to be a record for lowest hero endurance. Once you finally reach you're safe point and prepare yourself to fight them off, it goes to a cutscene to where your guy pulls some hardcore parkour, shooting and pushing enemies away like no big deal. Basically, you're going to be sneaking and scraping by just to watch clips of you doing awesome things.
Look, I was super stoked for this game when I heard about it. "Bethesda" and "Mastermind of Resident Evil" sells well, which would be good if they stepped up to their legacy. Look at the little tools and synergies in this game and tell me where else you've seen them from ol Bethesda and tell me they're "good" or "better" when they were fine as is. Look at the Keeper and Laura, two villains in here and tell me where else you remember seeing a big dude with a giant meat pounder and apron...or a creepy, skinny, long-black-hair-in-front-of-the-face girl before? Saying this game is good because of Shinji is like saying every Hellraiser movie and the Jericho game was good just because it had Clive Barker's name listed (it wasn't).
So now you're going "OK, wise guy, tell me what's survival horror game you're drooling over that I should get". Simple. Anything that actually involves you surviving and being horrified in trying to do so. Example? Outlast. No weapons, only a nightvision camera with limited power in an asylum full of people wanting to do their own thing to you. You will hide, run, and use strategy in trying to escape...and will actually feel helpless in trying to do so. How did the developers make this not so popular game work so well? Here's how: They used NO concepts like The Evil Within and didn't throw titles or names trying to make it sound better.
TL;DR
Get Outlast and its DLC. It's cheaper, scarier, you feel actual fear, and you don't have to deal with bull♥♥♥♥♥♥that a glorified company and the Shinji name should have delivered but didn't.
