The biggest thing I can say about Hydrophobia is that it's damn short. At under three hours, it's one of the shortest commercial releases I know of. It's a third-person shooter with a bit of Uncharted-style climbing, a hacking minigame, and a surprise gameplay twist near the end I won't spoil here, simply because it comes literally out of nowhere. I bought the game about three years ago and never touched it before today, but it proved a satisfying diversion. Hydrophobia is most notable for its water physics- player character Kate Wilson, a systems engineer, is aboard a massive oceangoing vessel in the midst of a terrorist attack, and nearly every area is at least partially flooded. This can be used to the player's advantage, triggering bulkhead breaches to toss enemies about in addition to the more genre-standard exploding barrels and exposed electrical currents. The swimming controls are competent and you have a generous oxygen meter, although the camera can be disorienting. Uniquely, you can grab objects such as crates while underwater and use them as portable cover. You have only one gun, a pistol, but it can be used with five different ammuntion types, including remote-trigger grenades. Hydrophobia succeeds better as an entire game about water levels then most games do in a single segment, and on that merit alone I can recommend it. It seems this title was  the first episode of a series, but the developer has since closed without further episodes being made and this title ends on an extremely abrupt cliffhanger. If that doesn't bother you however, Hydrophobia will make for an enjoyable afternoon.

It's like Left for Dead 2 with maces and crossbows instead of .45 Glocks and baseball bats. Like L4D2, the AI bots aren't the best in the world and it's much easier to play with a friend or three because they tend to focus on things they shouldn't, like enemies behind you when there's an Ogre in your face. It is possible to play with a full bot team, but be prepared to basically babysit them as you go through a map completing objectives. Unlike L4D2, you can upgrade your equipment between missions and even swap them out for new items. Or, if you really don't want a particular piece, you can smelt it down into upgrade crystals at the forge, which you can use towards getting a better item. Also, unlike L4D2, there are five characters, each with their own play style. Are you a sword and flintlock pistol type of man? Grab the Witchhunter. Do you like Dwarves and want to bash everything with your shield or a very large hammer? Grab the Holdseeker. Want to burn everything in your path? Grab the Bright Wizard. Like L4D2, the characters will talk to each other during a mission and will comment on their skill (or lack thereof). Also, like L4D2, the maps can get a bit repetitive, especially when it comes to gathering up enough crystals for better loot. Hopefully Fat Shark will address this in future DLC. I certainly recommend it for the asking price because you'll easily get 40+ hours of gameplay out of it and it's half of what most AAA games run when they're released. If you're worried about the investment, just wait for a Steam sale and grab it then, you won't be disappointed.

Aeon Command developed by Bat Country Games & released on 3rd July 2014 for the PC version. It has an average user score of 6.8 on Metacritic
& is categorized under the "Strategy" genre.
You'd be surprised to find out that Bat Country Game is an independent game company comprising of only  2 developer. Does Aeon Command live up to it's promises? Marketed as a strategy space game, collect resources and fight among 3 faction to take control of Aeon Nebula. As a RTS *PC* gamer, I will cry foul over the game's description but coming from a mobile device gamer, I certainly welcome Aeon Command. Does that sound confusing? Read on to be enlightened!
The controls are very simple. You can play the entire game by just using Mouse clicks. You also have keyboard shortcut keys to execute production of units/skills on the fly.
The visuals are just fine for me. This is a 2D space battle game. The space background & the ambient sound sets the tone for being in space. Each faction will have different designs of ships. Each ship will have different animations and audio for their weapons. The User Interface is kept simple and clean. Nothing fancy/cluttered.
The Story
As the game is marketed, there is  3 faction to choose from in the campaign mode, each having 8 levels - so making it a total of 24 levels. At the beginning of each level, you will be given a balloon message that describes the story@scenario to you - and what follows after that is..well a tug of war of endless wave of space crafts.
You practically try to overwhelm your enemy by mass producing space crafts and the ships will fly to the other end of the map trying to blow up the other faction's mother ship by themselves. You have no ability to control them. You only can decide the sequence of space craft to build. That's it. It is a 1 Lane tug of war and the best part is that you will be doing the same exact thing for 24 times regardless of the "story".
Sure, there are a few levels with twist in the story, take for an example where you have to survive for x minute against the cyborg faction who are sending endless suicidal crafts. After X minute, you'll have to eliminate them.  It's just sending 1,000,000 space craft to the other side of the map. for 24 times! Do not be mistaken, this is not a MOBA or Tower defense. The exact description would be a 1 Lane control. That's it.
You must be wondering how is this even possible for a game with such dull, uninteresting, repetitive game play is receiving "very positive" feedbacks on steam? For a RTS fan, you certainly would be utterly disappointed. There is very little "Strategy" involved. It's designed to be as a macro level management kind of game. One that is more suited/geared towards casual gamers. Its "fun" when you can overwhelm your opponent with 1 gazillion space craft. especially on multiplayer.
Aeon Command gives players the option to upgrade your space crafts and also your factions(think of it like a faction bonus). The spacecraft may look and feel different however they will always remain in the same "type of class" for every faction.
Your first space craft will always be a close range combat craft followed by a long range craft and then a support craft (healing/shield/disabler etc). It may feel slightly different from each faction but that's the general concept. It's not like starcraft/warcraft/red alert/supreme commander where you really have different kind of units! Even plant vs Zombie has more "strategy". I am sorry but that's how I feel/see this product as.
On multiplayer, you have  3 game mode:
I don't understand the minor differences in Close and Resources mode. Is this the best the design could come up with? The game engine limitation? If this was a tug of war, the close mode is like having a shorter rope by an inch and for the resource mode, you can have endless of people to pulling the rope. It may sound like a visible idea but in reality, the result doesn't mean anything! There is no difference in strategy/approach of playing. I always perform the same step - across all faction - on all level difficulty.
My Summary
Aeon Command is a straightforward game - which can be fun - however for any serious RTS fan, stay clear of this title, it is not what it's marketed to be. For me, the story is non-existent. There is little strategy. No, I dont take upgrades as strategy. The game play was uninteresting. Some flash games could even provide me with better gaming experience/fun. Overall, I had a dull gaming experience. Do I want to see another game made with this concept/game design? No! On the scale of 0 - 10, my personal rating for Aeon Command is a 4/10.
I am sorry Bat Country Game, you'd have to do better than this. The product feels like a flash game with uninteresting value. No replay value. No challenge. A proper follow-up to 2012's Hotline Miami featuring better music and continuation of the story. If you thought Hotline Miami was difficult then you better prepare yourself. The difficulty curve is almost nonexistant. It starts out really difficult and ends on brutally hard levels. This can be attributed to the layout of the levels. However, Hotline Miami 2 features larger levels with more enemies with guns and plenty of glass for them so see you thorugh. That being said, there are going to a lot of off-screen deaths you will not see.
The music and the story was enough to keep me going but man, that difficulty had me angrier than the first one. Fans of the first game will likely enjoy Hotline Miami 2. If you haven't played the first one, I highly suggest doing so. You will be missing a signinficant part of the story and the easier levels that will gradually help you with Hotline Miami 2. Hotline Miami is also dirt cheap so there is really no excuse.

I'm going to make this as clear as possible to avoid misunderstanding: THIS GAME ISN'T BAD.
Now, but why do I rate it down if I don't think it's bad? Well, because it's a bad sequel to the original game. Really, this game should've just been DLC for HM1, but come on - it's Hotline Miami - people would go NUTS if there was a sequel to the critically-acclaimed game!
Well, they made a second one, and I'm sure they genuinely tried to improve on the first game, but they took wrong steps at every turn. It's a tough cookie, so I'll put it down simply:
But unfortunately, that's where all the good stops.
My main gripe with this game is the level designs. Wide-open spaces. Long open corridors, huge rooms, and so on and so forth. The design is more realistic, sure, but I see a shotgun blast coming from the side of the screen before I even see an enemy, and that just pisses me off. Even with the shift function of looking around, the levels are so big that you at times cannot see them and are forced to restart multiple times in order to get around these. This isn't me raging about dying a lot - that I can handle - but when I die because my character was so blind that he couldn't see 20 ft in front of him, that's when I'm upset, because there's nothing I could do to prevent that.
There's other stuff like soundtrack and stuff, but that is minor compared to the glaring issue. I can only recommend this game to those who must play more Hotline Miami. Otherwise, if you are meh about the first game, this game can definitely wait until a sale.

Sadly, the game is passed its prime. There are too many similar and complete games out right now to justify pvkii. I put several hundred hours into this game; I LOVED this game, but I simply can't bring myself to get back into it. The most disappointing facet about this game is the level of support the game has gotten.
I get it, games take time, money and energy to make. It's a fact that probably doesn't get noticed nearly enough these games. The game has been out for over half a decade now and still has not managed to release half of the classes that were planned from the beginning. Each update has become more and more underwhelming as time goes on. When the game first came out, there was only one class per team. They were unbalanced and buggy, but they had personality and synergised well together. Later updates brought variety, engagement and even a complete overhauls of game mechanics. The game began a bit of a decent by the release of 2.3, which is a bit odd for me to say because i probably had the most fun during 2.3.
2.3 brought a new class, an updated engine and multiple bug fixes, but it had one flaw. 2.3  allowed player to choose between a manual and automatic block function. This may not seem like much to someone looking in from the outside, but modern game communities are finicky about the games that they've put so many hours into. Imagine, if you will, a game suck as Counter-strike 1.6 added some sort of option that reduced the amount of damage that a headshot inflicted; but, at the same time, increased how much damage a body shot would do. This would drasticly reduce the learning curve for new players, while leaving the game unaltered for the die hard veterans that have been eating and breathing this game for the past decade. You could balance the damage figures perfectly and draw all of the graphs you wanted, but the veterans are not going to like the fact that the skills they have honed have now been made slightly less effective so that some filthy pesant  with a brand new copy can feel accomplished. A small change that forever alters the way that the game is seen. Manual blocking was still the default option, even preferred by some of those old pvkii vets, but auto-block gave new players an arguably unearned and uneven playing field. This seemingly insignificant change drove a spike through the community.
And this brings me to the a very taboo topic in pvkii. The "community." Some will tell you that the community is in ashes. Some will tell you that the community is just fine. All can agree on the same thing, the community has gotten SMALLER. I, personally, won't be going into the specifics about the sociology behind the pvkii community because i wouldn't be able to progress beyond a ramble that leads to nothing productive. Instead, I'll bring up the previously mentioned issue, the spike that drove the community apart. Modern gaming is leaning towards a sort of bipartisan: "Core" gamers and "Casual" gamers. "Veterans" and "Noobs." "People that play more than me" and "People that play less than me." "12 years olds" and "12 year olds." The core guys bring stability to the community and the new comers bring life. Neither are perfect but both are vital. When the barely sentient guy that just installed the game manages to get a lucky hit on someone who has the pvkii logo tattooed on his forehead for so long that the ink is starting to seep into his brain and cause mood swings, two things happen. One: the new guy tells his friends, they tell their friends, who tell their friends and so on until, you got a reputable pack of these little poobrains wobbling about mashing the m1 button so hard that Razor's share holders are starting to get nervous and Two: the hardcore players lock themselves away in a single server so that they can beat each other over the head with their erect♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and talk about how good they are compared to everyone else while comparing size in peace. These two rabbles are what we have now, and what have to be appeased.
Updates after 2.3 left much to be desired. New voice overs for every class were added, leading to the reactions "WTF I LIKE THE OLD ONES" from the vets and "Oh cool, this game has voice acting" from the new guys. A new class was added, considered "lame and game breaking" by some and "easy to kill if you're not an idiot" buy others. Some old maps were taken out and put back in, leaving everyone to wonder where that balanced class was that was supposed to be added 3 patches ago. It seems nothing the poor devs can do makes anyone happy anymore for more than 2 seconds. The voices conflict each other 9 times out of ten, and it's a shame to see it all for nothing. So much love has been put into this project, that much is apparent just by booting it up and listening to the theme music. So why can't I give this game another chance? Why can't I find enjoyment in something so beautiful and unique and amazing since there's so much love smeared all over it?
A while ago, the game released a ranged class. This was the first exclusivly ranged-focused class added to the game. The devs balanced the archer by handing out arrow blocking shields like expired candy to pretty much everyone else. It took some skill and getting used to before you could manage anything with it. Naturally, as change tends to do, everyone was enraged for one reason or another. The other guys saw the utility of this archer class and the new guys hated every second that they couldn't play one. A few updates later, a NEW ranged class was added to the game. You know what they forgot? Anti-ranged classes. And i don't mean classes that have a really good chance against archers when they're right on top of them. I mean some kind of stealth unit that can sneak up behind rangers and one-shot back stab them. Something that totally obliterates archers and sharpshooters when used by a competent player. Something that makes you NOT WANT TO PLAY A RANGED CLASS. Naturally, these units would be completely destroyed by melee units and thus you achieve balance.
Now we run into the heart of the problem. We have a simple problem with a simple solution. Finish what was started, the world keeps spinning. But the problem isn't being solved. Updates have been excruciatingly slow, and depressing when they finally do get here. The most recent class, the Sharpshooter, isn't nearly as up-to-par as all of the other classes. Its another backpetalling archer with slightly more speed than you and seemingly unlimited ammunition. Without a counter class, my frustration with this game is doubled. Don't get me wrong, I like the idea of an Archer class and a Sharpshooter class and even the idea of having to find a way of dealing with them as a melee class. What i don't like is having to fight ranged classes and melee classes at the same time constantly. You've got two voices coming from the community. One says "U GUYS IM LIKE SUPR GUD AT RANGR YOLO420SWAGSNIPERWOLFNARUTO4EVER" and "No, it's easy. You've just got to use your shield and kite around this rock and run all the way around and wait until he's not paying attention and change classes 2 or 3 times and shoot him in the face. It's easy." (That is, IF you can hear them over the sound of errect♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥slapping against foreheads and keyboards.) I get it, you can get around them by kiting and shielding. I've done it many times. ITS NOT FUN.  I also get that you can start a fire with a stick and a rock, but that didn't stop matches from catching on. So two voices are left. Counter the rangers or don't counter the rangers. I get it, updates are in progress, these things take time blah blah blah, but the game play has been deteriorated. With a majority of the blocking mechanic has been practically removed and pure melee fighting nearly unheard of anymore, the melee combat is basic and unenjoyable. Balance it and i'll give it another try. Melee based games need fun melee combat.

At the beginning I was really enjoying Hydrophobia.  It had a nice post apocalyptic/dystopian feel about it, and lets be honest, the water effects are increadible.  But water doesn't make necessarily make a compelling world - just ask Kevin Costner.
The narative is pretty much 'by the book' stuff, even down to the heard but not seen accomplice who helps you as you begin your escape, right up until he decides to bail and leaves you on your own, but that's not an issue as you're quite self sufficient.  There are a few tricky puzzles, and choosing which ammunition to use during combat can certainly make these things easier or harder as you go along.
There are destrucible parts of the environment (power cables) that you can use to make your life easier - and we all know what happens when electricity hits water...
But all this enjoyment came to an abrupt end with the final battle.  It's cheap, it's annoying, it's frustrating but most of all, it let the story down.  I could have forgiven that battle if it actually tied into the narative, but it feels cheap and tacked on which is a real pity.
I will recommend this game, as I did enjoy it overall, but it did leave a bad taste right at the end.
Look, if you are going to buy this game, don't.

I'd easily recommend this game. Only about halfway through at the moment, but it looks, sounds and plays wonderfully. The main protagonist is a bit hamfisted, but so was leon. I want a game where I shoot someone in the head and it is just like a Tom Savini special effects special. It's literally like planet terror in terms of the effects. I love it. The sound design is amazing too, the first time you hear the lightning of the 3rd act, well, spot on. and let's not forget the lighting in general. Easily the best looking lighting I've ever seen in a game.
The pacing is good, and it's a mixed bag in terms of how some of the levels play. You can really feel the influence of the past legends with this game. The story might be a little crazy, but I like it. It's enough to be there, yet not cast too long a shadow.
I especially like the upgrade system too, and the game obviously rewards exploration. Especially early on you have nothing, and smart play really gets rewarded too. I found myself torn between what to upgrade, and honestly any route would have been decent. It's flexible and and choice is a good route to go depending how you play.
Regarding rehashing the past, sometimes the game doesn't need to create something completely new, but do something old very well. I think it does just that.
Again, can't  stress how beautiful the game is, sounds, and how well it plays. Worth every penny.

Polished visually, completely lacking in refinement. This game is ultimately a ruse. A mirage. At first glance it's beautiful. Visually, the combination of good graphics and Cel Shading is stunning. Quickly, however the true gamer realizes the actual gameplay is flawed beyond reproach. Lackluster clunky combat, an archaic quest system and VERY liminted voice acting make this game mediocre at best. A poor ecuse for an action RPG, and a poor excuse for either genre, period.
The combat barely passes as a Diablo clone. The camera options, while involved, are seemingly limited, scarring the experience at every turn. Choose one angle, you'll be doomed to limited view, choose another, you'll be thrust into a pseudo-3d world. Any camera you choose limits the experience.
Couple this with repetetive combat and repetetive gameplay. I.E. NO puzzle solving, no clickable objects. Basically, you kill, kill kill, LEVEL up, add stats,. collect loot, KILL some more repeat.
There are some notable points of interest. They have graciously added in their desperate quest to copy Diablo, more options for loot...you can get yellow, green, blue white AND artifact (brown and rarest) loot types. Beyond this, Silverfall is a hack and slash nightmare...it will remind you of all the cliches of a game of this genre, while satisfying next to none of those expectations.
Expect the expected with Silverfall. Expect the predictable. Barely worth the price of admission.

Previously wrote a review in which I did recommend the game however in light of the last update, I deleted said review in favour of this one.
I DO NOT RECOMMEND this game at all.
Developers felt that the already crazy grind (made shorter by spending real money for unlocks/veteran membership) was not making them enough money, so they now increased the amt of time by at least 75%, in some ribbon (perk/weapon xp) cases, more than 400%.
Why is this such a problem?
Well you see, there are many players who have been around since the beginning, or at least for a year, and in those builds, the time required to grind out certain NECESSARY perks, weapons, mods was a FRACTION of what it is today.
That means that you will get put into games where you're up against guys with fully modded out one hit kill weapons, top tier tanks, and most importantly gold level badges that give them a huge advantage over you.
What's that really matter, if I shoot someone with my rifle, they're gonna die, so who cares you say?
Well, that's just it....your gun will NOT kill them in one shot (unless you headshot them) where as their gun will kill you in one shot.  Even if you DO happen to grind out all the necessary experience to unlock all the mods required (and they cost a fkn ton of credits - in game currency- ) you STILL won't be able to one shot kill a lot of the "vets" because they have the Heavyset Gold badge (a perk that allows you to take 15% less damage)
Well big deal, right?  After a few weeks, I can grind it out and be on a level playing field, right?
NOPE.  Only if you some how are able to cram in 400+ hours of game time into those 2 weeks.
Reto has literally gone full retard with this last update, blatantly playing the greed card in an effort to coerce any new player or player who wants to unlock weapons/vehicles/mods in order to enhance their playing experience (basically, even the playing field) to spend hundreds of dollars.
Even if you DO spend the necessary money/gold to unlock a weapon or vehicle...you cannot pay to unlock/progress the mod/badges that play such a vital role in the efficiency of your character/weapon/vehicle.  You can only do that by grinding the exp, by killing enemy after enemy or driving around for literally 20+ hours.
Oh, think you've found a smart way to get exp, by just shooting your gun into the air for an entire match?  Driving around in circles?  Cycling a bike for 30+ min?  Nope, that's "EXPLOITING" and for that you can enjoy a PERMANENT BAN.   I'm not even making this stuff up.
I haven't even TOUCHED on the other negatives of this game, which there are a few.
-matchmaking is completely absent - you'll get put in games that are almost over, located on the other side of the planet, one team is STACKED while the other is newbs
-graphics are subpar, not what you see in the trailers at all
-optimization issues galore
-terrible menuing interface, since the game uses browser plugins
-movement and gravity feels like you're on the moon, not Earth
-vehicles drive/fly like they're just bricks with wheels/treads/wings
-it costs credits to maintain your weapons/mods and replenish ammo.  You have a KDR of 30:1 and an objective score of 10 caps and still actually come out in a credit deficit, making it a ridiculous treadmill to try to save up enough credits to buy new weapons (assuming you have the patience to unlock them)
Honestly, the game was fun for a while, because it's been so long since I've played a combined arms WW2 game...but the novelty has worn off, the glaring faults have shone through, and most of all, the developer has shown their true colours.
My only regret is giving them any money at all, as scumbaggery like this should not be rewarded in any form.
Hopefully another developer out there will see what H&G has done and how badly they've dropped the ball and fill the demand for a good, balanced, fair, PREMIUM tactical combined arms WW2 shooter.

Wakfu is a fun and adventurous game. It has turn based battle style fighting, a huge and expanding open world, interesting mob monsters (little birds called tofus- if you're vegitarian you won't want these Tofurkeys, Bow Meows, Treechnids, lots of weird stuff). Its a player run game, with 5 different governments that players can be elected into. Bonta, Amanka, Brackmar, and Sufokia cough cough Sufokia being the best, of course cough cough are the four land owning governments. The fifth is a group called the Riktus Clan who are sort of a pirate/rogue group who go around and wreck shop and steal land. You join one of the land owning countries at level 18 or so, and later get the option to join Riktus, if you're so inclined, aroud level 35.
The best way to level up is to scour the many dungeons scattered across each country, and the neutral lands (ex Astrub, The Sadida Kingdom, and other such islands found on the map). Getting into the dungeon itself provides a challenge as you have to fight area monsters to get keys or ingredients to make keys to get in. Each player requires a key to get in. Groups are suggested for dungeons, though you can use a 'sidekick' which is basically a second character you control. Sidekicks require you to use a key as well, as they count as a second person linked to yourself. At the end of a dungeon you earn experience, items and tokens which allow you to buy other items from a machine outside said dungeon. Those items from the machine are linked to your player character. You can also run the dingeon multiple times to get all the items from a set without them being linked (most times).
Then there are things that I consider 'sub classes' that help you make pretty much anything in the game. These jobs allow you to make armor, weapons, furniture for your havenbag/home, accessories, food, etc. They are on their own leveling system unrelated to your characters level. The CRAFTING professions are: A.O.E Weapons Master, Armorer, Baker, Chef, Close Combat Weapons Master, Handyman, Kama Minter, Leather Dealer, Long Distance Weapons Master, Jeweler, and Tailor at the time of this review. There are also GATHERING Professions, which help you get the ingredients for crafting. GATHERING Professions are: Lumberjack, Herbalist, Miner, Fisherman, Trapper, and Farmer. These professions also offer unique items to craft, though are best leveled up by actually gathering things.
This game is very time consuming.
But fun as all get out.
In this game there are a lot of guilds. When I say a lot I mean, like, over 500. Many may be in disuse or inactive, but there are a lot of options out there. Look into the guilds and join one that makes you comfortable, you can always make one of your own if you want to. Guilds provide boosts you can't earn without being part of a guild. Stuff like increased HP or damage for a certain element, depending on the guild level and amount of points they've earned. Guilds have 3 daily quests that grant 15-20 points per quest per character that does them. You also earn small amounts of guild points just doing whatever if you're grouped up with members from your guild- like the little environmental quests (like kick 10 Gobball Balls or stomp some weeds type things), running through more than one dungeon (though the one daily quest for that grants 20 each time after grants a few points too). You can always leave a guild as well, f it no longer suits your playstyle, though you will lose all related bonuses.
On the topic of dailies; there is a temple called the temple of almanax. It has 4 doors correlating to the seasons inside, and once a day you go to 'pray' to the merida of the day. It grants a token that allows you to buy cool stuff like costumes or a pet or haven bag upgrades, something like 10,000 exp, and a randomized bonus (something like +40 Wisdom or +30 HP and other things like that. the bonuses last one hour of gameplay).
Theres so much in the game, it is really worth it to give it a few hours to try, it is free after all. Theres also a user-run wiki for Wakfu that covers a bunch of stuff and is always expanding (albeit slowly sometimes). Theres also Ankama's site that has more info on specifics as well.
All in all, its worth a try at the very least. Its fun, its enjoyable, and its free (though you CAN choose to spend some real cash if you really want, but you don't have to)

Ok, this review is aimed at my old KF1 (and KF2 I guess) buddies. Essentially Vermintide places you in the fantasy Warhammer setting and has you fighting your way from point A to point B, using a combination of melee and ranged weapons to survive attacks along the way. Your melee attacks work really well, with a good dodge/push/block/charged attack  system in place. The ranged weapons rely heavily upon finding ammunition so you need to use with care, but there are a wide range of weapons, each with their own strengths. Melee is definitely the focus however. In some ways it may seem similar to KF_Damnation, but dont let this put you off. I hate damnation, but really enjoy this.
What I really like is the reward system. You level up and receive new weapons and gear by successfully completing maps/missions. At the end of the mission, you roll a set of dice, and the more successful dice rolls, the better weapon or gear you will be rewarded with. The weapon goes into your inventory pool, and you can either equip it to the appropriate perked character, or you can 'mess' with it some more. "Messing' with it can be done in several ways. Firstly, you can try and change the weapons traits. I should explain. Weapons have bonus traits on them. For example, traits may give you healing when you hit something, or provide the chance of an instant kill, faster attack speed, leech ammo etc. There is also a percentage chance applied to this trait, so for example, my flame sword has a 10% chance of healing me for 5 hp when I hit something. So I can roll some dice and try and change the trait to a some other ability that I would like, or, roll a dice and try and improve the percentage associated with the current trait. It costs a few tokens to do this. Alternatively you can meld 5 weapons of one particular level, into 1 weapon of a higher quality. The final way to mess with the weapons is just to 'salvage' them and convert them to tokens. These tokens can be used to reroll traits on existing weapons, or be used to create entirely new weapons if you'd rather.
I should also add that the quality of the weapon/loot item you receive at the end of the mission can be influenced by picking up 'tomes' and 'grimoires' during play. These give your end of game dice a better chance of successful rolls, but make the mission harder by limiting your healing options and maximum health throughout. Essentially they allow you to set your risk/reward level as you play. Brilliant!
I really like that there is a real tangible reward for completing missions. Unlike with KF1/KF2, there is no level cap (that I am are aware of) so you can keep improving your 'cred' if that's important to you. More importantly though, you keep getting weapon/gear drops so can keep modifying and crafting new gear, forever improving and honing your characters loadout.
There are 5 perk/classes at the moment, but it feels like only 3 really. Each has basically 4 main melee and 4 main ranged weapons each for you to choose from, but as stated before, you can customise those with different traits to your liking.
The environments are great. Detailed, atmospheric, balanced; though there is not a huge amount of maps just yet. Some people will find this a bit repetitive but I'm not minding it so far. Shame there is no option for custom maps at this stage, but the quality of the developer maps would be hard to measure up to anyways. There is a good variety of enemies, and while OP at times, usually they can be dealt with providing team work remains the focus.
There is no dedicated server yet, so peeps can hop into your game at any time unless you designate your game as private. Good and bad I guess. Scenes can get pretty busy at times when you are facing a horde so my internet struggles when hosting. If you play on your own while waiting for someone to jump in, bots will take control of your other characters to help out along the way. They are not infallible for sure, and sometimes will run away and hide, or stand by doing nothing while you slowly bleed to death, but with care, they can be utilised reasonably effectively.
All in all, this game gives you a Killing Floor like team game, with an awesome setting and a great motivation/reward system. Recommended.

I think Landrush is the best discipline in this game but you can't compete with the default gearing the 4WD trucks have. They've managed to make the trucks both accelerate slowly because of the giant leap between 2nd and 3rd gear and be too slow at top speed. I don't usually like to fiddle around that much with the vehicle setups but changing the gearing of the 4WD trucks is a must.
This is my default gearing:
1st: 0.565
2nd: 0.790
3rd: 1.105 (max)
Final drive: 0.130
This will give you a top speed of 191km/h. You'll hit the redline at the end of the straights on most tracks but if you don't then change the final drive a bit. I've heard the spotter say "You gained over four seconds that lap" at 100% difficulty many times so I think it works. Besides the gearing I also lowered the vehicle to -25mm (min) to reduce body-roll but other than that I've changed nothing else.
I've only driven this game in simulation mode and it's quite good fun in that mode. Sadly, the game is passed its prime. There are too many similar and complete games out right now to justify pvkii. I put several hundred hours into this game; I LOVED this game, but I simply can't bring myself to get back into it. The most disappointing facet about this game is the level of support the game has gotten.
I get it, games take time, money and energy to make. It's a fact that probably doesn't get noticed nearly enough these games. The game has been out for over half a decade now and still has not managed to release half of the classes that were planned from the beginning. Each update has become more and more underwhelming as time goes on. When the game first came out, there was only one class per team. They were unbalanced and buggy, but they had personality and synergised well together. Later updates brought variety, engagement and even a complete overhauls of game mechanics. The game began a bit of a decent by the release of 2.3, which is a bit odd for me to say because i probably had the most fun during 2.3.
2.3 brought a new class, an updated engine and multiple bug fixes, but it had one flaw. 2.3  allowed player to choose between a manual and automatic block function. This may not seem like much to someone looking in from the outside, but modern game communities are finicky about the games that they've put so many hours into. Imagine, if you will, a game suck as Counter-strike 1.6 added some sort of option that reduced the amount of damage that a headshot inflicted; but, at the same time, increased how much damage a body shot would do. This would drasticly reduce the learning curve for new players, while leaving the game unaltered for the die hard veterans that have been eating and breathing this game for the past decade. You could balance the damage figures perfectly and draw all of the graphs you wanted, but the veterans are not going to like the fact that the skills they have honed have now been made slightly less effective so that some filthy pesant  with a brand new copy can feel accomplished. A small change that forever alters the way that the game is seen. Manual blocking was still the default option, even preferred by some of those old pvkii vets, but auto-block gave new players an arguably unearned and uneven playing field. This seemingly insignificant change drove a spike through the community.
And this brings me to the a very taboo topic in pvkii. The "community." Some will tell you that the community is in ashes. Some will tell you that the community is just fine. All can agree on the same thing, the community has gotten SMALLER. I, personally, won't be going into the specifics about the sociology behind the pvkii community because i wouldn't be able to progress beyond a ramble that leads to nothing productive. Instead, I'll bring up the previously mentioned issue, the spike that drove the community apart. Modern gaming is leaning towards a sort of bipartisan: "Core" gamers and "Casual" gamers. "Veterans" and "Noobs." "People that play more than me" and "People that play less than me." "12 years olds" and "12 year olds." The core guys bring stability to the community and the new comers bring life. Neither are perfect but both are vital. When the barely sentient guy that just installed the game manages to get a lucky hit on someone who has the pvkii logo tattooed on his forehead for so long that the ink is starting to seep into his brain and cause mood swings, two things happen. One: the new guy tells his friends, they tell their friends, who tell their friends and so on until, you got a reputable pack of these little poobrains wobbling about mashing the m1 button so hard that Razor's share holders are starting to get nervous and Two: the hardcore players lock themselves away in a single server so that they can beat each other over the head with their erect♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥and talk about how good they are compared to everyone else while comparing size in peace. These two rabbles are what we have now, and what have to be appeased.
Updates after 2.3 left much to be desired. New voice overs for every class were added, leading to the reactions "WTF I LIKE THE OLD ONES" from the vets and "Oh cool, this game has voice acting" from the new guys. A new class was added, considered "lame and game breaking" by some and "easy to kill if you're not an idiot" buy others. Some old maps were taken out and put back in, leaving everyone to wonder where that balanced class was that was supposed to be added 3 patches ago. It seems nothing the poor devs can do makes anyone happy anymore for more than 2 seconds. The voices conflict each other 9 times out of ten, and it's a shame to see it all for nothing. So much love has been put into this project, that much is apparent just by booting it up and listening to the theme music. So why can't I give this game another chance? Why can't I find enjoyment in something so beautiful and unique and amazing since there's so much love smeared all over it?
A while ago, the game released a ranged class. This was the first exclusivly ranged-focused class added to the game. The devs balanced the archer by handing out arrow blocking shields like expired candy to pretty much everyone else. It took some skill and getting used to before you could manage anything with it. Naturally, as change tends to do, everyone was enraged for one reason or another. The other guys saw the utility of this archer class and the new guys hated every second that they couldn't play one. A few updates later, a NEW ranged class was added to the game. You know what they forgot? Anti-ranged classes. And i don't mean classes that have a really good chance against archers when they're right on top of them. I mean some kind of stealth unit that can sneak up behind rangers and one-shot back stab them. Something that totally obliterates archers and sharpshooters when used by a competent player. Something that makes you NOT WANT TO PLAY A RANGED CLASS. Naturally, these units would be completely destroyed by melee units and thus you achieve balance.
Now we run into the heart of the problem. We have a simple problem with a simple solution. Finish what was started, the world keeps spinning. But the problem isn't being solved. Updates have been excruciatingly slow, and depressing when they finally do get here. The most recent class, the Sharpshooter, isn't nearly as up-to-par as all of the other classes. Its another backpetalling archer with slightly more speed than you and seemingly unlimited ammunition. Without a counter class, my frustration with this game is doubled. Don't get me wrong, I like the idea of an Archer class and a Sharpshooter class and even the idea of having to find a way of dealing with them as a melee class. What i don't like is having to fight ranged classes and melee classes at the same time constantly. You've got two voices coming from the community. One says "U GUYS IM LIKE SUPR GUD AT RANGR YOLO420SWAGSNIPERWOLFNARUTO4EVER" and "No, it's easy. You've just got to use your shield and kite around this rock and run all the way around and wait until he's not paying attention and change classes 2 or 3 times and shoot him in the face. It's easy." (That is, IF you can hear them over the sound of errect♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥slapping against foreheads and keyboards.) I get it, you can get around them by kiting and shielding. I've done it many times. ITS NOT FUN.  I also get that you can start a fire with a stick and a rock, but that didn't stop matches from catching on. So two voices are left. Counter the rangers or don't counter the rangers. I get it, updates are in progress, these things take time blah blah blah, but the game play has been deteriorated. With a majority of the blocking mechanic has been practically removed and pure melee fighting nearly unheard of anymore, the melee combat is basic and unenjoyable. Balance it and i'll give it another try. Melee based games need fun melee combat.

Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number is a game that is so amazing, that I would love if they would finally add the Level Editor and played other player-made levels for hours. The game is really simple, all you have to do, is pick up a gun, baseball bat, knife, anything near your hand, kill all the enemies on the floor/in the area you are, kill all other enemies on the other floors/areas, get a score and youre done. Now what makes it so exciting you ask ? The fact that it is not a Run & Gun game like Serious Sam 3 (I dont have anything to that game, I absolutelly love it but comparing HM2 to SS3 is like comparing Portal 2 to the f*cking "Fish Fillets" or whatever that crappy game was called, or Dota 2 to LoL, its just that better), beacuse one shot (sometimes 2 but rarely) from an enemy can kill you, so you have to either believe in luck and be accurate, or move from wall to wall, while still keeping your combo up. I also love the art style, like it is only pixels, but good god, those pixels are amazing in action. BAM ! One shot from your gun, and tons of pixel blood gets out of your opponent's head, BAM ! Another shot and other opponent's guts fall out for some reason cause you shot him in the belly and that opened him wide, would that work in real life ? Propably not. Does someone care about this ? Nobody ! This game is amazing. And now I have to warn you, this isn't a game for kids (like you couldn't think of that from the description before). There is blood, guts, and sometimes naked girls everywhere. (Oh, and partial swearing, nothing much *sarcasm overload*). So if you are interested in a game, where you can kill everyone, and after that kill your whole family in real life because you get so angry at some levels, then this game is for you ! And a last word, buy it with the soundtrack. I sadly bought it without the soundtrack, but I think I am gonna buy it, because the music is so bloody amazing, that even my 3 hour collection of Trap/Dubstep/D&B/House etc. music isn't as amazing.

Silverfalll, developed by Monte Cristo delivers an average action RPG experience.  To it's credit it includes a wide variety of items, interesting stylized graphics, as well as complex crafting and skill trees.  Unfortunately, at high widescreen resolutions, the onscreen text and menus are incredibly small making it difficult and tedious to read quests and navigate the various character screens.  In addition, the camera control, while allowing 360 degree movement, is not automatically tethered to the orientation of the mini-map, making simple navigation a chore.  Lastly, the actual action can grow a little dull, as melee characters in particular need only select a target and sit back while the ai and pc automatically duke it out.  Despite these deficiencies, Silverfall is certainly a solid addition to any RPG library.

Yep, Warhammer 40k, enhanced chess game.
The biggest difference between the classic chess and regicid mode:
- you can move with only one unit, but share/use many ability points in one turn with other units.

Unknown to most historians, this was the version of Chess that Bobby Fischer played against Boris Spassky. (Fischer a huge Space Marine fan while Spassky more comfortable as Orks)
Seriously though if you like chess and are a 40K fan, is there even a choice whether or not to buy this?

There is one flaw with this game - the inability to roll back moves in either game modes. It's something I'm hoping the devs will eventually fix, though. So far they seem very communicative and responsive, which is a rare breath of fresh air these days.
The two different game modes have already been explained so I won't bother. I'm just going to tell you why I like the game and the devs: even if the Regicide system may not be entirely to your liking and you just want to play 40k skinned chess with friends (which you totally can, it's great), I recommend you also try the campaign (especially the new one with the orks) - it's worth it not just as a challenging game, but the ork dialogues are worth it in and of themselves.
Another nice touch is that the unlockable content (new chapters for marines and orks, new map, new campaign) can all either be purchased liek DLC or unlocked with Requisition - a resource you obtain playing the game.
And now that chapters each get their own quirks, being more than just different skins, the game has grown quite a bit in complexity.
Especially on sale, I wholeheartedly recommend getting this game if you like chess and 40k.

Ahhh, this game...  This game is definately worth sinking some hours into, especially if you're into Tactical RPG's, MMO's, or even managing a Nation!
I first found out about Wakfu by watching the series on Netflix.  I thought "Oh boy, i wonder if there's a game for this!"  Turns out my ignorant self was unaware of the series being based off of a game!
Finding out as much as I could, I was extremely pleased to find this game on Steam, and absolutely FREE, too!
Anyways, back to the game itself, I've spent a good 130 hours on it now and I am STILL exploring the world that there is to see!  After a while you get tired of playing by yourself (if you're a social introvert like me) and you want to expand a little.  That's where making/joining a guild comes in handy.  You can find plenty of people to kill and gather resources with.
The system incorporated into the game are kinda... well, up and down.  The currency system, as well as the ecosystem and government, is all player-run.  So you'll have to checkup daily for new prices on an item you want.  And the crafting system is a little over-the-top.  Why do I need almost 32 bits of wool to make clothes!?
All in all, it's a good time-killer if you need an excuse from the world and want something a little different than MMO's like World of Warcraft.
I give it a 8/10.

Contrary to the popular opinion, I did not enjoy Far Cry 2. I didn’t particularly like the setting, and the gameplay padding in the form of respawning guard posts was very annoying. When Far Cry 3 was announced, I did not have high hopes for it. I thought it was going to be another generic open world shooter made for the consoles and I completely ignored it.
In the winter of 2014, Far Cry franchise pack went on sale on Steam, and I thought it might be worth buying it because Far Cry 3 and Blood Dragon were included. I paid $9.99 for it. I did not want to pay anywhere close to full price for these games because Far Cry 3 requires Uplay - even the version purchased on Steam.
The story of Far Cry 3 centers around a group of tourists getting captured by pirates on a tropical island. The main character has to escape and defeat the pirates. There is a lot more to it than that, but that’s the gist of it.
The villain in the game received a lot of attention. I don’t get the hype for this character. I didn’t think it was badly written, quite the opposite, but it is by no means original. I still think Bioshock had the best villain in video games.
I enjoyed the gameplay in this game a lot more than Far Cry 2. Activating radio towers can be repetitive, it is not as bad as Far Cry 2 with respawning guard posts. In this game, whenever you capture an outpost, it gets taken over by the friendly forces, and it will turn into a safe zone, which can serve as a spawn point. This is way better than having to fight the same enemies repeatedly throughout the game.
The shooting mechanics are well done, and there is quite bit of weapon variety, but not a whole lot of customization. As a Battlefield 4 player, I couldn’t help but notice how limited the customization was. That said, they got the core mechanics right, the weapons definitely handle very well.
It is possible to approach the outpost missions as you please, but the enemy AI has this supernatural ability to pinpoint your exact location within seconds. When one guard discovers your position, all the guards know where and what to look for. This can get annoying when using the stealth approach, but more often than not, I take a more direct approach, so it didn’t really matter to me. The few times that I tried, I found it to be less fun.
I do have to mention the UI and the constant hand holding throughout the game. I do not understand why single player games use 3D spotting. I can see this being useful to an extent in multiplayer games, but in my opinion, if at all this exists in single player games, there should be an option to turn it off. As it stands, every enemy can be “spotted”, which puts an overhead icon on the enemy, and this even includes the wildlife...bad game design.
Exploring the island is a lot of fun, from land vehicles to wing-suit, it’s got everything! This is the part I liked the most about the game. Exploring new areas, finding vantage points to take out enemies using a sniper rifle is very reminiscent of the first Far Cry game.
Apart from the exploration, there is a lot crafting and leveling up mechanics in the game. I used them sparingly. The most important item to craft are the various syringes and backpacks. Syringe kits can be used for healing, and for other buffs such as the special vision which will allow you to scout the surroundings for wildlife etc.
I didn’t particularly care about the leveling up aspect of the game. This does not have a lot of impact on the gameplay, and I ignored it for the most part.
The story is not bad, but some of the missions can be a little annoying, especially when they devolve into QTEs.
All in all, I enjoyed the game, and I would recommend it.
Verdict - Worth the price I paid for it.

Ok, this review is aimed at my old KF1 (and KF2 I guess) buddies. Essentially Vermintide places you in the fantasy Warhammer setting and has you fighting your way from point A to point B, using a combination of melee and ranged weapons to survive attacks along the way. Your melee attacks work really well, with a good dodge/push/block/charged attack  system in place. The ranged weapons rely heavily upon finding ammunition so you need to use with care, but there are a wide range of weapons, each with their own strengths. Melee is definitely the focus however. In some ways it may seem similar to KF_Damnation, but dont let this put you off. I hate damnation, but really enjoy this.
What I really like is the reward system. You level up and receive new weapons and gear by successfully completing maps/missions. At the end of the mission, you roll a set of dice, and the more successful dice rolls, the better weapon or gear you will be rewarded with. The weapon goes into your inventory pool, and you can either equip it to the appropriate perked character, or you can 'mess' with it some more. "Messing' with it can be done in several ways. Firstly, you can try and change the weapons traits. I should explain. Weapons have bonus traits on them. For example, traits may give you healing when you hit something, or provide the chance of an instant kill, faster attack speed, leech ammo etc. There is also a percentage chance applied to this trait, so for example, my flame sword has a 10% chance of healing me for 5 hp when I hit something. So I can roll some dice and try and change the trait to a some other ability that I would like, or, roll a dice and try and improve the percentage associated with the current trait. It costs a few tokens to do this. Alternatively you can meld 5 weapons of one particular level, into 1 weapon of a higher quality. The final way to mess with the weapons is just to 'salvage' them and convert them to tokens. These tokens can be used to reroll traits on existing weapons, or be used to create entirely new weapons if you'd rather.
I should also add that the quality of the weapon/loot item you receive at the end of the mission can be influenced by picking up 'tomes' and 'grimoires' during play. These give your end of game dice a better chance of successful rolls, but make the mission harder by limiting your healing options and maximum health throughout. Essentially they allow you to set your risk/reward level as you play. Brilliant!
I really like that there is a real tangible reward for completing missions. Unlike with KF1/KF2, there is no level cap (that I am are aware of) so you can keep improving your 'cred' if that's important to you. More importantly though, you keep getting weapon/gear drops so can keep modifying and crafting new gear, forever improving and honing your characters loadout.
There are 5 perk/classes at the moment, but it feels like only 3 really. Each has basically 4 main melee and 4 main ranged weapons each for you to choose from, but as stated before, you can customise those with different traits to your liking.
The environments are great. Detailed, atmospheric, balanced; though there is not a huge amount of maps just yet. Some people will find this a bit repetitive but I'm not minding it so far. Shame there is no option for custom maps at this stage, but the quality of the developer maps would be hard to measure up to anyways. There is a good variety of enemies, and while OP at times, usually they can be dealt with providing team work remains the focus.
There is no dedicated server yet, so peeps can hop into your game at any time unless you designate your game as private. Good and bad I guess. Scenes can get pretty busy at times when you are facing a horde so my internet struggles when hosting. If you play on your own while waiting for someone to jump in, bots will take control of your other characters to help out along the way. They are not infallible for sure, and sometimes will run away and hide, or stand by doing nothing while you slowly bleed to death, but with care, they can be utilised reasonably effectively.
All in all, this game gives you a Killing Floor like team game, with an awesome setting and a great motivation/reward system. Recommended.

With Warhammer: End Times - Vermintide, we now no longer have to wait 80,000 years in order to experience what it is like to live in the world of Elois and Morlocks. Vermines, Skavens, rats, beings of the underworld or whatever you'd like to call them decides to invade the city of Ubersreik, and the heroes are there to drive them back to their underworld, while killing their families, burning their homes, nuking their cities and eradicating their existance on the way.
This game, like what many others have said, is very similar to that of Left 4 Dead 2 in terms of game-play, though there are apparent differences as well. You have two type of major weapons, melee and ranged. Both weapons vary depending on which of the 5 classes you chose. Some are versatile killers while others are ranged experts or indispensable tanks which can keep the whole team safe. The missions are similar to those of L4D2 as well, with half of them being campaigns where you have to venture into a place and clear a finale event before evacuating in a wagon-like transport, while the other halves are some defense or smaller event missions. Eneimes are similar as well, with hordes of small and weak rats, special rats with various attrabutes such as pouncing, strangling, gattling guns or toxic gases. There'll be a tank-like boss called rat ogre where the whole team has to gang up to defeat him, and the patrol armored rats where the team will have to hide while they move away, avoding their attention.
There is a leveling and weaponary system in the game as well. The levels means nothing except that they will award you with a new weapon (a rather weak one) with ever level you gained. The are no stats involved for the characters, such as strength or intellegence. The major prupose of the game lies in the weaponary system. At the end of each successful mission, be it the major campaings or smaller event missions, you will have a number of dice which you'll try to roll for better weapons. There is also a weaponary system where you can rank up your weapons or unlock skills for your weapons.
The game itself is not easy, though after a few days of gaming and a few trusted friends you should be able to handle higher difficulties. There are 5 levels of difficulties, though you can increase the difficulty of your game (if you are playing a campaign) by looking for and holding on to tomes and grimoires, of which the former will take up a health potion spot, while the latter a boosting potion spot and reducing the team's health points by a third.
Again, similar to L4D2, this game requires cooperative gameplay, so this is definitely a go if can gather enough friends (you need four players) who can gather together and play on a regular basis, as you'll most likely find rushers who will rush out, get pinned, die, and leave you with nothing but fustration.
P.S. The ending is kind of skimpy, though it's really not the whole purpose of playing this game, so I'll leave it for you to figure it out yourself.
Take some Left 4 Dead, sprinkle in some powdered Chivalry, add a dash of RNG and a Hard Mode that lives up to it's name and serve it all on a nice bed of Warhammer lore and Roleplaying goodness.

Three of us played this game for 2 hours, and then refunded it.
Reasons for the negative review:
+ Goblin♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Really? It's one thing to have it in the game, but it's another to force it on your players and not give them a way to cover up until later into the game. For 2 hours the most we discovered was a top hat.
+ Ranged weapon accuracy. This game doesn't use a crosshair, and the ranged attacks do not shoot in the middle of the screen. We found it extremely difficult aiming a ranged weapon, something that is a must-have in the early game.
+ Difficulty. I'm all for a difficult game, but this doesn't even give you a chance. Melee weapons are useless at the beginning of the game, and after a few levels you can buy armor but it's expensive and impossible to buy until you've progressed through the second stage. Enemies will kill you quickly if you get hit, and the "shields" many of these enemies have regenerate faster than you can damage them.
+ Leveling. After 2 hours of gameplay, we had reached level 2. By this point, we still hadn't unlocked anything useful in the shop to use to help us fight enemies or to survive. The process of leveling is incredibly slow. We didn't know how much longer we needed to get our butts kicked to finally be able to put up a fight, and after 2 hours we got tired of it. If they increased the xp gain or reduced the amount needed to level it would be better. At the moment, we feel pretty useless, just like a bunch of naked goblins.
+ Mushrooms. They were a good idea, but not well designed. You can eat the mushrooms to regain health, and once you're full on hp you can carry 3 mushrooms to throw and stun enemies. You should also allow us to eat them to restore some of our hit points. We found throwing the mushrooms to be more damage than good because of the short range that you can throw them. Chances are, you're going to stun yourself too and then you're going to die because you can't move and the 5 enemies following you will kill you in seconds.
+ Losing special abilities when an enemy dies. When your teammates die and you're the last one up, and you have a horde of enemies on your tail that you cannot shake, THAT is when the special abilities are going to help you in a jam! In this game, as soon as an ally is downed your special god ability is lost until you revive that play, which is impossible if there are enemies on you.
+ Instadeath. When all party members are downed, it's game over. You start at the first stage/biome again, and you lose all of your currency and purchased items. The only thing you keep is your goblin level. You can change it from Normal to Easy mode which means you get to stay on the stage you died on, but you still lose all of your stuff.
+ No "loot" to be looted. The only thing you can find is treasure, which is the currency you can use to purchased items at a shop. This treasure is usually found in treasure chests and boxes, but not from enemies or bosses. When your game is titled "Looterkings", wouldn't you expect to explore and find awesome loot?
+ In the second stage, if you encounter the Dead Elvin King mini boss it's game over. I'm not sure how you're supposed to defeat this mini boss as it spawns infinite ghosts and then absorbs them to heal itself. We couldn't even damage the boss as we were to busy running away from the ghosts that will almost instantly down you. I'm sure it's easier to defeat with better weapons and armor, but we never had a chance to find any of those.
+ This game is extremely repetative. You run through the same levels, kill the same creatures, hopefully level up eventually, die, and do it all over again from scratch.
+ Bugs. This game really feels like it should be in the early stages of development. We killed a mini boss and he glitched in a wall during his death animation, which made the game not realize he had been defeated. We couldn't progress to the next room, couldn't teleport out, and couldn't even kill ourselves with the lava as it just kept returning us to the room. We were forced to quit the game and lose our progress. Yay, fun!
I could go on more, but I think i've said enough for now. I'm ok with roguelike games, but this game is very punishing to new players. You start as a naked goblin, so expect to be treated like a naked goblin at the bottom of the food chain.

Looterkings:
~~~~~~~~~

Deep in the darkest dungeon, they’re all waiting for you! All you can see behind the curtains back stage is hundreds of red, almond-shaped eyes. This is it - the curtain opens and you know it’s your time to shine! You walk onto the middle of the stage with your incredible goblin smile, looking straight at the audience. Then comes the outburst, “LET’S LOOT EVERTHING IN OUR PATH!” The horde went wild, “WE ARE THE LOOTERKINGS!”
Looterkings is a co-op dungeon crawler where you control one of four funky goblins. Your goal is to clear dungeons, loot and make your way up to the surface to the ultimate prize, which is to reach the sacred halls of the Elven Queen.
On the main menu, you’ll be able to join or host a game. Before you do so, head up to the lootery option and choose one of the four skins available to you. By hosting a game, you can choose to play by yourself, in the event that none of your friends are able to play with you. If you do, it will take a good hour or so to level up and to accumulate enough treasure with a view to purchasing better weapons and armour at the merchant store. It’s fun, challenging, and it will take you several attempts to reach the first mini boss. It’s a lot more fun when you play with your mates, but don’t expect to have an easy run.
The gameplay is cool; you have to clear rooms of enemies on your way to the elevator to go to the next level up. You’ll get additional gems if you’re successful, too. The interesting aspect about the opponent in each of the chambers is that they’ll respawn at least once, and occasionally twice, before being exterminated. There are over thirty-five different enemies, including bosses. Some of them will have melee weapons and others will throw projectiles which are mostly magic spells. Let me tell you, it’s so much fun when they come at you in huge numbers. Make sure to smash wooden boxes, pots and pin-point the big chests, as they hold plenty of loot. Then, when you have enough gold and have levelled-up several times you might be able to purchase better weapons and armour at the store. Oh, I nearly forgot to talk about the mushrooms! As you fight your way through the chambers, you’ll definitely going to receive damage and yes, the answer to returning your goblins to maximum health is to eat some mushrooms. But not all of them are good for you! There is a certain kind of mushroom to avoid; the ones with funny spots, as they can kill you instantly, or make you feel sleepy and we don’t need that in battle. However, if the health gauge is at its maximum, you can collect and throw them to your enemy, inflicting damage. The other way to inflict greater damage is when you trigger the beserker mode. To do so, you’ll have to successfully hit fifteen enemies in a short period of time and then it will last for around ten seconds.
Graphically the game looks good and runs fine. There’s a good number of weapons and costumes to unlock. In terms of controls, they’re fine but I must admit it’s not that easy to aim if you use the crossbows or staffs. The other downside, there are not many online games at this stage, which is a bit of a shame because it is a fun game to play.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Nice graphics
-	Randomly generated dungeons
-	Funny goblins with dangly bits
-	Fun CO-OP game
-	Good replay-ability
-	Achievements
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	No trading cards
-	Aim when using a crossbow and staff could have been better

Hey, coming here from playing the game both before and after it left Early Access, in both cases playing with a friend.
Armor seems to matter a fair bit more in 1.0, but I'm still forced to use the same tactics of hiding and plinking for many of the enemies, just as mentioned in numerous Early Access reviews.  I got further along due to the buff to armor, but later levels still prove to be too hard to be reasonable.  Damage sponge enemies?  Check.  Getting 2-3-shot by enemies?  Check.  Just like in Early Access...
Looterkings devs, I address all this because of your comments in this review:
You said...
"As stated in my other comment, we are working and improving the balancing constantly.  ...  What really is a problem for devs are people joining in on EA, wanting a polished, final game, being disappointed, giving bad reviews and forgetting about the game. EA is meant to be for balancing and polishing the game."
I quite agreed with this logic when the game was still in Early Access.  I like to be patient.  So I was eager to see where the devs took the game now that it's out of Early Access - now that it can be 'fairly judged'.  And I gotta say...I'm not impressed.  It barely feels like any balancing was done outside of armor feeling a bit more useful - but not enough, not nearly enough.  Where is the actual balancing?  I don't see it.
My last run ended in the library, where me and my friend were chased around my books who would bite our faces off or shoot us in the face for 1/3rd of our health if we tried to attack too close, and who were so fast that we couldn't get away from them all long enough to safely attack.  We ran around endlessly until we died.  That wasn't balance, that wasn't difficulty, that was just doom.  And it sure as heck wasn't fun.
I see the same problems existing as they have for a year. There's more content in 1.0 sure, and I'd love to enjoy it, I really would!  But I just can't.  Because there has been basically no identifiable balance to the, at-times, stupidly-hardcore enemies.
I should specify, I've been playing entirely on Normal mode.  I haven't tried Easy mode, because it has penalties and because it kind of would make me feel like a loser.  (I suspect it can get just as unfair though, unless the AI is actually retooled in it; but I heavily doubt it.)  Regardless, Normal mode should imo be considered a universal term for a moderate difficulty in a game; what I'm experiencing feels more like Very Hard or Hardcore mode if they were to exist.  (There are only Easy and Normal modes in the game atm, as far as standard modes go.)
So, devs.  Seeing as this game is out of Early Access, I can judge the game fairly now, right? So what's your reasoning now for the disbalance?
As negative as I sound, I do like this game, and I want to like this game more.  Heck, I enjoy difficult games, which this can be; but it can just as easily be unfair.  So, I can't recommend buying this game right now, not at the somewhat-high price-point. Even if you're really raring for a challenge, at least wait for a sale.
I'll be happy to update my review if things are retooled or rebalanced.

I didn't enjoy this game as much as I hoped I would. The whole water gimmick was cool at first, but eventually just became annoying.
Graphics: The water graphics, for the most part, look decent. The graphics design is pretty cool, although I'm a sucker for the whole cyberpunk futuristic look. Other than that it's nothing too special.
Story: The voice acting is pretty bad, which makes it hard to care about the characters. The story itself is relatively straightforward and cliched, and is a whopping 3 hours long, so that is definitely not a selling point of this game. The writing is uninspired, although there was one line that made me laugh: "I've got two balls and neither one is crystal."
Gameplay: The gimmick of this game is the use of large amounts of water to your advantage, whether it be to access high areas, put out fires, or sweep enemies off of their feet. That feature itself was pretty well done, but it was not utilized very often, and when it was, it was laid out step by step. There was absolutely no intuition required, which made the mechanic pretty boring. Other than that, the cover system is frustratingly bad, the gunplay is unsatisfying, and the controls are stiff.
Overall, don't spend your time or money with this game, unless you're a...uh...water fanatic? It's really nothing special and I found myself frustrated more often than entertained. 3/10

I'd like to think there was a really grat idea... that was just never fully realized, or they just didn't quite know how they wanted to effectively pull it off. See, it's one thing to advertise a game with having an ability, but it's another to save this until the last chunk of the game.
There are some well implemented ideas, unfortunately, none of which go well with what the intended vision might have been. Combat mechanics are awkward, some of the controls a tad unresponsive, and you're never completely clear on exactly how you're supposed to accomplish certain tasks. Oh, and you'll likely die a lot from trial and error trying to either figure out how to solve a puzzle, or drowning. Usually the latter.
I like the cover mechanics, although it's probably best to stick with the Sonic Rounds, since not only are they the highest accuracy, but they also don't have ammo, and you charge them. And you can use them underwater. Of course, your enemies can use shotguns underwater... which is kind of cheap if you ask me.
I wouldn't say this is a terrible game, as there are elements that do work... sort of, but I probably wouldn't recommend this, unless they decided they really, really wanted to try this.
[SPOILERS]
Now... if they had allowed you to use your "waterbending" powers a lot sooner, like say... I dunno, before the end of the first act, I think it could have easily been a much better game. Alas, that's not the case, and unfortunately, there's only a few short segments where you can try out your new powers, and it's incredibly short lived.
Plus the ending is kind of like they were trying to close it as quickly as possible. It's awkward.

Do you like Total War games? You you wish you could be apart of them and control your army in first/third person? Well now you can. This is within my top 5 best gams Ive ever played.
Sceptical? At first the game looks low quality and meger fun. In reality the graphics  arnt as bad as they seem, they are quite diverse. The shadowing is good and texture quality is a 6-7/10. AI is very fun either way. They form up when you fight them, you can form your men up, make very selective orders for a specific type of soldier and hopefully win at the end.
The missions in single player can take hours to complete a full quest line but its very much worth it. It passes time and gives the game the feel of actually traveling to your location. On top of that cultural divides are in the game as well depending on where you go. People are different, quests are different, its like stepping into a new small world every town you go to.
Multiplayer? That is one of the best parts. Mass multiplayer maps can be very fun. Defend the castle, rush, TDM, FFA and more are avalible to explore and have fun with.
What if the base game gets annoying you ask? Simple. Theres alot and I mean ALOT of mods for it. These range from a simple feature change to a total overhaul like the Star Wars mod, the Lord of the Rings mod, Warhammer mod, Britwaldia mod and far more. (My favorites are the Japanese Shogun mod, and the Britwaldia mods)
Overall i give it a 9.5/10.

Have to say, I've been really disappointed so far with Evil Within. The problem with that is that the enemies sometimes appear out of nowhere and you have no idea what you did wrong. Disarming certain traps, such as bombs, carries with itself the dangers of blowing you up if you so much as misson the first try.

I think they even reused the characters from Vanquish; Sebastian looks and acts very similarly to Sam Gideon. Also I'm a huge fan of horror, but even I think the gore was excessive at times. They practically -painted- the place with it.

Its a fun time waster. Has cool maps, plenty of games modes, and nice graphics compared to other blocky games. It has a map editor so you can create your own maps and upload them to the workshop which is pretty cool. All the classes are well balanced, meaning no matter what class you pick you're able to get kills against all the other classes... unless you aren't very good at the game. Of course, some classes might be better for certain maps and game modes, but I feel thats a given. For certain game modes its great to be strategic and dig up from beneath them or approach from the back. There are very little hackers in the game. I've only seen two. I have never experienced bad lag in the game. A lot of people say they do, but thats because they use the game finder instead of the server list. ALWAYS use the server list and sort the servers by ping. If you play on a server with high ping thats youre fault, not the games, so don't complain about lag. The game gets a ton of hate because its different from the original game before Jagex bought it. I honestly like this version better. Jagex has listened to the customers and made a lot of changes and its a lot better now than when it was first released. I would definitely recommend this to anyone who likes fps games, sandbox games, or is a fan of casual games.
