Left for Dead like game play but set in the Warhammer universe. More Melee focused first Person however you do have a secondary weapon which is ranged and very important for taking out special units in troublesome situations.
Unlike L4D there is a actual reason to keep playing for more than just teamwork, LOOT! Zombies are replaced by Skaven (Rat creatures for the uninformed) as you pass through the level you pick items that heal, make you more powerful, ammo and items that give you better chances of da good loot at the end of the game. At the end of the game you roll dice and the number of successful diced roll determines the quality of the loot you receive.
Each race/character has access to race/char specific weapons, those weapons are (Mostly) unique weapons stats/characteristics, so each characater has its own specific play style as well which makes the game unique and replayable.
Great game, especially if you love the Warhammer. Even if you don't give two hoots about warhammer you will still love this game as it is essential that your team coops throughout to be able to complete the levels especially on difficulty levels Nightmare and Above. A breath of fresh air as most games seem said to be designed for coop end up lonewolf encouraging. There is also no benefit in knowing the lore in the Warhammer universe as it the gameplay and skill in blocking that determines players skill.
The game has its occasional bug and you do on rare occasions (like all games) have the odd idiot, however there is a kick player function (thankfully rarely used).
The game is also very reasonably priced at $30 (USD) and much to my surprise these days no day one DLC!
Buy it. You will not be dissappointed!

This game is probably one of the best open-world games out there, especially when it's on sale.
You start FC3 as a white boy who ♥♥♥♥ed up and parachuted with his two brothers and three friends onto a jungle island that is occupied by pirate slavers, who promptly capture you.  One quick escape later and you're waking up in a hut with a tatoo being put on your arm and plopped into a world full of pirates to shoot, towers to climb, treasures to seek, and minigames to play.
The story is pretty batshit.  For one thing, the tatoo I mentioned is magic and gives you superpowers.  You'll meet crazy pirates, drug lords, and an awesome German mercenary named Sam.  You'll get high using a flamethrower to light fields of pirate-grown weed on fire.  You'll fight a madman in a psychadelic landscape.  You'll take jungle drugs and have visions of the future.  All that having been said, the story does have a very grounded theme: how far will you go into the jungle?  It's well done and manages to keep things from going too off the rails.  The plot has a nice loop of crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥> serious♥♥♥♥♥♥> crazy♥♥♥♥♥♥and feeds it to you relentlessly.
The gameplay is open-ended.  You can either sneak or go in guns blazing, and the tatoo (which doubles as your skill system) lets you pick and choose what you want in terms of upgrades.  You can buy better guns or you can climb radio towers to reveal the map and get guns for free.
And that brings me to my favorite thing about this game: the Handbook.  It keeps track of everything you have left to do.  No more need to guess how many towers are left to climb or how many doodads are left to collect - it's all laid out neatly, and even tells you what milestones will get you upgrades!  More games should have this functionality, as it lets people obsessed with earning all the guns and gadgets get that out of the way early.
Only thing sorta lacking is the music.  It's okay but kinda unmemorable save for two missions.  But other than that I'd recommend this game in a heartbeat.  Play if you are at all a fan of FPS.

So you work your way to the 9th lvl or so and want to become sniper (all in all you were one-shoted so many times by high lvl, full gear players so you want revange) so you pay for becoming sniper AND THAN you have to buy a SNIPER RIFLE for like 150k ingame money. Jackbox Party Pack is one of the few games that anyone can play and enjoy. I play it with my family and my friends. I personally prefer the third Jackbox to this one, but it's still great. I'll go over each of the games and my thoughts on them.
This is a great game where you're given a question and everyone types in an incorrect answer. Everyone's answers show up along with the true one. You take a guess and if your answer is correct you get points. If not, the people who gave the answer your chose gets points. One of the best games of the pack.
This is one of the less competitive/serious games of the pack. A scenario is given and one player is selected to be the judge. Everyone else picks two sounds that would best go along with the scenario. The judge then picks their favorite. It's fairly simple, but can give a good few laughs. My only problem with this is that for me it got old pretty quick, but it's still a good one to try out.
I love this one. It's very similar to the board game Masterpiece for those who have played it. At the start of the game each player draws art which is then assigned a random value which no one knows. Players will be given chances to bid on other pieces of art and they will be given hints by art experts on what is valuable. For example, an expert might hint that a painting of a bowl is what they're looking for, so if you see the painting they're talking about you'll know to bid high. Because everyone gets different hints it gives a good element of strategy to the game. The artists also get a percentage of the final bid on any of their paintings, which gives them a reason to try to drive the price up. But if they end up buying their own artwork they get no money in return. This is my personal favorite of the pack, but most people I've played it with don't feel the same way. I couldn't tell you why, but that is something to keep in mind.
I haven't played this one much, as I got kind of tired of Quiplash after the first Jackbox. It's a fairly simple game where two players are given the same prompt and try to give their best and funniest answers. The audience then votes on who they think did better. This game is best with larger groups of people, at least 5+. It's also the best game to play if you're streaming Jackbox on Twitch. It's not bad with the right group of people, but not one I'm a big fan of.
This is the only cooperative game in the pack. You work with the other players and communicate the information you have on your devices to try to disarm bombs before they go off. It's very similar to Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes. It is a very fun game, but keep in mind that it does have an actual ending. You can play randomized levels for infinite content, but the premade levels are finite. Also, don't just buy Jackbox if you're interested in this game. While it is fun, Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes simply does it better.
Seeing as the third Jackbox is out now, I would recommend that if it's your first time buying a Jackbox game, but if this is on sale pick it up.

As a particular lover of turn based games and role playing games in general, I decided to give a try to this MMO. Once he landed on Steam, I got into the beta and started to enjoy the universe of the World of the Twelve.
Despite having few hours compared to many other players, I can say this game is actually enjoyable and well made. However, there are some factors that could lead some people to avoid this title for various reasons. Let's analize every detail of the game. If you want to skip the wall of text, just go to the end, where there's a short version.
The graphic is 2,5D Cartoonish - Style, similar to animes. I like it, but somebody may not appreciate it. Colourful environments, characters and enemies (aka mobs).
However, sometimes you'll encouter a bunch of graphical bugs like invisible enemies, sidekicks not appearing,
or colors that make your eyes to cry blood (phosphorescent enemies).
At last, talking about the active parts of the game, while the enemies are well made and be distinghuished between their gender, the characters (not including npcs) tend to be more feminine. If you give a try to the game, you'll notice that even the males look like females.
There isn't so much to say about the sound. Each sector has its own, enjoyable track, including islands. The only bug you may encounter is an infinite loop after the dungeon of Zeppelantern.
Here we come, in the longest part of the review. Let's start with the choice of your avatar. You can choose between 15 different races, each one with its peculiarities and abilities. You can even decide if you want to have a male or a female, with the exception of
Regarding the gamestyle, it's a turn - based game during the fights against the mobs and the other players, while it's in real time during your journeys, explorations, harvests and crafts. Yes, because in this game you don't only get experience by killing tons of monsters or by completing dungeons you may access with specific keys and after you reach certain levels, but you can also produce your own items by collecting the resources in the environment and by crafting them in specific workshops.
You can also decide to group with some other people (or recruit up to 2 sidekicks) to face evil forces or stronger enemies that you couldn't defeat if you were alone.
Now the negative aspects of the gameplay. The tutorial itself is kinda crappy, made not properly because it teaches you only some parts of the game. It's useful just to know how's the interface, how to fight and how to collect and plant the enemies in the field in order to generate a wave of monsters to fight. Ah yeah, also to get the starting experience when you'll start with the real game itself.
The second most negative aspect is the interface. It isn't intuitive at the beginning, you can't move nor rotate the camera while you're in real time (but you can zoom in and out), while in the turn-based combats you can move it in a way the game doesn't explain. In fact, it doesn't tell you that holding the right button of the mouse and moving the cursor on the borders of your screen will allow you to see the entire battlefield.
And, at last, the quest system of the main missions is kinda...lame. You don't get involved in the main story and you do just some random quests in order to get experience and your first and only free sidekick. But, considering how's the game, you don't play it surely for the main quests.
The game is totally f2p. You're granted access to every part of the game (with the exception of the last 2 islands introduced not long ago), you can choose a nation at level 18 and do every kind of job. The nation system will allow you to player versus player fights and each nation has its own peculiarities. You're granted a free sidekick you can keep forever with every single character you make (until 5 per account) plus a free additional sidekick with a weekly rotation system.
The real money allows you to buy the sidekicks and keep them forever, cosmetics, costumes and booster packs that let you drop more loot and get more experience (in a small percentage however) plus the access to the last 2 optional islands. However, these zones are reserved for characters around level 140+.
- 15 races to choose from, with possibility of gender changing, that can reach until level 200.
- Different zones and islands to explore, with a huge variety of enemies
- 4 Nations to choose from, each one with its dominant element and peculiarities.
- PVP, Guilds and PVE system
- Huge quantity of dungeons, with specific dungeons you may find only in a certain nation
- Rewarding system well made
- Great variety of jobs, in harvesting and crafting, letting you to get your own items and to collect kamas (the game currency) fastly
- Colourful graphics
- Good sound system
-
- Shabby tutorial that teaches few things compared to the real potential.
- Not-so intuitive interface
- Main quests system not involving and realized superficially
- Might be boring if you focus only on getting experience
- Requires a lot of time and patience, 2 things that most people don't own...unfortunately.
I recommend to try this game at least once to every kind of afficionado of rpgs/mmorpgs. However, if you are included in one of the following categories I'm enlisting, just don't play this game:
a) You don't like turn based games
b) The story and the drama in a game is everything for you
c) The graphics is the most important thing for you
d) Anime haters

This takes everything that made Dirt Rally great and vastly expands upon that. Starting with visuals now I can't crank it past medium and get a smooth experience but even on medium across the board this is a visually stunning game so even if you aren't running the latest and greatest spec wise you can still really enjoy the visuals this game has to offer. In terms of imersion my mind is just simply blown, each game in the Dirt franchise had improved on immersion for some time now but this is for sure the most immersive rally racing experience out there. I'll start with a small touch that really was big for me despite how simple it was, when you finish a race instead of going straight into the results screen like most racing games you actually have to slow down your car and stop at the ending zone by the marshal which is a really small yet amazing touch for added immersion this is expanded on even more if you run in the cockpit view it just feels realistic. Sounds are amazing, so during a stage I had some brake damage that I didn't know about, but since I only went with fixing what was visually damaged rather than inspecting during a repair area I didn't know the brake was damaged so I went into the next stage with a brake that was not going to last. Ultimately the brake started to stick and made this terrible grinding sound, as horrible as it sounded it was great, but the real beauty was when the brake pad was finally just ground to the point it no longer worked or made contact and the horrible stound stopped as well. That is an attention to detail that I just love and I feel can really make a good game and help push it into what makes it a great game.
One of the things I felt was really lacking in Dirt Rally was the crew, at the end of the day they were nothing more than something you spent money on and picked the ones with the specific perks you wanted, when their contract was running out you renewed it. In Dirt 4 however your crew is an extension of you and your brand, they aren't just something you throw money into them and your wins/losses will affect their performance. So when you win races their moral goes up and in turn they get positive modifiers that make them perform better. The same applies to if you go on a losing streak they will start to get negative modifiers, on top of that you get to choose how much they get paid, while I haven't looked much into this yet I assume the more you cut them in for the more losses they can handle before they start to be negatively affected. Adjusting to a female navigator was different, I had grown so accustomed to a male navigator. But the wonderful thing about the navigator they are a part of your crew, they have a name and all that good stuff that is put right on the car with yours, you really get that feeling of your navigator is your partner, without them you are at a loss. Jen (navigator's name) will quickly rub off on you and feel like a long time friend and she has emotion in her voice and directions, it's not just another bland emotionless navigator, it is a very refreshing change to the franchise.
Overall Dirt 4 is an amazing experience from what I've seen so far if you liked Dirt Rally and you want to take your immersion to the next level then Dirt 4 is for you.

Having loved Dirt Rally, and the Dirt Series from Dirt 2, I was excited to play Dirt 4 from all the hype.
I was advised against buying it from my steam friends.  But, I thought, it can't be that bad, surely.
Well, it is.  Remember Windows 8, how it tried to be a desktop OS AND a mobile OS, but failed miserably at both, well, that is what Dirt 4 is.  It tries to be Dirt Rally, and it tries to be Dirt, yet somehow ends up being worse overall than either of those.
Dirt 2 is still my favourite dirt game.  It's just a btter all round experience than Dirt 4.  And do you know, it has better graphics and handling than Dirt 4.  It's just a fun game.  Whereas dirt 4 is soulless, the graphics are considerably worse than Dirt 2.  The tracks are just so plain and the procedurally generated tracks make them look like a game from decades ago.  Even Sega Rally (What a great game) had better graphics and course diversity than this.
I can't stress how dissapointing it all is.  Like I say, I'm a Dirt fan, and a Dirt Rally fan, shame this is neither of these two.  It's just a rubbish game, with rubbish graphics, terrible handling (in either mode), boring gameplay, compared to either of it's previous games.
Save your money, or spend it foolishly buying this game only to let it linger in your steam collection, unloved, reminding you every time you see it what a silly decision it was to buy this game, despite all the warnings not to.

Right, so I was scrolling up and down on my enormous steam library list, looking for something to play, and I ended up picking random things on my list and installing them, this was one of the things.
Hydrophobia: Prophecy is very short, the game time you see I have played is the time it took me completing this title, and I have no intentions to return to this title anytime soon.
As it starts up my first impressions was that it looked pretty good, although considering it came out in 2010, it is certainly not the best looking title of its time. The most interesting thing in the visual side, is the water, wich looks great and wich is also simulated very nicely, more on that later. The game starts out in the protagonists apartment, showcasing a futuristic but messy home, of an engineer living on some boat-a-majig. There is snippets of lore scattered around the world, but I found it to be largely uniteresting, and uninspired. It seems as if it is set in the futuristic setting everybody and thier mom uses, with white walls and sharp edges. Also the simple colouring, as you might see in titles such as Mirror's edge, is used here. Oh Mirror's Edge, released in 2008; much supirior in terms of visuals.
My first impressions was: "Alright, nothing I haven't seen before, but it seems as if it could be okay".
Aaaand not really. The game is just sub-par in every aspect. It shows interesting gameplay concepts, but fails to utilise them in any way. For example gunplay: I like the idea of the whole one gun thing, where you have a single gun whose primary ammotype is an infinite charge style ammo, wich is cool, big fan of that, but it just feels slow and the gun has no feel to it. They use it in one, yes ONE (1) puzzle, and then they throw you at the boss, wich is incredibly easy, you dodge a thing shooting at you, and then when it cools down you shoot it with one of the ammotypes, to stun it, and then you grab a barrel and throw at it. I spent $60 to back this game on Kickstarter, and right now, I regret it. For all the things AQ3D has managed to pull off, it has failed in every single way in terms of balance. The game was nearly-perfectly balanced in the Alpha and even Pre-Alpha stages, but as soon as the Closed Beta started, the team has removed all essence of fun from this game by turning it into an unbalanced mess.
It's a grindfest. A boring grindfest. The level curve between areas is insane, the amount of experience required to hit each level is even more insane, the amount of experience you get is minimal, and the need to rely on other players is way too high, for even the most basic of grunts. Don't even get me started on how long it takes to get through dungeons, or how many of them have incorrect level requirements. Level 6? These guys attack me like they're level 20.
There is no smooth transition for players to level up between areas, because they're stuck in old areas for way too long as they spend hours upon hours to get to those higher areas. The best part is when I see players in between areas wearing the same exact gear, because specific items are the only specific items to equip. Anything else and you won't make it anywhere.
Don't get me wrong, there's lots of positive things in here. Artix Entertainment's trademark humor is in spades in the intro segment, with the new cutscene system that looks and feels just like an AE game, and I'm looking forward to seeing it implemented more throughout the game as the story is fleshed out. Battles, especially activating skills and chaining them together for specific effects, feel satisfying to look at and hear (until you deal with the balance on the damage numbers and all the "Miss" and "Dodge" - seriously, WHY can I miss my own heals?!). The art style works very well for a game that needs to be on both mobile and Steam; a lot of people contend that this game looks bad, but I personally really enjoy this look.
But all of this is blocked by the balance problems. I hope that Artix and his team will look at these issues seriously, because the game can't grow in its current state. It'll fall flat on its face if even more classes and items are added before the current system is balanced. Once better balance exists in the game, I'll feel more secure in my $60 Kickstarter backing.

*I know little to nothing about Warhammer lore*
To say that Vermintide is basically Left for Dead would be a gross oversimplification.
The unique thing about Vermintide is that the game is focused mostly on melee, and the enemies aren't mindless zombies.
The way the melee combat works and looks are both outstanding. There is a loot system which means there is a ton of variation in playstyles, The ranged weapons cover everything from bows, pistols (flintlock), to magic. There are, as of now, 5 classes in the game. They aren't all so different that one would need to relearn the game, but different enough so that they all feel unique.
The enemies aren't stupid. Well, they ARE ratmen, so they are a little stupid, but they have tactics that they will use. Example, they are more likley to attack you in a group. If you approach an isolated one, there is a good chance he will run and hide. They tend to drop down from the top of buildings, swarm, and sneak up from behind. Like LFD, there are special mobs that spawn. Theres an armored rat, a rat that throws toxic gas, a rat with a machine gun, an assassin, a giant troll rat, and more. The game clearly had inspiration from LFD, but the key difference is that you aren't just hacking and slashing your way through hords. The game has a more tactical focus that encourages the group to try and work together.
Here's an example:
a game I just played, our party was 2 guys with swords and sheilds, 1 guy with a greatsword and a brace of pistols, and a fire mage. We ran through collecting hidden treasures to increase the chance of good loot at the end of the level with our sheild walls in the front and back of the party while the other two were in the middle of the group demolishing rat men at a range and hacking them down as they closed in.
****THE PATROL****
I didn't know where to put this but it deserves its own highlight.
In each match there is a large patrol of heavy armored rat men that are much more agressive and difficult to kill. It is up to the group to decide if they want to fight the patrol for the exp, or avoid them entirely and hide until they pass. This decision has many times been the deciding factor if the group will make it to the end of the stage for myself and many others before me. It's a neat system and it deserves an honorable mention.
The game alt+tabs well, there are lots of options for optimizing your performance on your system, and it looks/run pretty damn good.
The game isn't perfect by any means, but the devs have already released one free DLC and are planning on releasing more free and paid DLCs in the future. If you're sick of Left for Dead and want another good hord-based objective game set in a fantasy universe, then this game may just be what you're looking for.
Key things about the game-
*Leveling system
*Loot system
*Teamwork focused
*Light crafting system
*Satisfying melee combat

As a variation on Left 4 Dead theme, Vermintide is a coop survival game based on a simple yet polished and intense game mode.
Five different and brilliantly depicted characters, together with their own weapon sets, offer several combat moves and play styles, based on both melee and ranged weapons. Weapon feel and combat animations are well-refined and great to enjoy, as well as the mission settings (Stingray graphic engine is powerful but suffers from some performance issues).
End-mission reward system and five difficulties push the player to refine his skill and coop tactics, granting diversity and longevity to a basic simple format.
Vermintide is a perfect example of how well-realized simple ideas are enough, and should be the core, to build an amazing gaming experience.

If you don't communicate with your team or work together, you will lose. This game relies on teamwork and strategizing. Think of it as a WW2 version of ArmA, guns have bullet drop, firing like a madman will result in you missing any target over 10m thanks to the realistic recoil. Tanks seem overpowered, but are slow, sluggish and have long reload times, they are only a real threat if you catch their attention trying to do some stunt out of Battlefield. Planes often dive bomb you and often miss due to the excitable pilot getting caught up in the moment, unless you are in a tank....then you are most likely buggered.
Each weapon has their own strengths and weaknesses, SMGs are good for indoors and suppression but lack the range, Bolt actions are devastating upon hitting their targets but have slow fire rates (obviously) and frighteningly long reloads, Semi-Rifles are the bridge between those 2, offering good range and fire rate with medium damage. Machineguns are nightmares to take on but thankfully, not many use them. Every weapon also comes with a zeroing option, but you usually use that for the bazookas and anti-tank weapons.
The best part is how each vehicle has their weakspots and all require a correct angle of approach to deal any real damage, tanks tend to have theirs on the rears and turrets, planes seem to be the pilot's seat and wings, light vehicles and armour often have theirs around the engine and wheels, or you could just aim for the driver.
Leveling up can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥though, but getting ribbons for unlocks is much easier, and ranks only really matter if you want to switch your role to that or Tank crew, Pilot, Recon or Paratrooper. The spawns can sometimes drive you insane, as I have often been spawned facing away from the battle or in the sights of an enemy, but these are only minor flaws, and the gameplay more than makes up for such.
To those out there who want a FPS that goes back to WW2, Heroes and Generals is the answer. So maybe its F2p and requires real money to unlock stuff earlier or get a few shoddy camos. But it's faring quite well for a game that is still in Beta.
Looking forward to updates and new content.

Let me start out by stating that, though it may say I've only played Wakfu for 1.8 hours, at the time of writing this review, I have many more hours with this game under my belt.
I have been playing Wakfu long since before it's arrival on Steam, and I enjoyed every second of it, but this game is not without its flaws, I will start this review by simply stating the pros, and cons of Wakfu.
------------
PROS
Wakfu features a rather unique battle system, that I have yet to see in any other game, (With the exception of Wakfu's predecessor, Dofus.) Not to mention Wakfu's challenge system, a system that chooses two random challenges for a battle, these challenges grant bonus exp, and ingame currency.
If you enjoy variety in classes and builds for these classes, you'll enjoy the classes Wakfu has to offer, choose from fifteen classes, with each class have three elements to choose from, use a single elemental tree of spells, or mix up your elemental prowess with two, or all three of the elements for a class.
Wakfu also features a unique feature, players control the world, ranging from governments, to the enviorment in of itself. Control the animal populations, step up as a governor, and lead your nation.
------------
CONS
As much as I love Wakfu, I can't deny it has many flaws, be they small or big, to start off the CONS, we'll begin with that fact that Wakfu can, in some ways, be pay to win, with the recent addition of "Booster Packs" which provides the player with a boost in EXP gain, loot drop rates, and ingame currency gains.
Wakfu also suffers from the fact that it is, for the most part incredibly grind heavy, with few quests tossed in to simply introduce you to areas more or less at later levels, some may view this as a bad thing, or a good thing.
------------
Overall, Wakfu is a good game, though far from perfect, but far from being a trash, it earns a simple 8/10 from me.

A fine naval-centric warfare simulator with a wide selection of included scenarios, free community-made scenarios and optional paid DLC.
I have had Harpoon, WinHarp, H2, and H3 on my computers since forever.  Back in the day my volunteer work proofreading the H97 database earned me a Harpoon ballcap from Mr. Bond himself.  This title (CMANO) is another take on modern naval warfare and I enjoy its variety of 4-d chess.
I could care less about arguing which fuel/sensor models are more accurate but overall this title accurately allows you to experiment with the principles of modern-day naval operations big and small.  There are some differences compared to Harpoon regarding comms and BDA, not right-or-wrong but different choices the devs have made.
Be sure to install the free "Community Scenario Pack" and free "Database Images & Descriptions Add-ons" available from
after installing this game.  This will add 350+ scenarios of all varieties to the game as well as more platform pictures and expanded platform descriptions.
I can recommend the "Uncle Marks Tutorials" scenarios for beginners as well as the  four "First Contact" standalone scenarios that are CMANO's version of the classic Harpoon GIUK "Dawn Patrol" -- short, tactical and a nice way to learn the navigation, weapon, and sensor controls.
PURCHASING NOTE:  It makes sense to purchase this title directly from Matrix/Slitherine because then you get the Steam-free version, a key to register the title with your Matrix account, AND a Steam-key if you prefer playing via Steam.
What I learned too late:  Purchasing from Steam (as of this writing) DOES NOT give you a key for CMANO to register on Matrix.  Five of the Steam-bought DLC (Northern Inferno, Old Grudges, Don, Brexit, Spratly) do give you keys to register your Steam purchase on the Matrix site but again, the main CMANO program does not.
I enjoy the title so much I repurchased it on the Matrix site when it was on sale just to get a Steam-free version...
Some negatives:
The program interface is not the best.  There's one main map window where you fight, no multiple views like H2/H3.  And other windows like the Message Log get overlaid on top of the main map making that part of the map useless.  The developers for some reason disabled the Minimize button on the  "Message Log in separate window" option.  Maybe on a multiple-monitor setup this works but I play mostly on my laptop.  I wrote a little external Windows utility to enable the Minimize button when the program is running but that's not something the average user will do.
Hotkeys for selecting and giving orders to units do not work unless the map is clicked first which feels wrong since the map feels naturally like it's the app's main window.  When the mouse is over the map the Hotkeys should work.  Having to left-click on the map to enable Hotkeys often de-selects the current unit.  Right-clicking is even worse because it re-centers the map.
These issues make it feel like one is fighting the interface.  Sure I can get used to it but still...
Major parts of the game seem to be written in managed VB .NET so it's perhaps not as fast as it could be if written in native code especially with the number crunching required of a simulation of this type.  The small- to medium-sized scenarios I have played have not lagged per se but I do have it running under the 1-sec "pulsed" update mode which makes it feel more realistic, like I'm TAO in the CIC, LOL.
I can't comment on the Scenario Editor but it looks full-featured, especially now with the addition of Lua scripting.
Overall a fun game/sim that I have added to my always-installed-on-laptop collection of Harpoon1/2/3.  The more time and knowledge you put into it the more it will give back.
To support the devs and further development I bought all DLC, this is my kind of game.  Thank you!

1545 hours of play. Do I recommend CMANO? It depends...
The traditional for / against:
Pro:
+ a very big data base
+ characteristics of ships, planes, armaments, sensors, etc ... very detailed and important
+ a simple to use editor that allows you to create your own scenarios
+ the integration of LUA very well done
+ the micro-management by the IA of certain aspects of the combat (for example: choice of targets and shooters, and number of missiles fired in "dense" aerial combat)
+ the application of IRL tactics in the game leads to the expected consequences
+ support by developers (which still tends to decline)
Con:
- the price ! the price ! the price. Definitely the game is sold too expensive. Even on sale it is too expensive. At this price, we should not find the elements that I will now list.
- With the exception of some very specific elements, the AI ​​is stupid without name. All the intelligence of the adversary relies on the ability of the author of the scenario to manipulate the editor and to program in LUA.
- even very complex scenarios are easy to win and the player's victory is often overwhelming
- there is practically no replayability on a scenario. The AI ​​does not analyze the situation, all its decisions are scripted or preprogrammed (planned missions)
- "mysterious" freezes, temporary but exasperating without any real relationship to the number of units represented or the situation
- The essential micro management in air combat, on pain of seeing his F16 C piloted by Maverick being shot down by a North Korean Mig-21
- the global and static weather: it is the same weather in Cyprus and Murmansk throughout the duration of the scenario. Not very serious for a 24-hour scenario in the Mediterranean, but more annoying when long-range bombers enter the scene in a clash over several days
- a UI worthy of Windows 3.1
In conclusion: this is not an RTS (like Wargame), this is not an operational/strategic wargame (like...Hearts of Iron), this is not a simulation (like DCS). It is an OPFOR simulator. Personally I use it a lot to "evaluate" the doctrines and the OOB of the Cold War (moreover in this respect we were lied to, the Soviets would never have set foot in Europe).
I love this program, but - beyond its price (omg ! its price!) - I recommend it only for former military , hard core wargamers , history  and/or geopolitics enthusiasts  and only for those who accumulate at least 3 of the above 4 characteristics.
Otherwise...big disappointment.

This is a Newbie review.  I feel that writing a review after some 30 hrs play is cheating; I am only just starting out.  I watched this game for a while but held off partly because of the high price tag, but mainly because I thought I may find it overwhelming.
I picked the game up on sale.
Now I wish i'd bought this game earlier - full price be damned; its worth it!
Some elements of the UI could be a bit better; it's fine but lacks some intuitive elements with the mapping/unit movement elements (and why is the middle mouse button redundant? it could free up the right mouse for unit based drop down menus).
The windows style menu system is  good though; it's logical and provides a nice breakdown of how things work.  And there is plenty to work at!
It reminds me of learning Microsoft office for the first time; learn a few things and build on it - while that may sound uninteresting, it works.  Its is possible to wonder why something is not doing what you want/expect but the answer can usually be found by checking through the various options rather than scanning through the manual (which I have barely read).
Which is one of the games stongpoints; the community is excellent.  Baloogans turorials are a must  (there are others out there too).  The actual stock game tutorials are OK, though you must pay attention to the text and just get stuck in.
As for the gameplay; it's captivating.  The graphics may be abstract, but they are functional and provide a great canvas for your imagination to do the rest.
As more of a WW2 buff, the game reminds me of Steel Panthers in its detail in assessing and reporting all occurancies.
The database is huge (I recommend adding the community pics - check the guide in the steam forums).  Its easy to just check the internet on the fly too if you want to check stuff out in more detail, but such is the game's detail there are plenty of items (weapons and sensors particularly) that hold more info in the games database than i can find on the net.
You dont need to have an encyclopedic knowledge, just familierize yourself with the unit loadout of a scenario as best you can and just jump in (and if you get owned just think of it as a fancy roguelike and try again!).
If you are even slightly intrested in this game, its probably worth it, but be prepared for an initial bit of effort in getting throught the tutorials and be sure to check out the community help - you will soon be flying/sailing solo.

Hydrophobia: Prophecy. What I think of it.
Warning! Long review is long. You have been warned.
-Default Gameplay Mechanics: 7/10
The default buttons are a bit annoying, but they can be remapped. Way points are misleading and don't help when you're stuck.There are things you have to look at very closely to be able to progress. The cover system sometimes doesn't wanna work so the character doesn't go for cover. Diving underwater sometimes happened randomly when I didn't want to dive. Health regen system, which is common in many games, makes an appearance in this one. The boss sometimes glitched out (see Boss Difficulty below).
-Resolution: 10/10
Many resolutions to pick from. I was able to play it with my laptop connected to my big screen TV via HDMI on full screen.
-Maximum Overall Graphics: 10/10
Hands down, the best water graphics I've ever seen. Ending cutscene had the worst graphics in the entire game. Water graphics could easily make up for it.
NOTE: The game is all about the water.
-Storyline: 6/10 (SPOILERS)
A metropolis floating on water is attacked by a terrorist group known as Neo Malthusians. You, the character, are trapped and the area you are in is flooding. With the guidance from your buddy working the security cameras, you find a way to **escape**.
It was good for the first 2 acts then suddenly became wtf on the second half of act 3. And it only has 3 acts. The game can be beaten in less than 4 hours if you know what to do. My first playthrough was 4 hours. And that's not beating it 100%.
**It has a horrible ending with no resolution of any kind whatsoever. After beating the boss practically nothing happens**
-Normal Enemy Difficulty on Easy: 9/10
The enemies were pretty easy. They did get some cheap hits every now and then. It's hard to tell if an enemy is dead or down from a certain distance.
-Boss Difficulty: 6/10
The last and only boss is ludicrously powerful. A woman (who can be assumed as the terrorist leader) takes control of a machine that has a mini-gun, rocket-type projectiles, and grenade launcher. It sometimes glitched out to the point where I had to restart the battle almost 10 times. When it tossed out bombs, it covered a large portion of the room and they're very hard to see so I didn't know where was considered safe. Getting cornered for one second is almost guaranteed death unless you're lucky to survive.
Price: $4.99
A bit high price for a short game. I got it when it was on special for $0.49, so I don't really regret it.
-Overall: 6.5/10 - Pretty much the MetaScore (for once I agree with it)
I liked the game. The majority of the storyline is good and it's not too long to beat. But, it had some painfully obvious problems (everything mentioned above). If the developer/publisher company didn't go bankrupt a couple of years ago, they could have made this game so much better.
I'd recommend it, but honestly, you'd be better off buying it on sale for $0.49 than the regular $5 price.

As a variation on Left 4 Dead theme, Vermintide is a coop survival game based on a simple yet polished and intense game mode.
Five different and brilliantly depicted characters, together with their own weapon sets, offer several combat moves and play styles, based on both melee and ranged weapons. Weapon feel and combat animations are well-refined and great to enjoy, as well as the mission settings (Stingray graphic engine is powerful but suffers from some performance issues).
End-mission reward system and five difficulties push the player to refine his skill and coop tactics, granting diversity and longevity to a basic simple format.
Vermintide is a perfect example of how well-realized simple ideas are enough, and should be the core, to build an amazing gaming experience.

If you don't communicate with your team or work together, you will lose. This game relies on teamwork and strategizing. Think of it as a WW2 version of ArmA, guns have bullet drop, firing like a madman will result in you missing any target over 10m thanks to the realistic recoil. Tanks seem overpowered, but are slow, sluggish and have long reload times, they are only a real threat if you catch their attention trying to do some stunt out of Battlefield. Planes often dive bomb you and often miss due to the excitable pilot getting caught up in the moment, unless you are in a tank....then you are most likely buggered.
Each weapon has their own strengths and weaknesses, SMGs are good for indoors and suppression but lack the range, Bolt actions are devastating upon hitting their targets but have slow fire rates (obviously) and frighteningly long reloads, Semi-Rifles are the bridge between those 2, offering good range and fire rate with medium damage. Machineguns are nightmares to take on but thankfully, not many use them. Every weapon also comes with a zeroing option, but you usually use that for the bazookas and anti-tank weapons.
The best part is how each vehicle has their weakspots and all require a correct angle of approach to deal any real damage, tanks tend to have theirs on the rears and turrets, planes seem to be the pilot's seat and wings, light vehicles and armour often have theirs around the engine and wheels, or you could just aim for the driver.
Leveling up can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥♥though, but getting ribbons for unlocks is much easier, and ranks only really matter if you want to switch your role to that or Tank crew, Pilot, Recon or Paratrooper. The spawns can sometimes drive you insane, as I have often been spawned facing away from the battle or in the sights of an enemy, but these are only minor flaws, and the gameplay more than makes up for such.
To those out there who want a FPS that goes back to WW2, Heroes and Generals is the answer. So maybe its F2p and requires real money to unlock stuff earlier or get a few shoddy camos. But it's faring quite well for a game that is still in Beta.
Looking forward to updates and new content.

On the whole, this is a good set of party games everyone and anyone can enjoy. Grab some friends and indulge in pure comedic genius in video game form.
Fibbage: A quasi-trivia game where you have to make convincing answers to trivia questions for your friends to pick, and then try to parse through the lies to find the truth. A personal favorite.
Quiplash: Each player is given two prompts, and they have to try to make a funnier answer than the player with the same prompt. The other players have to vote on which of the responses they find funnier, and the responders get points depending on how many people voted for theirs. More fun with more people, and ideal for streaming, but still fun no matter the occasion. Except funerals. Probably in bad taste there.
Earwax: Quiplash with one prompt, one judge which changes each round, and, most importantly, audial responses. Not as good as the former two, but it can be fun for a few rounds.
Bidiots: Each player draws a few paintings, and then players bid for them depending on what they think they are. Not as good as Drawful before it, and definitely the weakest of the bunch.
Bomb Corp: The only co-operative or single-player game of the bunch. Players need to work together to defuse perplexing bombs by cutting wires according to certain rules. Essentially Keep Talking and Nobody Explodes, except more thinking-based and with a less complicated manual. In other words, a riot.
It's Fun.

As a long time fan of the DiRT series and having spent a fair amount of time in DiRT 4, I felt I would share my impressions with any potential buyers:
Intentions behind DiRT 4:
- To forward the DiRT Franchise
- To appeal to a wider audience than DiRT Rally
I will not do a significant amount of comparing this game to DiRT Rally, because while made by the same publisher and studio, they are different games and were created for different reasons. DiRT 4 is a more polished game because it was never in Early Access, like DiRT Rally was, which started off little than an enhanced demo.
Graphics:
DiRT 4 is clearly based from the same engine and platform that was used for DiRT Rally, so anyone familiar with that game will immediately gain some familiarity.  While DiRT 4 will never take home any awards for its graphics, there's nothing particularly about the game that is an eyesore other than some bland textures used for the engine compartment if you happen to wreck in such a way that the hood comes up.  The environments, cars, roads, weather effects, and particles are all perfectly acceptable for modern standards of racing video games. DiRT 4 perhaps has an advantage over some other racing titles because it is focused on a narrow scope or type of racing that more all-around detail can be provided whereas other games cannot always pull this off.
Performance wise, DiRT 4 will flat out scream on modern graphics hardware, the game provides no challenge to my GTX 1080Ti fully cranked.  I have a friend who plays the game on a 780Ti and also has no trouble keeping the game running at 60FPS, a testament to the overall quality and playability of the game.  This is a critical factor in its gameplay, following below.
Gameplay:
While Codemasters clearly made some offerings here to attract a more casual crowd to DiRT 4, the improvements to the driving systems from DiRT Rally are noticeable and have been commented upon in other reviews; the rally cars now seem to have a noticeable amount of weight and you can execute shifts very effectively to master the courses and challenges provided to you.  DiRT 4's greatest asset lies here - while nothing but 1 or 2 things is particularly painful about this game, if you really like the driving feel of rally and can weigh "what the game gives back" to you for your time...this game has at least 40-50 hours of solid gaming to offer you.
The only painful item of note in the gameplay for myself is the AI, which often seems to not have any given level of predictability into knowing what difficulty provides your ideal experience.  I find myself toggling between Challenging and Demanding quite often because either I am getting blown away by the AI or I am blowing them away.  For the sake of progressing the career, I don't mind the latter, I just want to finish it.  But when I want a realistic experience, this is proving not the easiest to attain.
Sound:
The cars sound like cars, the road sounds like road. When you crash it sounds like a crash. That's all I got.
Immersion:
DiRT 4 provides a very solid career mode in terms of features...it exposes you to different disciplines of off-road racing including Rally, LandRush, Rallycross, and Historic Rally.  Going through the career will put you in several different cars and locations, all with varying degrees of technical and natural challenge. Additionally you get the ability to create and manage a team, color scheme, sponsors, staff, accomodations, etc. Codemasters is really on to a solid path with this...I hope DiRT 5 takes this a level further.
Here's where immersion falls apart, just a little.  While the driving experience is great, the career mode after a number of hours gives you a sense you have done and accomplished a lot...the ugliest part of DiRT 4 then starts to show itself: Repetition.  There are only 5 Rally locations to play and while there seems to be a very good variance in how stages can be built into those locations...your will to go back to the same place over and over and over and over again will be tested. In the context of one event that's not bad, but later in career mode you'll do championship after championship running the same locations and stages over and over with different cars or the same cars. This is really the only place where DiRT 4 suffers noticeably; for some this will mean they will never finish career mode. I for one love the driving experience so I will power through the repetition, but I do notice it. I sincerely hope DLC is in the future to add more locations.
Multiplayer:
I don't have a lot of hours in MP for DiRT 4 yet, but other than splitting events into daily/weekly/monthly style engagements, nothing else about the game changes.
Achievements:
There are 48 achievements at present, many of which will be gained by natural progression. For achievement hunters, this one is fairly easy to complete without sinking massive amounts of hours to do so.
Overall:
For $40 or less, DiRT 4 is worth your time if you're a rally racing fan or just like racing games. It will not be the greatest experience in gaming you've ever had and there's certainly room to continue to evolve, but if this is the foundation that DLC or future DiRT games build upon, Codemasters could have easily done worse.

After 200+ hours on Dirt Rally and 50+ on Dirt 4 using my G27 wheel I have to disagree with the vast majority of negative reviews for this game and I can say that this is a good, solid, fun game. It's important that it's called Dirt 4, not Dirt Rally 2 because of what the two different titles are trying to achieve. I'm not saying the game is perfect, but it's certainly got a lot of positives to it that far outweigh the negatives in my opinion.
To start with, the positives:
Car physics and damage models have been completely overhauled and upgraded in Dirt 4 compared to Dirt Rally and Dirt 3. The cars actually have weight to them now and managing the roll and weight transfer under braking actually feels really good. This is particularly noticable in the RallyCross car classes compared to Dirt Rally. In DR, some lurched so much at just the slightest touch of the brakes. In D4 this has been made so much better and they feels great now. Damage is also more realistic and when you damage your gearbox or transmission you actually hear and feel the clunkyness in the engine.
The career mode has also seen a large improvement. We have different categories of events from Rally, Historical Rally, RallyCross and Landrush and a huge selection of cars to choose from. You don't have to do anything you don't like and can chop and change as much as you like. As a fan of RallyCross I'm thrilled that junior categories are added as well as more tracks and cars in the RX Supercar class.
Adding onto the whole career segment is a team management aspect similar to Dirt Rally but expanded and improved. You can create your own team livery and add sponsors to your car, as well as improving your team's facilities to upgrade car parts and hire better staff.
Real time multiplayer has been added so you can race against your friends on rally stages at the same time, rather than just setting times and competing through the leagues feature that was in Dirt Rally. As someone who loves multiplayer this is a HUGE positive for the game and was my #1 complaint with Dirt Rally. To have it added in has been fantastic. There were a few issues with it at launch where players would be disconnected by the game and then unable to rejoin for a period of time however this was fixed within the first week of the game's release.
The negatives:
We were promised the handling would be exactly like Dirt Rally. It's not exactly like Dirt Rally. Pretty self explanatory, however it's pretty damn close and still very enjoyable. Some cars feel like they understeer a lot, while others always oversteer too much and a select few feel like they're on rails. This can be fixed with car setups pretty easily but hopefully this will be adjusted in a future patch.
Your stage and procedurally generated stages. I'm torn putting this here. It's a great addition to the game and adds a lot of replayability, particularly to the multplayer side of the game. I think it's great because it addressed one of the key issues Dirt Rally had in the limited stages you can race on. And for the first 50 hours of Dirt 4 it's been great. However I have noticed a few landmarks or unique sections of certain stages that crop up and know what to expect when I see them. It's still enjoyable, but there needs to be more than 2 variations of a hairpin turn in future "your stage" development.
Leagues from Dirt Rally aren't in Dirt 4. Ok so I said real time multiplayer was a huge boost for the game and it is, however I don't see why both leagues and real time multiplayer can't co-exist. It's hard to round up my mates and get on for races all the time, so leagues is great in that we can still compete over a week for who has the best times over some stages. Really hope this gets patched in as leagues were a great feature of Dirt Rally and would really help the multiplayer aspect of Dirt 4.
All in all Dirt 4 is a great game that I've enjoyed playing. Is it better than Dirt Rally? No, but I'd say it's not trying to be better than Dirt Rally since it's called Dirt 4, not Dirt Rally 2. It has several aspects that've been improved upon from Dirt Rally and is a worthwhile purchase for any Rally fans, especially RallyCross fans! It's easily got the best RallyCross content of any game out there!

Contagion is a zombie game that offers you several game modes and maps to explore and survive the rise of the infecteds in game modes such as Escape and Extraction. The gameplay is relatively slower paced in modes like Escape as compared to other zombie games like No More Room in Hell and Left 4 Dead 2. In Hunted mode, you're placed with not just the threat of zombies, but also your fellow survivors trying to hunt you down. Not to mention, you can also play as one of the zombies when you died as a survivor, hence providing you the ability to command other zombies to hunt down your former survivor friends. Furthermore, you can also play as a cockroach instead of the typical and boring spectator camera.
Pros:
*Devs did a great effort in producing a game with an apocalypstic atmosphere with the great use of lighting and eerie background music.
*Offers many game modes and several maps to survive.
*Every time you play Escape and Extraction, objectives are shifted which provides you with unique pathways to explore the world of the living dead.
*A large variety of weapons to choose from.
*Instead of waiting for the game to finish after you died as a survivor, you can play as a zombie.
*You can play as a cockroach instead of becoming a boring spectator camera.
*Has steam workshop to customise your game.
Cons:
*Some guns seems to be unfinished. e.g. when unloading the Remington 870, the racking sound of the pump cannot be heard, unlike the Mossberg 590.
*The Scar-L's suppressor doesn't actually reduce the noise effect of the gun on the zombies, but rather attract more zombies.
*Some melee weapons have their sound misplaced in the animation, especially performing a stealth kill on the zombies. e.g. baseball bat.
*Lack of updates and new contents for the game which the devs had promised.
*Some maps such as Barlowe Square can be a maze in game modes such as Escape, which can be hideous sometimes when you try to complete an objective.
*Some maps such as Roanoke PD has a bug where you can sometimes hear the helicopter's sound on the roof even though it has not spawned yet. Likewise, when you enter back into the police station building after the trip to the roof, the roof environment sound can still be heard.
*When you spawn into an Escape game, you start at the beginning of the map, regardless of how many objectives other players had completed. This can be annoying when you try to catch up to other survivors.
*Has a bug where zombies can sometimes get stuck in some places of the map. Such as windows or furniture when they're spawned.
All in all, I still personally enjoy this game regardless of the unfinished contents, bugs and lack of new updates. Its still fun to play with your friends and a game worth a try if you're into zombie, horror and survival games.

This is basically WH40K's take on chess. You can play in a classic (chess) mode, or in Regicide mode, which incorporates unit abilities, skills, strengths and weaknesses. In the latter mode, it becomes like a turn-based battle from any TBS WH40K game (like Chaos Gate, etc.) but with a chess overlay (you can queen your pawns, if your king dies you lose, etc.). What this means is that you can kill enemy units even though you've already made your turn during the chess phase.
From what I can see, this game holds a lot of promise and can be great fun.
What I think would REALLY make it fun would be (and this may already be in the works) persistent troops (that improve with battles won), equipment and armor upgrades, maybe even some RPG elements, and perhaps some sort of overarching storyline to tie everything together. These are the things that made the Dawn of War franchise great.

For now, I'm recommending this game, and will update my review as the development progresses.

I think this was one of TellTale's first games, along with BTTF. As with that game, I will say that this is a very linear game, unlike their later attempts. If you're expecting the same choices and branches, you will be disappointed.
Tales of Monkey Island is... different from the older Monkey Island games, holding a very strange position in the franchise. This is, I suspect, the first game that wasn't made by LucasArts. Many of the people from the original games are involved, but there is a strangeness about the game that wasn't in the others.
The graphics aren't bad. If you've seen any other TellTale games, you'll know what they're like. The art direction is reminiscent of Curse of Monkey Island which is no bad thing. Voice acting is top-notch as always, with Alexandra Boyd, Earl Boen and Dominic Armato doing splendid work as Elaine, LeChuck and Guybrush. Music isn't bad, with some eerie voodoo music tied in with the usual Monkey Island themes.
Tales of Monkey Island, however, seems to rely very much on shock value, going to places where none of the previous games had gone to. The humour is still there, as are the quips and the fun puzzles. But it's darker, particularly the final episode, and while it did its job in shocking me when I first played the game, it's a bit jarring now that I know it's coming (and I'm in a position to compare it with Curse of Monkey Island).
Tales of Monkey Island is significantly better that the Remastered versions of the first two games (which I returned because of how uncanny valley I found the graphics), but not as good as Curse of Monkey Island. I'd rate it at about the same level as Escape from Monkey Island, which I rather enjoyed, but found a bit frustrating because of the inventory controls.
There's a pretty blatant sequel hook at the end, I wonder if anything will ever come of it. I have yet to see TellTale bring out a second season of any property.

Tactics fans of the older Rainbow Six and SWAT games will definitely want to play this game. Realistic damage with an overhead view makes for an addicting experience. This game is deceptively simplistic, but it has a pretty robust planning system. You can plan an entire map before a bullet is even fired, but there is an on the fly planning feature, which is sometimes necessary to use to adapt your original plan. You can choose which directions to face while moving, waiting until areas are cleared, things like that.
I love the XP system for a squad; you gradually earn skill points to spend in different ability trees as your squad levels up. There are also weapons and equipment you can purchase using stars earned from completed missions. And there is A LOT of content here; dozens of single missions, several campaigns consisting of linked missions where operative injury or death will carry over, and don't forget about the Steam Workshop support full of custom missions. I downloaded the Rainbow Six mod that substituted all the old music, chatter, and sound effects from the older games.
Rainbow Six fans who loved to plan will find an itch scratched, but there are definitely areas left to be desired. The main complaint I have with the game is the planning is sometimes buggy or not deep enough. There are no teams, so you'll have to plan waypoints for each operative; that can get tedious if you're on a mission with 8 deployed. Often, if I'm trying to plan on the fly, I'll pause and put a go-code down for my man. Sometimes, if I try to plan a waypoint past it, it'll delete the go code and my man will just waltz into a room and ignore the original order. Other times, even when the go code is on a door, my operative will still ignore it and go charging in. The lack of depth is also frustrating: the game bases flashbanging rooms off of doors, but the AI is not smart enough to adapt to flashbang a room if a door is now open, when on the original plan it was closed. This forces you to have to order the flashbang again, but from outside the room. You'll have to redo any waypoints after that as well. Also, there are a couple multi-level maps where you can't even plan out the entire thing, making time trials far more difficult.
I love the game when stuff goes right, but I find things slightly infuriating when the things that are going wrong are because the planning system is flawed in some key areas. Still, I can't help but come back to the game, because I still enjoy it immensely. When things go bad because of a boneheaded AI decision, I can only just shake my head and restart, trying to figure out a way around the game's jenk.
But god damn, when I pull off a great takedown, you bet your♥♥♥♥♥I'm saving that replay. 7/10.

This is a tech demo showing of water physics, and that's about it. The models are pretty, the water physics look nice, but it's terrible beyond that. I can imagine the situation, "Good work, fellow 3d artists, we've made a nice looking game, and the water physics have raised the industry bar! Wait, where's the guy with the game mechanics? We don't have game mechanics! Ah well, slap on some third-person cover shooting, some shoddy climbing mechanics, and a hacked together story led by a whiney protagonist."
Combat is a bit of a mess. You get a sonic gun that non-lethally takes down enemies, but they immediately drown in water, so there's no point in a no-kill run. But if you can get past that, the thing can push explosive barrels in enemy faces that are hopelessly floating in water, that's fun.  Climbing is boring and irritating. One moment I'm a one woman army fighting against misguided terrorists, the next I'm suffering with a terrible camera slowly jumping up some pipes and trying to judge where I'll land from jumping to the next wall. To be honest, the climbing killed the game for me. The campaign is short enough for you to complete in a couple of hours, but I doubt you'll complete it due to a jump at the end in which if you mess up, you have to start about 5 minutes back to where you started, and you'll be messing that jump up a lot. I don't even know what's past that jump, I raged and left after about seven attempts.
Though I'll give the game credit where it's due, but it's not enough to redeem it. The combat is a mess, but playing with the physics to kill your enemies is fun, a la Half Life environment kills. Story wise, it started off alight by having memorabilia explain the protagonist's background, but then collapsed when she started talking. Jesus, can that woman whine. Then you got the "We're killing everyone and everything, including us," terrorists. My eyes rolled out of my head when I saw the doomsday machine.
Recommendation: Buy it to play with the physics and look at the pretty water, that's it.

This game isn’t perfect. But it’s the best rally game ever made.
The handling isn’t consistently intuitive across the game, but I have every faith in the developers who are true rally fans to continue iterating. For the time being, the driving is rewarding and fun, if a little frustrating at times, with snap oversteer and very neutral default setups. The simulation mode is complex in its geometry and physics, evidenced through in depth and effective tuning options. The rally cross cars, however, feel incredible, even though there are a lack of tracks.
Your Stage is good. There are repeated corners, but the stages are far more unpredictable than other Rally games where the challenge is to learn the stages. Trusting the co driver gives a far more real representation of what the sport is about. The timing of particular notes does need changing though; I shouldn’t feel like backing off on a straight in fear that the hairpin at the end will be called too late. There needs to be more locations, and some more stage variation, but I am yet to be bored of the 5 initial ones, after 70 hours of gameplay.
Team management features are poor and confusing. Hiring staff is too expensive for the effect it has, perks make little difference, and not being able to load a tuning setup because your chief engineer is in a bad mood is just plain bad game design. Sponsors are confusing and give inconsistent rewards. It is frustrating to see no better sponsor deals after investing heavily in PR staff. Rebalancing is required.
Overall, this game is excellent. It has a complex enough handling model to satisfy hardcore racers for some time. It is more fleshed out than Dirt Rally, and has more longevity with Your Stage. My positive review is in trust of Codemasters who are true fans of the best sport in the world to continue development to solve the odd feeling some vehicles have, as other reviewers have highlighted.
Nonetheless, Dirt 4 is a loving rendition of our sport, and it will only get better.

I was skeptical about this purchase at first. After the really, really well-made DiRT Rally, this new game could only be better or at least just as good. However, I didn't immediately like the Simulation handling and anti-aliasing seemed to have some issues as well. After 43 hours of game time, I can now say with confidence that this is a fantastic rally racing game!
Yes, the handling took a bit of getting used to - but that's always the case when a new racing game is released. After learning its intricacies, I'm enjoying the stages and races a lot. If there's something that bothers you about the handling, you can simply change and adjust it. There is an incredible amount of adjustments you can make to the handling models and difficulty levels. Additionally, you can fine-tune all the cars, obviously.
DiRT 4 looks beautiful. The different weather effects, skies, and lighting effects can make stages look pretty and/or very thrilling. If AA is an issue for you, try using Nvidia Multi-Frame Sampled Anti-aliasing. Even the lowest level of MFAA will take care of any jaggies. Know your options.
Like with DiRT Rally, the best thing about this game is the sound effects. Engines, the breaking of parts, and stage sound effects sound phenomenal. Codemasters are still the kings of car sounds. No other racing game currently released sounds as good as DiRT 4 does.
I'm a huge fan of the daily/weekly/monthly competitive events, and being able to have many of these randomly generated using the My Stage feature is genius. No more constantly racing against other people on the same tracks over and over again. Of course, there are set pieces, but it makes a big enough difference for these events.
The only things I would like to see changed and improved are the timings of some of the pacenotes for some of the main stages. Having Uphill and Downhill notes back would be great. Of course, a few more racing locations wouldn't hurt either.

I love this game. I got this less than a week ago and I already have 90 hours into it, however, I think there are a few misconseptions about it though that I would like to correct. The biggest one that I noticed being that this game is for the *hardcore* military enthusiasts; those who know a lot about aircraft specs, military tactics, and most importantly, the lingo. A few of the positive reviews say that it's not for people who enjoy dabbling in Arma 3, which I disagree with completely. You do NOT need to know military equipment, nor do you need to know anything about history and warfare. What you do need is a passion for interpreting information, carefully laying out plans, and then watching them unfold, which I think is the best part.
It took me 5 hours to do the first tutorial and fail it, another 5 hours to do it and succeed, and before I could even do any of that, came the 7 hours it took me to understand just what the ♥♥♥♥ I was actually looking at, 3 hours to learn how to do anything, and 4 hours to figure out what the different aircraft do and what things were. Before I started playing I had no clue what Attack aircraft are, "If they're called attack, why aren't they attack other planes?" or why my bombers seemed to suck at their job because the target was still standing after a bombing run, fooled by games like War Thunder that make it seem increadibly easy.
This game is not flashy. It's not Men of War, or World of Warships, or anything like that, and you won't be in the trenches with your men watching them exchange fire; it's a database of information that you can use to play imaginary army men, and it's the most fun I've ever had, with such a passionate, and patient community who don't mind the fact that I'm asking another question about what things do in the steam discussions page.
The joys of this game are simple. You conduct military operations with aircraft and naval vessels, setting up missions and parameters, before you watch the blips on your screen do just that. For those who want realism, you can watch in real time, for those who want to play around for a few minutes, it goes up to 300x time compression. I find myself holding my breath, waiting for missiles or battleship salvos to land, and biting my lip when I take return fire. My heart stops when the tail member of my Wing catches a missile and crashes into the side of a mountain, his sacrifice carving the way for the strike team to drop their payloads on target.
For people who want to set up a battle of World of Warships, just for the hell of it, you can do that too with the scenario editor, and anything that you want to share can easily be published for other people to play on the workshop.
The biggest problem people have with this game is the price of entry, and I do agree that it is steep, so looking around for better deals or waiting for a sale is the best option, but do not let the price disuade you from getting it entirely, there are ways of finding better prices. If you would like to try the game, starting with the standalone DLC, Command: Chains of War may be a better option, for $20 you get the engine and access to its campaign, but everything else being unaccessable without the base game. If you're on the fence because of the price, start with Chains of War.
This game is not for those seeking tense, first person combat, but for those who enjoy thinking about a problem and figuring out a way to overcome it to complete your orders. If you also want to learn about aircraft and history, and enjoy studying, this is for you as well. I can't recommend this game enough, and never put so much time into something in such a high frequency.

Great wargaming simulator for armchair air force generals and admirals
Basically, you can design any mission you want in a sandboxy google earth-like map
You can take command of every ship, aircraft, military installation and land unit you spawn (land units are not very optimized, as this game has a naval-air focus).
The unit list is almost encyclopedic as the naval-air and often land forces of almost every country since the 1950s are available to command. This includes destroyers, jet fighters, ground attack aircraft, nuclear capable bombers such as the B-52, tanks, foot infantry and SAM sites
You can equip all units with additional weapons, sensors and munitions for the missions you want to send them on.
Need to take out a tank formation but only got MiG-23s?
No problem, just have compatible air-ground missiles back at it's airbase and it'll be ready to take out those pesky tanks after it's done re-armimg!
Really recommend this game for strategy gamers that love attention to detail and a keen imagination

This game continues the harmonious combination of pumping 80's music and ultra-violent gameplay that made the original so engaging. There is a much greater emphasis on world-building and story in this one, which from the point of view of the narrative makes for a game within a game all of its own - trying to piece together the non-linear story.
Multiple character perspectives adds variety in one sense as the player is encouraged to experiment with varied play styles. However the unfortunate side-effect of this increased narrative focus is that the player cannot choose their own approach to every level; they are limited by the abilities and movesets of whoever the game dictates you play. This leads to some moments of frustration as not all of the characters are equally effective. If you have played the first game, what I am describing is the gameplay equivalent of not being able to choose which mask you are wearing on each level.
Overall this game is worth your money. I have no regrets about paying full price for it.

Great game.  Everyone compares it to Left 4 Dead 2, and you can't really blame them.  It's a horde game.
What keeps me playing (and will keep me playing for a while) are clean melee mechanics, interesting objectives during missions, pacing, and focus on teamplay.
The risk vs. reward system implemented in the way you get loot is interesting, and while many people question it, I support it.  To get to roll on the loot table, you MUST be victorious in the mission.  I think this forces more people to play the game "properly" for their own benefit.  It encourages teamplay.  Of course, it does open the doors for trolls, but thus far, I've yet to experience one, and I only play pubs.
Also, you can pick up items to boost the number of dice you get to roll on the loot table.  These items take up useful slots, like your engineer slot for Grimiores, or your Health potion slot for Tomes. (both of which reward extra dice).  This adds an extra risk vs reward scenario that each player must consider during the course of the game (usually).
I find myself balancing melee with ranged as all of the characters.  This is interesting because in most games, you tend to focus more on one or the other.
The loot is upgradable, none of it is really overpowered... they found a way to balance things just right, it seems.
Great game.  I definitely recommend picking it up.  It's worth full price, and definitely worth sale prices.  Enjoy!

Let me preface - I like grinding in games. Grinding out quests, monsters, cash, drops, I enjoy it. This game however, takes it to a whole new level.
You have to grind out the same monsters quest after quest after quest, so you can collect materials to craft items that anybody else at your level is going to have. There's no diversity, no RNG, nothing to mix up the grind or even really to reward it.
Leveling is slow and there's a strange mix between the enemies being extremely weak and then all of a sudden, overwhemlingly unbeatable.
Lastly the controls are a little off the wall. They're awkward and annoying to handle, especially your camera angles.
I really wanted to like this game. I wanted to spend countless hours grinding out levels and gear, questing and exploring cool new areas, but in it's current state I just can't do it, nor can I recommend that you should try.
TLDR - Overly grindy and monotonous, unbalanced enemy difficulty, awkward controls.
It is a very new game, perhaps the devs will manage to salvage it and make it into something awesome.

Best thing about the turn based system is that you have time to chat in fights with your team and discuses tactics our just have a good chat.
